залить.etymology: Formed from prefix за- ('over, full') + лить ('to pour'), inherited from Old East Slavic лити, from Proto-Slavic *liti ('to pour', from PIE *leyH-).

залог.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic залогъ ('pledge, security, deposit'), from Proto-Slavic *zalogъ, an o-grade deverbal noun corresponding to *založiti ('to lay down behind, pledge, pawn', from *za- + *ložiti).

заложить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic заложити and Proto-Slavic *založiti ('to lay behind, lay down as a foundation or pledge'), formed from за- + ложить ('to lay, place', Proto-Slavic *ložiti).

history.meaning: to place behind, lay a foundation, pledge
to found (a building); to give as security
to lay (a foundation), build into a budget; to pawn, mortgage; (colloquial) to inform on

замазать.etymology: Formed from prefix за- ('over, cover') + мазать ('to smear, daub, anoint'), inherited from Old East Slavic мазати, from Proto-Slavic *mazati; the slang sense 'to bet' comes from billiards and card players' argot ('to chalk/mark up a stake').

history.meaning: to smear over, putty up; (slang) to bet

заманить.etymology: Formed from the prefix за- ('into') + манить ('to beckon, lure, entice', inherited from Proto-Slavic *maniti).

history.meaning: to lure in, entice into a trap or place

замараться.etymology: Reflexive form of замарать ('to soil, dirty, stain'), formed from prefix за- + марать ('to smear, soil, dirty', from Proto-Slavic *marati) + -ся.

замаринованный.etymology: Past passive participle of замариновать ('to marinate'), formed from prefix за- + мариновать, borrowed via French mariner or German marinieren from Italian marinare ('to pickle in sea-water brine'), from Latin marīnus ('of the sea').

замена.etymology: Deverbal noun formed from заменить ('to replace, substitute'), built from prefix за- ('in place of, for') + мена / менять ('exchange, barter / to change, swap', from Old East Slavic мѣна, Proto-Slavic *měna, cognate with Lithuanian mainas 'exchange' and Latin mūnus / commūnis).

заменить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with the prefix за- ('in place of') and менить ('to change, exchange'), derived from мена ('exchange, barter', from Proto-Slavic *měna, cognate with Lithuanian mainas 'exchange').

заменять.etymology: Imperfective of заменить ('to replace, substitute'), formed from за- ('in place of, for') + менять ('to change, exchange', derived from мена 'exchange', Proto-Slavic *měna / *měniti).

замерзание.etymology: Verbal noun from замерзать ('to freeze'), formed from prefix за- + мерзать (imperfective of мёрзнуть 'to freeze', from Proto-Slavic *mьrznǫti) + suffix -ние.

замерять.etymology: Secondary imperfective formed in Russian with the suffix -ять from замерить ('to measure off, gauge'), itself built from resultative prefix за- + мерить ('to measure'), from Old East Slavic мѣрити and Proto-Slavic *měriti (denominative from *měra 'measure', ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *meh₁- 'to measure').
замерять.notes: Preferred by builders, tailors, and technicians for taking practical physical dimensions or meter readings (замерять окно, замерять напряжение), alongside more general измерять.

замести.etymology: Formed from prefix за- ('over, up') + мести ('to sweep'), inherited from Old East Slavic мести, from Proto-Slavic *mesti ('to sweep, throw'), from PIE *met-.

заместитель.etymology: Agent noun formed with the suffix -тель from заместить ('to take the place of, replace, act for'), built on за- ('in place of') + место ('place', Old East Slavic мѣсто, Proto-Slavic *město). Literally, 'one who stands in the place of a superior, a deputy or vice-head'.

history.meaning: to take the place of → substitute, deputy

заметаться.etymology: Formed with the inchoative prefix за- ('begin to') + метаться ('to toss about, dart frantically back and forth'), the reflexive of метать ('to fling, cast', inherited from Proto-Slavic *metati).

history.meaning: to rush/toss about -> to start darting or tossing about

rootFamily.gloss: to rush about, toss and turn

заметить.etymology: Formed from the prefix за- + метить ('to mark, aim at, note'), derived from мета ('mark, sign, target', from Proto-Slavic *měta).

заметка.etymology: Formed with the noun suffix -ка from заметить ('to mark, notice, take note of'), built on prefix за- + мета ('mark, target, sign', from Old East Slavic мѣта, Proto-Slavic *měta). Originally 'a physical notch or mark made to remember something', then 'a brief written note or jotting'.

заметно.etymology: Adverb and impersonal predicate continuing the short neuter singular of заметный ('noticeable, perceptible'), derived from заметить ('to notice, mark').

заметный.etymology: Derived from заметить / замета ('mark, sign; to notice'), from prefix за- + метить ('to mark, aim', from мета 'mark, target', Proto-Slavic *měta) + adjective suffix -ный.

замечание.etymology: Verbal noun from замечать ('to notice, observe, make a remark'), imperfective of заметить (from за- + метить 'to mark', Proto-Slavic *mětiti) + suffix -ние.

замечательно.etymology: Adverb and predicative short neuter of замечательный ('remarkable, wonderful'), formed with the suffix -тельный from замечать ('to notice, remark, observe').

замечательный.etymology: Derived from замечать ('to notice, observe, remark upon', from за- + метить, Proto-Slavic *mětiti) + the adjective suffix -тельный, originally meaning 'worthy of notice, remarkable' (a semantic calque of French remarquable).

замечать.etymology: Imperfective of заметить ('to notice, observe, remark'), formed from за- + мечать / метить ('to mark, aim at', derived from мета 'mark, sign, target', Proto-Slavic *měta): originally 'to put a mental mark on something'.

history.meaning: to mark down -> to notice, observe

заминка.etymology: Formed with the noun suffix -ка from замяться ('to hesitate, falter, pause awkwardly'), the reflexive of замять ('to crumple, tread down, hush up'). The root мять / мин- descends from Proto-Slavic *męti ('to press, knead, trample'), from PIE *men- ('to tread, press'). Literally 'a momentary stumbling or shuffling in place', it commonly appears in без заминки ('without a hitch').

history.meaning: to falter, hesitate → slight hitch or pause

замок.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic замъкъ ('door lock, bolt'), a deverbal instrument noun formed with suffix -ок from замкнуть (Old East Slavic замъкнути 'to lock, fasten shut', from prefix за- + *mъknǫti 'to push, slip a bolt shut'). (Stressed on the first syllable, замок 'castle' is an early calque via Polish zamek of Middle High German slōz, which meant both 'lock' and 'fortress that locks a pass'.)

morphemes.meaning: bolt, fasten (мкнуть) with mobile vowel о

замок.notes: Stress distinguishes two words from the same historical source: **замок** ('lock', genitive **замка**) vs. **замок** ('castle', genitive **замка**).

замолчать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with the inceptive prefix за- ('entering a state') and молчать ('to be silent'), inherited from Old East Slavic мълчати (and Old Church Slavonic млъчати), from Proto-Slavic *mьlčati ('to be silent').

history.meaning: to fall silent, stop talking, shut up

замораживать.etymology: Imperfective of заморозить ('to freeze'), formed from за- + морозить ('to freeze', derived from мороз 'frost, freezing cold', Proto-Slavic *morzъ with East Slavic pleophony -оро-) + the imperfectivizing suffix -ивать.

history.meaning: to freeze (food, water, or financial assets)

morphemes.meaning: frost, freeze (with о -> а and з -> ж)

заморачиваться.etymology: Colloquial reflexive imperfective of заморочить ('to confuse, baffle, muddle one's head'), formed from prefix за- + морочить ('to cloud, bewilder', from East Slavic морок 'darkness, gloom, mental fog', Proto-Slavic *morkъ) + -ся.

history.meaning: to bother, obsess over, trouble oneself

замороженный.etymology: Past passive participle of заморозить ('to freeze'), formed from prefix за- + морозить ('to freeze', from мороз 'frost', East Slavic pleophonic form of Proto-Slavic *morzъ).

замороченный.etymology: Colloquial past passive participle of заморочить ('to bewilder, muddle, overcomplicate'), from prefix за- + морочить ('to cloud, confuse', from морок 'gloom, fog', Proto-Slavic *morkъ).

заморочить.etymology: Formed from completive за- + морочить ('to cloud the mind, befuddle, fool'), derived from East Slavic морок ('darkness, fog, mental haze, illusion', from Proto-Slavic *morkъ with East Slavic pleophony -оро-; compare Church Slavonic мрак 'darkness').

history.meaning: mental fog -> to befuddle -> to muddle, confuse, pester

заморочить.notes: Often used in the idiom заморочить голову кому-либо ('to muddle someone's head / confuse or distract someone').

замотаться.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed with the circumfix за-...-ся ('to exhaust oneself by doing') + мотать ('to wind, reel, shake, rush about', from Proto-Slavic *motati).

history.meaning: to get worn out rushing around

замочный.etymology: Relational adjective formed with the suffix -ный (with к > ч palatalization) from замок ('lock, padlock'), inherited from Old East Slavic замъкъ (deverbal from замкнути 'to lock, close up', Proto-Slavic *zamъknǫti).

замуж.etymology: Univerbated adverbial phrase inherited from Old East Slavic за мужь ('behind/for a husband', accusative of motion after the preposition за), preserving the archaic inanimate-like accusative singular form мужь of муж ('husband', Proto-Slavic *mǫžь). In traditional Slavic patriarchal law and custom, a woman married 'behind a husband' (into his household and protection: выйти замуж 'to get married' and быть замужем 'to be married').

history.meaning: to go in marriage behind/to a husband
in marriage (said of a woman getting married)

замужем.etymology: Univerbation of the Old East Slavic prepositional phrase за мужьмь ('behind a husband', i.e. under a husband's protection and household), from за ('behind') + instrumental singular of муж ('husband, man', from Proto-Slavic *mǫžь).

history.meaning: behind a husband, married (of a woman)

замученный.etymology: Past passive participle of замучить ('to torment to exhaustion, wear out'), formed from prefix за- + мучить ('to torment, torture', from мука 'torment', Old East Slavic мучити, Proto-Slavic *mǫčiti).

замыкание.etymology: Verbal noun from замыкать ('to lock, close a loop or circuit'), from prefix за- + мыкать (imperfective of -мкнуть 'to close, lock', Proto-Slavic *mъknǫti); короткое замыкание ('short circuit') calques German Kurzschluss / French court-circuit.

замышлять.etymology: Imperfective of замыслить ('to conceive a plan, plot'), formed from за- + мышлять / мыслить ('to think, devise', derived from мысль 'thought', Proto-Slavic *myslь).

замёрзнуть.etymology: Perfective verb formed with the prefix за- and мёрзнуть ('to freeze, feel cold'), inherited from Old East Slavic мьрзнути, from Proto-Slavic *mьrznǫti ('to freeze'), related by ablaut to мороз ('frost', from *morzъ with East Slavic pleophony -оро-).

morphemes.meaning: inchoative verb suffix and infinitive ending

занавеска.etymology: Derived with the suffix -ка from занавес ('curtain, hanging') / занавесить ('to hang a curtain over'), formed from за- + на- + весить ('to hang', from Proto-Slavic *věsiti).

заначка.etymology: Colloquial deverbal noun from заначить ('to hide away, stash for later', from East Slavic dialectal/argot заначити 'to mark off or tuck away in secret') + suffix -ка.

занести.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic занести, formed from the prefix за- ('in on the way, behind, upward') + нести ('to carry', from Proto-Slavic *nesti).

history.meaning: to carry in, bring in; to record

занимать.etymology: Imperfective of занять ('to occupy, borrow'), inherited from Old East Slavic занимати, formed from the prefix за- + -нимать (iterative of ять 'to take', from Proto-Slavic *zanimati < *za- + *jьmati).

history.meaning: to take up, occupy; to borrow

заниматься.etymology: Reflexive form of занимать ('to occupy, engage') with the enclitic -ся ('to occupy oneself with, study, practice').

заново.etymology: Adverb formed by univerbation of the prepositional phrase за ново ('for new, anew'), combining the preposition за with the short neuter accusative singular of новый ('new', from Proto-Slavic *novъ).

history.meaning: anew, all over again, from scratch

заносить.etymology: Imperfective of занести ('to bring in, carry in, drift over'), formed from the prefix за- + носить ('to carry', iterative of нести, from Proto-Slavic *nositi).

history.meaning: to bring in, carry in; to skid

занятие.etymology: Verbal noun from занять ('to occupy, engage', from Old East Slavic заяти, Proto-Slavic *zajęti, from *za- + *jęti 'to take') + -тие; the sense 'occupation, pastime, class' developed under the semantic influence of French occupation.

занятый.etymology: Adjectival passive participle of занять ('to occupy, take up, borrow'), formed from the prefix за- and the Proto-Slavic root *jęti ('to take', Old East Slavic яти). In predicate position, the short form занят / занята / заняты ('busy, occupied') is standard.

занять.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic заняти (future займу, past занял), from Proto-Slavic *zajęti ('to take up, occupy, borrow'), formed from prefix *za- + *jęti ('to take, grasp', from PIE *h₁em- 'to take', cognate with Latin emō 'to take, buy' and Lithuanian im̃ti 'to take').

history.meaning: to occupy (a seat, room, time); to borrow

заняться.etymology: Reflexive form of занять ('to occupy, take up', from Old East Slavic заняти, Proto-Slavic *zajęti, built on *za- + *jęti 'to take'): literally 'to occupy oneself with (+ instrumental)', hence 'to take up, attend to, get busy with'.

history.meaning: to occupy oneself with, attend to (perfective)

заодно.etymology: Adverb formed by univerbation of the prepositional phrase за одно ('as one single thing, together'), from the preposition за ('for, as') and одно ('one', neuter of один, Proto-Slavic *jedьno).

history.meaning: in league together; at the same time, while one is at it

заодно.notes: Has two everyday meanings: 'in cahoots / acting as one' (они с ним заодно) and 'at the same time / while I'm at it' (заодно купи хлеба).

запад.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic / Old Church Slavonic западъ ('setting of the sun, west'), deverbal noun from западать / запасть ('to fall behind, set [of the sun]', from *za- + *pasti, Proto-Slavic *zapadъ, calquing Ancient Greek δύσις).

запаниковать.etymology: Formed from the inchoative prefix за- ('begin to') + паниковать ('to panic'), from паника ('panic'), borrowed via French panique from Ancient Greek πανικός ('pertaining to Pan, sudden terror attributed to the god Pan').

запара.etymology: Colloquial deverbal noun from запарить / запариться ('to steam until exhausted; in slang, to be swamped with frantic work'), formed from за- + парить ('to steam', from пар 'steam', Proto-Slavic *parъ).

запасной.etymology: Formed with the adjectival suffix -ной from запас ('store, supply, reserve'), a deverbal noun from запасти ('to lay in stores, save up for later', built on за- + пасти 'to keep safe, guard, herd', the same root as спасти 'to save').

history.meaning: to lay in store → reserve supply → spare, backup

запасть.etymology: Formed from prefix за- ('behind, deep into') + пасть ('to fall'), inherited from Old East Slavic пасти, from Proto-Slavic *pasti; the colloquial sense 'to fall for someone' comes from запасть в душу ('to sink deep into one's soul/memory').

history.meaning: to fall behind; (colloquial) to fall for

запах.etymology: Deverbal noun from запахнуть ('to begin to smell, emit a scent'), formed from the prefix за- + пахнуть ('to smell, blow softly', from Proto-Slavic *paxati / *paxnǫti 'to puff, blow, emit an odor').

запекать.etymology: Imperfective of запечь ('to bake until browned orencrusted'), formed from prefix за- + пекать (iterative of печь 'to bake, roast', inherited from Old East Slavic печи, Proto-Slavic *peťi / *pekti, PIE *pekʷ-).

запереть.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic заперети (future запру, past запер; showing East Slavic pleophony -ере-), from Proto-Slavic *zaperti ('to brace shut, bar, lock'), formed from prefix *za- ('shut') + *perti ('to press, prop, brace with a wooden bar', from PIE *per- / *sper- 'to prop, spar').

history.meaning: to brace shut with a bar, lock

запертый.etymology: Past passive participle of запереть ('to lock, shut, bar'), inherited from Old East Slavic заперети, formed from за- ('behind, shut') + переть ('to press, push, prop', from Proto-Slavic *perti).

запеть.etymology: Formed from the inchoative prefix за- ('begin to') + петь ('to sing', inherited from Old East Slavic пѣти, Proto-Slavic *pěti).

history.meaning: to begin to sing, break into song; (slang) to start talking under questioning

запечатать.etymology: Perfective verb formed from prefix за- ('closed, shut') + печатать ('to stamp, seal'), derived from печать ('seal, signet, stamp'). Old East Slavic печать and Proto-Slavic *pečatь originally denoted a heated branding or wax-stamping tool, derived from *pekti ('to bake, burn', PIE *pekw- 'to cook, ripen'). It is thus distantly cognate with Russian печь ('oven, to bake') and English cook.

history.meaning: seal, signet → to close with a seal

запечённый.etymology: Past passive participle of запечь ('to bake or roast in the oven until browned or encrusted'), formed from за- + печь ('to bake, roast', from Proto-Slavic *peťi).

history.meaning: to bake in the oven -> oven-baked, roasted, gratiné

запилить.etymology: Formed from prefix за- + пилить ('to saw; figuratively to nag relentlessly', from пила 'saw', Proto-Slavic *pila); the modern slang sense 'to make, create, post' spread in the late 2000s from the viral phrase «Дверь мне запили!».

history.meaning: to saw into, nag to death; (slang) to make, post

записанный.etymology: Past passive participle of записать ('to write down, record'), formed from prefix за- + писать ('to write', inherited from Old East Slavic писати, Proto-Slavic *pisati).

записать.etymology: Formed by prefixing за- ('down, into a record') to писать ('to write', from Old East Slavic писати, Proto-Slavic *pьsati).

записаться.etymology: Reflexive form of записать ('to write down, register, enroll', from за- + писать 'to write', Proto-Slavic *pisati) + -ся ('to write one's own name down, sign up').

history.meaning: to sign up, register, book an appointment

записка.etymology: Formed in Russian with the noun suffix -ка from записать ('to write down, note', built on за- + писать 'to write'): a short handwritten note or message left for someone.

записывать.etymology: Imperfective of записать ('to write down, record, register'), formed with the iterative suffix -ывать from за- + писать ('to write', from Proto-Slavic *pisati).

записываться.etymology: Reflexive and middle/passive verb formed from записывать ('to write down, record, register', imperfective of записать, from за- + писать 'to write', Proto-Slavic *pisati) + -ся.

history.meaning: to write down -> to sign up, book an appointment, be recorded

rootFamily.gloss: to sign up, make an appointment (perfective)

запись.etymology: Deverbal noun formed from записать ('to write down, record, register'), from за- + пись (from the root of писать 'to write', Proto-Slavic *pisati).

запить.etymology: Formed from за- + пить ('to drink', inherited from Proto-Slavic *piti); with inchoative за- (used intransitively) it means 'to start drinking heavily, go on a binge', while with sequential за- (used transitively) it means 'to wash down food or a pill with a drink'.

history.meaning: to go on a drinking binge; to wash down (with water)

запихать.etymology: Colloquial perfective verb formed from prefix за- ('into') + пихать ('to shove, push, stuff'), inherited from Old East Slavic пихати, from Proto-Slavic *pixati (iterative of *pьxati 'to pound, thrust').

заплакать.etymology: Inchoative perfective verb formed from prefix за- ('begin to') + плакать ('to weep, cry'), inherited from Old East Slavic плакати, from Proto-Slavic *plakati ('to beat one's breast, lament, weep').

history.meaning: to start crying, burst into tears

запланировать.etymology: Formed from perfective prefix за- + планировать ('to plan'), from план ('plan'), borrowed via German Plan and French plan from Latin plānus ('flat, level; ground plan').

заплатить.etymology: Formed from the perfective prefix за- + платить ('to pay', inherited from Old East Slavic платити, from Proto-Slavic *platiti, originally 'to hand over a piece of linen cloth [*platъ] as currency').

заподозрить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with the inchoative prefix за- ('begin to') from подозрить / подозревать ('to suspect'), which was built on Church Slavonic подъзьрѣти ('to look askance or from underneath at', from под- 'under' + зреть 'to look').

заполнить.etymology: Formed from prefix за- ('completely, full') + полнить ('to fill'), denominative verb from полный ('full'), inherited from Old East Slavic пълнъ, from Proto-Slavic *pьlnъ (PIE *pl̥h₁nós).

запоминать.etymology: Imperfective of запомнить ('to commit to memory, remember'), formed from prefix за- + поминать ('to remember, mention', from Proto-Slavic *pominati, related to *pьmněti 'to remember, think', PIE *men-).

запоминаться.etymology: Reflexive form of запоминать ('to memorize, remember'), formed from prefix за- + поминать (Proto-Slavic *pominati 'to remember') + -ся.

history.meaning: to be remembered, stick in the mind

запомнить.etymology: Formed from the perfective prefix за- ('fixing in memory') + помнить ('to remember', inherited from Old East Slavic помьнити, from Proto-Slavic *pomьniti).

запотеть.etymology: Formed from the inchoative/covering prefix за- + потеть ('to sweat, perspire, mist over'), derived from пот ('sweat, moisture', from Proto-Slavic *potъ, from PIE *pekʷ- 'to cook, heat').

history.meaning: to mist over, steam up, break into a sweat

заправить.etymology: Formed from prefix за- ('in, into order') + править ('to set straight, direct, arrange', from Old East Slavic правити, derived from правый 'straight, right, proper'). Means 'to tuck in, put into neat order' (заправить кровать 'to make the bed'), as well as 'to dress (a salad) or fuel (a vehicle)'.

history.meaning: to set straight, put in order
to tuck in, make (a bed); to season, refuel

заправиться.etymology: Reflexive form of заправить ('to set right, tuck in, dress [food], fill [with fuel]'), formed from prefix за- + править ('to direct, set right', from правый 'right, straight', Proto-Slavic *praviti) + -ся.

запрашивать.etymology: Imperfective of запросить ('to request formally, inquire; to ask a price'), formed from за- + прашивать (the iterative stem of просить 'to ask, request', from Proto-Slavic *prositi).

morphemes.meaning: ask, request (with о -> а and с -> ш)

запредельный.etymology: Prepositional-prefixal adjective formed from за пределом ('beyond the limit/boundary'), from за- ('beyond') + предел ('boundary, limit', borrowed from Old Church Slavonic прѣдѣлъ, from *per- + *dělъ 'division') + -ный.

запрет.etymology: Deverbal noun from запретить ('to forbid, prohibit'), borrowed from Old Church Slavonic запрѣтити ('to threaten, enjoin, forbid', compare native East Slavic запереть), from Proto-Slavic *za-pertiti ('to warn sternly, forbid').

запретить.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic запрѣтити ('to threaten, enjoin sternly, forbid'), formed from за- and прѣтити ('to threaten, restrain, warn', from Proto-Slavic *pertiti). The stem shows the Church Slavonic treatment прѣ- (whereas native East Slavic had перетить 'to obstruct, oppose').

запрещать.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic запрѣщати ('to forbid, admonish, threaten'; with Church Slavonic -щ- from *tj), imperfective of запрѣтити, from prefix за- + прѣтити ('to threaten, restrain', Proto-Slavic *pertiti).

запрещённый.etymology: Past passive participle of запретить ('to forbid, prohibit', with regular Church Slavonic reflex *tj -> щ), borrowed from Old Church Slavonic запрѣтити ('to rebuke, command strictly, forbid', from Proto-Slavic *zaprětiti).

запрос.etymology: Deverbal noun from запросить / запрашивать ('to request formally, ask a price'), formed from за- + просить ('to ask, request', Proto-Slavic *prositi).

history.meaning: to inquire, ask -> official inquiry, search query; (plural) expectations

запускать.etymology: Imperfective of запустить ('to let go into, launch, start up; to neglect'), formed from prefix за- + пускать ('to let go, release', iterative of пустить, from Proto-Slavic *pustiti).

запустить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic запустити, formed from the prefix за- + пустить ('to let go, release, send forth', from Proto-Slavic *pustiti), developing both 'to launch, set in motion' and 'to let run wild, neglect'.

запутать.etymology: Perfective verb formed from prefix за- ('into a state') + путать ('to tangle, hobble, confuse'). The base verb derives from Proto-Slavic *pǫtati ('to bind with fetters, entangle'), built on the noun *pǫto ('fetter, cord, bond', Russian путы), from PIE *pent- ('to tread, path, bridge'). Its passive participle запутанный means 'tangled, knotted, complicated'.

запутаться.etymology: Reflexive derivative of запутать ('to tangle up, confuse'), formed from за- + путать ('to tangle, hobble', derived from путо / путы 'hobbles, fetters for a horse's legs', Proto-Slavic *pǫto) + -ся.

history.meaning: to tangle -> to get tangled up, become confused

зарабатывать.etymology: Imperfective of заработать ('to earn by working'), formed from prefix за- + рабатывать (iterative of работать 'to work', from работа 'work, labor', Proto-Slavic *orbota).

заработать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with the prefix за- and работать ('to work', from работа 'work', Proto-Slavic *orbota). Combines two productive meanings of the prefix за-: (1) 'to acquire or earn through working' (заработать деньги) and (2) 'to begin working or functioning' (мотор заработал).

history.meaning: to earn by working; to start working

заработаться.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed with the circumfix за-...-ся ('to get overly absorbed or worn out in doing') + работать ('to work', from работа, Proto-Slavic *orbota).

history.meaning: to get carried away with work, overwork

заработный.etymology: Relational adjective derived from заработать / заработок ('earnings, wages gained by work', from за- + работать 'to work', Proto-Slavic *orbota) + suffix -ный, chiefly in заработная плата ('salary, wages').

заражение.etymology: Verbal noun in -ение from заразить ('to infect, contaminate'), built on за- + разить ('to strike, smite', Proto-Slavic *raziti; compare зараза 'contagion, pestilence', originally 'a striking down').

зараза.etymology: Deverbal noun from заразить ('to infect, originally to strike down, smite'), formed from prefix за- + разить ('to strike, smite', from Proto-Slavic *raziti, causative-iterative related to *rězati 'to cut, strike').

заразиться.etymology: Reflexive form of заразить ('to infect, originally to strike down'), formed from prefix за- + разить ('to strike', Proto-Slavic *raziti) + -ся.

history.meaning: to get infected, catch a disease

заранее.etymology: Univerbation of the prepositional phrase за ранее ('in the earlier [time]'), from за ('for, at') + ранее ('earlier', comparative of рано 'early', from Proto-Slavic *rano).

зарегистрировать.etymology: Formed from perfective prefix за- + регистрировать ('to register'), borrowed via German registrieren from Medieval Latin registrāre, from registrum ('list, register', from Late Latin regesta 'things recorded').

зарезать.etymology: Formed from prefix за- ('to death, completely') + резать ('to cut, slice, slaughter'), inherited from Old East Slavic рѣзати, from Proto-Slavic *rězati ('to cut, carve').

зарезервировать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with the prefix за- from резервировать ('to reserve, keep in reserve'), borrowed via German reservieren and French réserver from Latin reservāre ('to keep back, save up').

history.meaning: to reserve, book (a table or room)

зарекомендовать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with the prefix за- from рекомендовать ('to recommend'), borrowed via German rekommandieren / Polish rekomendować from Medieval Latin recommendāre; in modern Russian used almost always with себя (зарекомендовать себя 'to prove oneself, establish a reputation').

history.meaning: to recommend -> to prove oneself, establish one's reputation

заровнять.etymology: Formed from the prefix за- ('covering over, filling in') + ровнять ('to make level or even', derived from ровный 'even, flat', Proto-Slavic *orvьnъ).

history.meaning: to make even -> to level out, smooth over (earth or a pit)

зародить.etymology: Formed from the inchoative prefix за- ('initiate, conceive') + родить ('to give birth, beget', inherited from Proto-Slavic *roditi).

history.meaning: to engender, plant (an idea, hope, or doubt)

зарождаться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective of зародиться ('to be conceived, germinate, originate'), formed with the Church Slavonic alternation д > жд (зарождати сѧ) from prefix за- + родить ('to give birth, bear', Proto-Slavic *roditi) + -ся.

зарплата.etymology: 20th-century syllabic abbreviation (stump compound) of заработная плата ('earned pay, wages'), compounded from заработный ('earned by work', from заработать 'to earn') + плата ('pay, payment', from платить 'to pay').

зарыть.etymology: Formed from prefix за- ('into, cover over') + рыть ('to dig'), inherited from Old East Slavic рыти, from Proto-Slavic *ryti ('to dig, tear up').

зарядить.etymology: Formed from prefix за- ('put into working order') + рядить ('to arrange, prepare, equip'), inherited from Old East Slavic рядити, from Proto-Slavic *ręditi (denominative from *rędъ 'row, order').

зарядка.etymology: Derived with the nominal suffix -ка from зарядить ('to load [a gun], charge [a battery or person with energy]'), from за- + рядить ('to arrange, prepare, put in order', from ряд, Proto-Slavic *rędъ).

засада.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic засада ('ambush, garrison stationed in cover'), from Proto-Slavic *zasada, deverbal from *zasaditi / *zasěsti ('to sit down behind cover', from *za- + *saditi / *sěsti).

засвидетельствовать.etymology: Formed from perfective prefix за- + свидетельствовать ('to bear witness, attest'), derived from свидетель ('witness'), borrowed from Old Church Slavonic съвѣдѣтель (originally from съвѣдати 'to know', reshaped by folk etymology after видѣти 'to see').

заседание.etymology: Verbal noun formed with -ание from заседать ('to sit in session, hold a meeting'), from за- + седать ('to sit', iterative of сесть, from Proto-Slavic *sědati).

засекать.etymology: Imperfective of засечь, formed from за- + секать / сечь ('to cut, chop, notch', Proto-Slavic *sěťi): originally 'to cut a blaze or notch on a tree or tally stick to mark a boundary or point', whence засекать время ('to mark the exact moment on a watch, time something') and 'to spot/locate a target'.

history.meaning: to notch a mark -> to time with a watch; to spot, detect

заселить.etymology: Perfective verb formed from prefix за- ('into') + селить ('to settle, lodge, house'), derived from село ('village, settlement') and Old East Slavic селитися ('to take up residence'). The root descends from Proto-Slavic *selo ('dwelling, settlement, cultivated field'), from PIE *sel- ('human settlement, dwelling, hall'). In hotel and inn usage, заселить гостя / номер means 'to check a guest into a room'.

history.meaning: to settle, check into a room

rootFamily.gloss: to check in, take up residence

заселиться.etymology: Reflexive of заселить ('to settle, populate, move into'), formed from prefix за- ('into') + селить ('to settle', derived from село 'settlement, village', Old East Slavic село, from Proto-Slavic *selo 'inhabited land, farmstead, dwelling'). In hotels and housing, заселиться means 'to check in, move into a room or flat'.

history.meaning: to move in, check into a hotel room

засиять.etymology: Formed with the inchoative prefix за- ('to begin to...') + сиять ('to shine, radiate light, beam'), inherited from Old East Slavic сияти and Proto-Slavic *sijati ('to shine, glow', related to тень/сень and Gothic skeinan / English shine).

history.meaning: to start shining, light up, beam

заскочить.etymology: Formed with the prefix за- ('in on the way') + скочить ('to jump, leap, bound', from Proto-Slavic *skočiti), literally 'to hop in briefly, drop by'.

history.meaning: to jump behind/in; to drop by, pop in

заслуга.etymology: Deverbal noun from заслужить ('to earn by service, deserve'), formed from prefix за- + служить ('to serve', from слуга 'servant', Old East Slavic слуга, Proto-Slavic *sluga).

заслуживать.etymology: Imperfective of заслужить ('to earn, deserve'), formed with the suffix -ивать from за- + служить ('to serve', from Proto-Slavic *služiti).

заслужить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic заслужити ('to earn by service, merit'), formed from the prefix за- + служить ('to serve', from слуга 'servant', Proto-Slavic *sluga / *služiti).

заснуть.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic засънути ('to fall asleep'), formed from the inchoative prefix за- + снуть (< *съпнути, semelfactive/inchoative of спать 'to sleep', from Proto-Slavic *sъpnǫti).

засориться.etymology: Reflexive form of засорить ('to litter, clog with debris'), formed from prefix за- + сорить ('to litter', denominative from сор 'sweepings, dirt, rubbish') + -ся.

history.meaning: to get clogged, become choked with debris

заставать.etymology: Imperfective of застать ('to find in place, catch someone somewhere'), formed from prefix за- + ставать (imperfective of стать 'to stand, come to be', from Proto-Slavic *stati, PIE *steh₂-).

history.meaning: to find, catch (someone at a place)

заставить.etymology: Formed with prefix за- from ставить ('to set, place, make stand'), inherited from Old East Slavic заставити ('to block, set in place, compel'), from Proto-Slavic *staviti.

history.meaning: to set, place, cause to stand
to force, to make (someone do something); to block

заставлять.etymology: Imperfective of заставить ('to block, set in front; to compel, force'), formed from за- + ставлять / ставить ('to place, stand', from Proto-Slavic *staviti).

застать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic застати and Proto-Slavic *zastati ('to come upon, find someone in a place'), formed from за- + стать ('to stand, step', Proto-Slavic *stati).

history.meaning: to step behind/upon, find in place
to find, catch (someone at home or in the act)
to catch, find (someone somewhere); to surprise (застать врасплох)

застегнуть.etymology: Perfective/semelfactive verb in -нуть formed from за- + стегать ('to stitch, quilt, fasten with a clasp or button', from Proto-Slavic *stęgati).

history.meaning: to button up, buckle, zip up, fasten

застраховать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with за- from страховать ('to insure against loss'), coined in nineteenth-century Russian from страх ('fear, peril, risk', Proto-Slavic *straxъ; compare the commercial expression на свой страх и риск 'at one's own peril and risk').

history.meaning: peril, risk -> to insure against risk -> to insure

застрелить.etymology: Formed from prefix за- ('to death') + стрелить ('to shoot'), inherited from Old East Slavic стрѣлити, from Proto-Slavic *strěliti (denominative from *strěla 'arrow, shot').

застрять.etymology: Inherited from East Slavic застряти / застрянути, formed from the prefix за- + *stręti ('to stick fast, bog down, linger', related to Old Church Slavonic стрянути and Russian мешкать / стряпать).

заступаться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective of заступиться ('to step in front of someone to shield them, intercede, defend'), formed from за- ('behind/shielding') + ступать ('to step', Proto-Slavic *stǫpati).

history.meaning: to step in front of to protect, intercede
to stand up for, to defend

заступиться.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed from prefix за- ('in front of to shield') + ступить ('to step, tread', inherited from Old East Slavic ступити, Proto-Slavic *stǫpiti) + -ся, literally 'to step in on someone's behalf'.

history.meaning: to stand up for, intercede, defend

застыть.etymology: Formed from prefix за- ('into a fixed state') + стыть ('to grow cold, congeal', shortened from стынуть, from Proto-Slavic *stynǫti, related to *studъ 'cold').

засудить.etymology: Formed from prefix за- ('condemn, judge unfavorably') + судить ('to judge, try in court'), inherited from Old East Slavic судити, from Proto-Slavic *sǫditi (from *sǫdъ 'judgment, court').

засунуть.etymology: Formed from prefix за- ('into, behind') + сунуть ('to shove, thrust, poke'), inherited from Old East Slavic сунути, from Proto-Slavic *sunǫti ('to push, thrust, pour').

засыпать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic засыпати and Proto-Slavic *zasypati ('to fall asleep', imperfective of заснуть), built from inchoative за- + the iterative stem *-sypati of спать (*sъpati 'to sleep', showing regular Proto-Slavic lengthening of the root yer *ъ -> *y > ы in iterative verbs).
засыпать.notes: In the sense 'to fall asleep' the stress is always засыпать (paired with заснуть); a homograph from сыпать ('to pour, strew') means 'to fill up or cover by pouring' (perfective засыпать, imperfective засыпать).

затащить.etymology: Formed from the prefix за- ('into, up') + тащить ('to drag, pull, haul', an East Slavic verb related to таскать 'to carry, drag').

history.meaning: to drag, haul -> to drag into or up; (colloquial) to drag someone along to a place

затевать.etymology: Imperfective of затеять ('to start up, devise, undertake'), formed from the prefix за- + dialectal/archaic теять ('to do, make, contrive', from Proto-Slavic *tějati / *dějati).

затем.etymology: Adverb formed by univerbation of the prepositional phrase за тем ('after that, behind that'), combining the preposition за ('behind, after') with тем, the instrumental singular of то ('that', Proto-Slavic *to).

history.meaning: then, after that, subsequently; (with чтобы) in order to

затечь.etymology: Formed from prefix за- ('into; swell with stagnant fluid') + течь ('to flow'), inherited from Old East Slavic течи, from Proto-Slavic *teťi (*tekti), from PIE *tekʷ-; of a limb, 'to go numb or stiff from impeded circulation'.

history.meaning: to flow into; to go numb or stiffen (of a limb)

затея.etymology: Deverbal noun from затеять ('to undertake, contrive, start'), formed in East Slavic from prefix за- + bound stem -теять (altered from задеять 'to begin to do', from Proto-Slavic *dějati 'to do, put').

затеять.etymology: East Slavic verb formed from prefix за- + -теять ('to contrive, start'), explained by Vasmer as a transformation of задеять ('to begin to do, lay down', from Proto-Slavic *zadějati, from *za- + *dějati 'to do, place').

history.meaning: to lay down, begin to do

заткнуться.etymology: Reflexive form of заткнуть ('to plug up, stopper, gag'), formed from prefix за- + ткнуть ('to poke, thrust, stick', semelfactive of тыкать, from Proto-Slavic *tъknǫti) + -ся, literally 'to stopper oneself'.

зато.etymology: Fused adversative conjunction from the prepositional phrase за то ('in exchange for that, to make up for that'), combining за ('for, in exchange for') + то ('that', neuter of тот).

history.meaning: on the bright side, on the other hand, to make up for it

затонуть.etymology: Formed from completive за- + тонуть ('to sink, drown', inherited from Proto-Slavic *tonǫti < *topnǫti, with simplification of *pn -> н; related to топить 'to sink, submerge').

history.meaning: to sink -> to sink to the bottom, founder (of a ship)

затормозить.etymology: Formed from prefix за- ('bring to a halt') + тормозить ('to brake, slow down'), denominative from тормоз ('wheel brake, drag shoe', borrowed from Greek τόρμος 'socket, pin, peg keeping a wheel in place' or via Turkic).

затрата.etymology: Deverbal noun from затратить ('to spend, expend'), formed from prefix за- + тратить ('to spend, consume, waste'), inherited from Old East Slavic тратити, from Proto-Slavic *tratiti.

затягивать.etymology: Imperfective of затянуть ('to pull tight; to draw in; to delay'), formed from prefix за- + тягивать (iterative of тянуть 'to pull, draw', from Proto-Slavic *tęgnǫti).

history.meaning: to tighten; to drag out, delay

затянуть.etymology: Perfective verb formed from prefix за- ('tight, shut, into') + тянуть ('to pull, draw, stretch'). The verb тянуть descends from Old East Slavic тянути and Proto-Slavic *tęgnoti ('to pull, stretch'), from PIE *ten- ('to stretch, pull tight'). It is a cousin of English thin, tend, and tension.

затянуться.etymology: Reflexive form of затянуть ('to tighten; to prolong, drag out'), formed from prefix за- + тянуть ('to pull, stretch', from Proto-Slavic *tęgnǫti) + -ся.

history.meaning: to be tightened; to drag on

зафиксировать.etymology: Formed from perfective prefix за- + фиксировать ('to fix, secure, record'), borrowed via German fixieren (and French fixer) from Medieval Latin fīxāre, from Latin fīxus, past participle of fīgere ('to fasten, fix').

захват.etymology: Deverbal noun from захватить ('to seize, grab, capture'), formed from prefix за- + хватить ('to grab, snatch', from Proto-Slavic *xvatiti).

захватить.etymology: Formed from prefix за- + хватить ('to grab, seize, snatch'), inherited from Old East Slavic хватити, from Proto-Slavic *xvatiti ('to snatch, grasp').

history.meaning: to grab, bring along; to seize, capture

захватчик.etymology: Agent noun derived from захватить / захват ('seizure, capture', from за- + хватить, Proto-Slavic *xvatiti) + the agent suffix -чик.

заходить.etymology: Imperfective of зайти ('to drop in, enter, go behind'), inherited from Old East Slavic заходити, formed from за- + ходить ('to walk, go', from Proto-Slavic *xoditi).

history.meaning: to go behind, set, drop in

захолустье.etymology: Prepositional-prefixal neuter noun formed with за- ('behind, sheltered by') + dialectal холусть / халуга ('wattle fence, thicket, sheltered corner', of Slavic origin) + suffix -ье, originally 'a secluded spot behind a fence or thicket'.

захотеть.etymology: Inchoative perfective formed from the prefix за- ('begin to') + хотеть ('to want, wish', inherited from Old East Slavic хотѣти, from Proto-Slavic *xotěti).

history.meaning: to feel like, begin to want

захотеться.etymology: Impersonal reflexive perfective verb formed from inchoative prefix за- ('begin to') + хотеть ('to want, wish', inherited from Old East Slavic хотѣти, Proto-Slavic *xotěti) + -ся.

history.meaning: to feel like, begin to want

зацепиться.etymology: Reflexive form of зацепить ('to hook, snag, catch on'), formed from prefix за- + цепить ('to hook, fasten', related to цепь 'chain', from Proto-Slavic *čěpiti) + -ся.

history.meaning: to catch, snag on, get hooked

зачать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic зачати ('to begin, conceive'), from Proto-Slavic *začęti, formed from prefix *za- + *čęti ('to begin', compare начать, from PIE *kʷen-).

зачем.etymology: Univerbation of the prepositional phrase за чем ('behind/for what?, for what purpose?'), combining the preposition за ('for') with чем, the instrumental singular of что ('what', from Old East Slavic чьто).
зачем.notes: Asks about purpose or goal ('what for?'), whereas **почему** asks about cause ('because of what?').

зачитать.etymology: Formed from the prefix за- + читать ('to read', from Proto-Slavic *čitati); in official and public usage it means 'to read out loud (a document, verdict, or announcement) before an audience'.

history.meaning: to read out loud to an audience; (colloquial) to wear out or fail to return a borrowed book

зашиться.etymology: Reflexive form of зашить ('to sew up'), from prefix за- + шить ('to sew', Old East Slavic шити, Proto-Slavic *šiti, PIE *syuh₁-) + -ся; in colloquial medical slang, 'to have an anti-alcohol implant stitched under the skin'.

history.meaning: to sew oneself up; to get an anti-alcohol implant

защемить.etymology: Formed with prefix за- from щемить ('to pinch, squeeze, press painfully'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *ščemiti ('to pinch, clamp, squeeze'; related to щемящий).

защита.etymology: Deverbal noun from защитить ('to shield, defend, protect'), borrowed with Old Church Slavonic щ (< *tj) from защитити, derived from за- + щит ('shield', Proto-Slavic *ščitъ).

защитить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic защитити / Old Church Slavonic защитити ('to shield, protect, defend'), formed from за- ('behind') + щит ('shield', from Proto-Slavic *ščitъ).

history.meaning: to cover with a shield, defend

защитник.etymology: Agent noun derived from защитить ('to defend, shield', borrowed/modeled with Church Slavonic -щ- from защитити, from за- + щит 'shield', Proto-Slavic *ščitъ) + suffix -ник.

защитный.etymology: Relational adjective formed with the suffix -ный from защита ('protection, defence'), a deverbal noun from защитить ('to protect, shield'), built on prefix за- ('behind') + щит ('shield', from Proto-Slavic *ščitъ): literally 'placing behind a shield'.

защищать.etymology: Imperfective of защитить ('to defend, protect, shield'), borrowed from Old Church Slavonic защищати (with South Slavic щ < *tj), derived from за- ('behind') + щит ('shield', Proto-Slavic *ščitъ).

защищаться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective of защитить ('to defend, shield'), formed with Church Slavonic -щ- (*tj) from защищати, derived from prefix за- + щит ('shield', Proto-Slavic *ščitъ) + -ся.

защёлка.etymology: Deverbal noun from защёлкнуть / защёлкать ('to click shut, snap shut'), formed from prefix за- + щёлкать ('to click, snap', onomatopoeic Proto-Slavic *ščьlkati).

заявить.etymology: Formed from prefix за- ('forth, publicly') + явить ('to show, manifest, reveal'), inherited from Old East Slavic явити, from Proto-Slavic *javiti (causative from *javě 'openly, manifestly').

заявка.etymology: Deverbal noun derived from заявить / заявлять ('to declare, submit a claim or entry', from за- + явить, Proto-Slavic *javiti) + noun suffix -ка.

заявление.etymology: Verbal noun formed from заявить ('to declare, announce, state officially'), built from the prefix за- and явить ('to show, manifest, make public', from Proto-Slavic *javiti 'to make manifest').

history.meaning: to declare → official statement, written application, police report

заявлять.etymology: Imperfective of заявить ('to declare, state officially, report'), formed from за- + являть / явить ('to show, manifest, make known', derived from явный 'evident, open', Proto-Slavic *javiti).

history.meaning: to declare, announce, file a report

morphemes.meaning: show, make known (from явить with в -> вл)

заяц.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic заяць, from Proto-Slavic *zajęcь ('hare'), formed with the diminutive suffix *-ьcь from an earlier consonant-stem *zaję (stem *zajęt-, literally 'jumper').

званый.etymology: Originally the past passive participle of звать ('to call, invite', inherited from Old East Slavic зъвати, Proto-Slavic *zъvati, PIE *ǵʰewH-), lexicalized as an adjective meaning 'invited, by invitation' (as in званый ужин).

звать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic зъвати (present зову, зовеши, with strong yer ъ vocalized to о in present forms), from Proto-Slavic *zъvati ('to call, invite, name'), continuing Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰewH- ('to call, invoke'), directly cognate with Sanskrit hávate ('calls, invokes') and Avestan zavaiti.
звать.notes: Used in the standard construction for telling or asking someone's name: **Как вас зовут?** ('What do they call you? / What is your name?'), **Меня зовут...**.

звезда.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic звѣзда ('star', Old Church Slavonic звѣзда), from Proto-Slavic *gvězda (with regular East and South Slavic palatalization *gvě- > звѣ-; compare Polish gwiazda), from Balto-Slavic *źwaiźdā (compare Lithuanian žvaigždė̃ 'star').

звенеть.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic звьнѣти ('to ring, sound, clink'), from Proto-Slavic *zvьněti (e-grade counterpart of *zvonъ, Russian звон 'ringing, peal'), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰwen- ('to sound, resound').

зверь.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic звѣрь, from Proto-Slavic *zvěrь ('wild animal, beast'), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰwer- ('wild beast'; cognate with Lithuanian žvėris, Latin ferus, Ancient Greek θήρ).

звон.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic звонъ ('ringing sound, peal of bells, clinking'), from Proto-Slavic *zvonъ, an o-grade noun built on the root *zvьněti ('to ring, resound', from PIE *ǵʰwen- 'to sound, ring'; compare Old Church Slavonic звьнѣти).

звонить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic звонити ('to ring a bell, resound'), from Proto-Slavic *zvoniti, a denominative verb from *zvonъ ('ringing sound, bell', modern Russian звон), related to *zvьněti ('to ring, tinkle').

звонко.etymology: Adverbial form in -о of звонкий ('clear-ringing, resonant, voiced'), formed from звон ('ringing sound, peal of bells', from Old East Slavic звонъ and Proto-Slavic *zvonъ).

звонок.etymology: Formed in East Slavic from звон ('ringing sound, peal', from Proto-Slavic *zvonъ) + the diminutive/instrument suffix -ок: originally 'a small handbell or door-bell', and later extended to the ring of a bell and to a telephone call.

звук.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic звукъ (Old Church Slavonic звѫкъ, 'sound'), from Proto-Slavic *zvǫkъ, a nasalized o-grade derivative of the same Indo-European acoustic root *ǵʰwen- ('to sound, resound') as звон ('ringing') and звенеть ('to ring').

звучать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic звучати ('to sound, resound'), a stative/intransitive verb in *-ěti (with *k + *ě > чa) derived from звук ('sound', from Proto-Slavic *zvǫkъ).

звучный.etymology: Derived from звук ('sound', from Old East Slavic звукъ, Proto-Slavic *zvǫkъ, nasal-infix ablaut relative of звон 'ringing') + the adjective suffix -ный (with palatalization к > ч).

звякнуть.etymology: Semelfactive perfective verb formed with the single-action suffix -ну-ть from звякать ('to clink, jingle'). The root звяк- is an expressive Slavic sound-imitating formation closely related to звон ('ringing') and звяга ('resonant sound', Proto-Slavic *zvęga / *zvonъ), capturing the short metallic clink of keys, coins, or glass.

history.meaning: to clink repeatedly → to give a single clink

звёздный.etymology: Derived from звезда ('star', inherited from Old East Slavic звѣзда, from Proto-Slavic *gvězda, from PIE *ǵʰwoyǵʰdʰeh₂) + the relational adjective suffix -ный.

здание.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic зъдание ('building, edifice, creation'), verbal noun of зъдати ('to build, fashion out of clay', from Proto-Slavic *zьdati, related to *zьdь 'clay, wall').

здесь.etymology: Formed from Old East Slavic сьде ('here', Old Church Slavonic сьде), built from the proximal demonstrative stem *sь ('this') + the locative adverbial suffix *-de (compare где 'where'). After loss of the weak yer vowel caused voicing of сд- to зд- (зде), Russian reinforced the word with a second enclitic demonstrative -сь ('this').

здоровенный.etymology: Colloquial augmentative adjective derived from здоровый ('healthy; colloquially big, robust, hefty', from East Slavic здоровъ, Proto-Slavic *sъdorvъ 'sound, made of good wood') + the expressive augmentative suffix -енный.

здорово.etymology: Formed from the neuter short form of здоровый ('healthy, robust, big, fine'), inherited from Old East Slavic съдоровъ (displaying East Slavic pleophony -оро-), from Proto-Slavic *sъdorvъ ('made of good wood, sound, healthy', from *sъ- 'good' + *dervo 'tree, wood'). With stress on the first syllable (**здорово**), it functions as an enthusiastic colloquial evaluation ('great, cool, awesome!'); with stress on the second syllable (**здорово**), it is a colloquial greeting ('hi, hello!').

здоровый.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic съдоровыи ('healthy, sound, strong', with East Slavic pleophony -оро-; compare Church Slavonic здравыи), from Proto-Slavic *sъdorvъ (from *sъ- 'good, well' + *dorvo / *dervo 'tree, wood', literally 'made of good wood, sturdy as a tree').

здоровье.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic съдоровье (showing East Slavic pleophony -оро-), formed with the abstract neuter suffix -ье (*-ьje) from съдоровъ / здоровый ('healthy, sound'), from Proto-Slavic *sъdorvъ ('of good wood/timber, robust', from *sъ- 'good' + *dervo 'tree, wood').
здоровье.notes: Used in the standard toast **За здоровье!** ('To your health!') and in **На здоровье!** ('You're welcome!', said in reply to thanks for food or hospitality).

здравие.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic здравие ('health, soundness', corresponding to native East Slavic здоровье), derived from здравъ ('healthy, sound', from Proto-Slavic *sъdorvъ).

здравствовать.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic здравьствовати ('to be in good health, thrive'), formed from здравъ ('healthy', South Slavic counterpart of здоровый, from Proto-Slavic *sъdorvъ); the imperative здравствуй(те) ('be healthy!') became the standard Russian greeting 'hello'.

здравствуй.etymology: Second-person singular imperative of здравствовать ('to be in good health, thrive'), formed on the Old Church Slavonic stem здрав- (corresponding to native East Slavic здоров- in здоровый), from Proto-Slavic *sъdorvъ ('sound, healthy'). Literally, здравствуй! is a wish meaning 'be healthy!'.

history.meaning: healthy → to be in good health

здравствуй.notes: The first **в** is silent in pronunciation: **[здраствуй]**.

здравствуйте.etymology: Grammatically the formal plural imperative of здравствовать ('to thrive, be in good health'), so greeting someone with Здравствуйте! literally wishes 'be healthy!'. The root здрав- is the Church Slavonic counterpart of native East Slavic здоров- (здоровый), from Proto-Slavic *sъdorvъ ('sound, sturdy', literally 'of good wood', built on *sъ- 'good' + *dervo 'tree, timber').

history.meaning: healthy → to be in good health

здравствуйте.notes: Pronounced with a silent first в (sounded like 'zdrastvuyte'). Use singular *Здравствуй* with one close friend or relative.

здрасьте.etymology: Colloquial phonetic contraction in rapid everyday speech of the formal greeting здравствуйте! ('hello!', literally 'be healthy!', second-person plural imperative of здравствовать, from Church Slavonic здравъ 'healthy').

history.meaning: be well! (formal greeting) -> hello, hi (casual); well I never! (ironic surprise)

здрасьте.notes: Besides being a casual spoken 'hello', здрасьте! (or ну здрасьте!) is very often used as an exclamation of ironic surprise or protest ('Well, of all things! / Come on now!').

зелень.etymology: Collective feminine noun in -ь formed from зелёный ('green', from Old East Slavic зеленыи, Proto-Slavic *zelenъ, from PIE *ǵʰelh₃- 'green, yellow, flourishing'; cognate with золото 'gold', жёлтый 'yellow', and English yellow). Names both outdoor greenery and culinary fresh herbs (dill, parsley, scallions).

зелёный.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic зеленыи ('green'), from Proto-Slavic *zelenъ, related to зелье ('greenery, herbs') and золото ('gold'), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰelh₃- ('green, yellow, gleaming').

земля.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic земля ('earth, ground, soil, land'), from Proto-Slavic *zemľa, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰéǵʰōm ('earth, ground'; cognate with Lithuanian žemė, Latin humus, and Ancient Greek χθών).

земной.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic земьныи and Proto-Slavic *zemьnъ ('earthly, terrestrial'), relational adjective formed with -ный from the older unextended root *zem- of земля ('earth, ground, land', Proto-Slavic *zemľa, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰéǵʰōm 'earth').

зеркало.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic зеркало (alongside Church Slavonic зерцало), from Proto-Slavic *zьrkadlo, built from the gaze root *zьrěti ('to look, behold') plus the tool suffix *-dlo (regularly becoming -ло in East Slavic): literally 'a looking-tool'.

зефирка.etymology: Colloquial singulative/diminutive formed with -ка from зефир ('zephyr, light fruit-puree and egg-white confection; originally the gentle west wind'), borrowed via French zéphyr and Latin zephyrus from Ancient Greek ζέφυρος ('west wind').

зима.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic зима ('winter'), from Proto-Slavic *zima, continuing Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰéy-m- ('winter, snow'), directly cognate with Lithuanian žiemà ('winter'), Latin hiems, Ancient Greek χειμών, and Sanskrit héman ('in winter'; also the root of Himalaya, 'abode of snow').

зимний.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic зимьнии, relational adjective formed with the suffix -ний from зима ('winter', from Proto-Slavic *zima, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰéy-m- 'winter, snow').

зимой.etymology: Grammaticalized instrumental singular (зимою / зимой) of зима ('winter'), inherited from Old East Slavic зима, from Proto-Slavic *zima, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰéy-m- ('winter, snow'; cognate with Latin hiems, Sanskrit hima).

злить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic зълити ('to anger, provoke'), causative verb formed with -ить from злой ('evil, angry, malicious', from Proto-Slavic *zъlъ).

злиться.etymology: Reflexive of злить ('to anger, irritate'), derived from зло / злой ('evil, anger / angry, wicked', from Old East Slavic зълъ, Proto-Slavic *zъlъ, from PIE *ǵʰwels- 'crooked, wrong'; compare Lithuanian atžūlùs 'rude, harsh').

зло.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic зъло ('evil, harm, misfortune'), substantivized neuter singular of злой (Old East Slavic зълъ, 'bad, evil'), from Proto-Slavic *zъlo (from *zъlъ, originally 'crooked, twisted', cognate with Lithuanian atžūlas 'coarse, perverse').

злодей.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic зълодѣи ('evildoer, malefactor', calquing Ancient Greek κακοῦργος and Latin maleficus), a compound of зъло ('evil', Russian зло) + the agent stem of дѣяти ('to do, act', Proto-Slavic *dějati).

злой.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic зълъ (long form зълыи), from Proto-Slavic *zъlъ ('bad, evil, angry, crooked'), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰwel- ('to bend, curve, deviate from the right path'; compare Lithuanian Pa-žulnùs 'sloping, crooked', Avestan zūrah- 'deceit, wrong', and Sanskrit hválati 'goes astray').

злостный.etymology: Formed in Russian with the adjectival suffix -ный from злость ('malice, spite, anger', from злой 'evil, angry'); in legal and official Russian it came to mean 'willfully persistent, habitual, flagrant' (as in злостный неплательщик 'habitual non-payer').

history.meaning: malice, anger -> malicious; chronic, habitual (of an offender)

злостный.notes: The middle -т- is silent in standard pronunciation: [злосный].

злость.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic зълость and Proto-Slavic *zъlostь ('malice, wickedness, anger'), formed with the abstract noun suffix -ость from злой (*zъlъ 'evil, bad, angry').

змея.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic змия ('snake, serpent'), from Proto-Slavic *zmьja (feminine counterpart to *zmьjь 'serpent, dragon'), derived as a taboo formation ('earth-crawler') from *zemja ('earth, ground', PIE *dʰéǵʰōm).

знак.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic знакъ and Old Church Slavonic знакъ ('sign, token, mark'), formed with the suffix *-kъ from Proto-Slavic *znati ('to know, recognize', from Proto-Indo-European *ǵneh₃-): literally 'that by which something is known or recognized'.

знакомить.etymology: Denominative verb derived from знакомый ('acquainted, familiar'), originally the present passive participle of знати ('to know', inherited from Old East Slavic знати, Proto-Slavic *znati, PIE *ǵneh₃-).

знакомиться.etymology: Reciprocal/reflexive form of знакомить ('to acquaint, introduce'), derived from знакомый ('acquainted, familiar', originally old present passive participle of знати 'to know', from Proto-Slavic *znati) + -ся.

знакомство.etymology: Formed in Russian with the abstract/collective suffix -ство from знакомый ('acquainted, familiar; acquaintance'), which originated as the present passive participle of an older verb *знакомить / знати ('to know', Proto-Slavic *znati).

history.meaning: acquainted, familiar -> acquaintance, meeting, circle of acquaintances

знакомый.etymology: Originally an old present passive participle in -мый formed from знакомить / знак ('to acquaint / sign, token of recognition', built on the Proto-Slavic root *zna- 'to know', modern Russian знать). Used both as an adjective ('familiar, known') and as a substantivized noun ('an acquaintance').

знаменитость.etymology: Derived from знаменитый ('famous, celebrated', from Old Church Slavonic / Old East Slavic знаменитъ 'marked, distinguished', from знамя, gen. знамени 'sign, mark, banner', Proto-Slavic *znamę) + abstract/person suffix -ость.

знаменитый.etymology: Inherited via Old Church Slavonic знаменитъ ('marked, distinguished, renowned'), formed with the adjectival suffix -итый from знамя (stem знамен-, from Old East Slavic знамя, genitive знамене 'mark, sign, banner', built on Proto-Slavic *znati 'to know').

знаток.etymology: Agent noun derived from знать ('to know', inherited from Old East Slavic знати, Proto-Slavic *znati, PIE *ǵneh₃-) + the suffix -ток (built on the participial stem знат-).

знать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic знати ('to know, recognize'), from Proto-Slavic *znati, continuing the ancient Proto-Indo-European root *ǵneh₃- ('to know, recognize'), directly cognate with English know, Latin (g)nōscō, Ancient Greek γιγνώσκω, Lithuanian žinóti, and Sanskrit jānāti.

значение.etymology: Verbal noun formed with -ение from значить ('to mean, signify'), derived from знак ('sign, mark, token', from Proto-Slavic *znakъ, from the root of *znati 'to know').

значит.etymology: Originally the third-person singular present tense ('it means, it signifies') of значить ('to mean, signify'), derived from знак ('sign, mark', from Proto-Slavic *znakъ / *znati 'to know'). Used parenthetically in conversation as 'so, then, that means'.

значительно.etymology: Adverbial form of значительный ('significant, considerable'), derived from значить ('to mean, signify'), from знак ('sign, mark', Proto-Slavic *znakъ, from *znati 'to know').

значить.etymology: Formed from знак ('sign, mark, token', from Proto-Slavic *znakъ, built on the same Indo-European root *ǵneh₃- 'to know, recognize' as знать) + verbal suffix -ить: 'to be a sign of, signify, mean'.

значок.etymology: Diminutive of знак ('sign, mark, emblem') formed with the masculine diminutive suffix -ок (with regular velar palatalization к → ч). Russian знак derives from Proto-Slavic *znakъ ('mark, token, sign'), built on the verb *znati ('to know, recognize', PIE *ǵneh3- 'to know'). It is a direct Indo-European cognate of English know, token, and Greek gnosis.

знающий.etymology: Lexicalized present active participle of знать ('to know', inherited from Old East Slavic знати, Proto-Slavic *znati, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵneh₃- 'to know', cognate with English know).

зодчий.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic зодъчии ('potter, mason, builder'), derived from зодъ ('clay; clay wall or building'), an o-grade ablaut noun related to зьдати ('to mold from clay, build', Proto-Slavic *zьdati, from PIE *dʰeyǵʰ- 'to knead clay').

золотистый.etymology: Adjective formed with the colour/hue suffix -истый ('having the sheen or tint of') from золото ('gold'), inherited from Old East Slavic золото (with East Slavic pleophony -оло-) and Proto-Slavic *zolto (cognate with English gold).

morphemes.meaning: having the tint or lustre of

золото.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic золото and Proto-Slavic *zolto ('gold', showing regular East Slavic pleophony -оло- from *-ol- between consonants; compare Old Church Slavonic злато and Polish złoto), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰelh₃-to- ('yellow, gleaming metal'), directly cognate with English gold and German Gold.

золотой.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic золотыи ('golden, made of gold'), derived from золото ('gold', showing East Slavic pleophony -оло- from Proto-Slavic *zolto; compare Old Church Slavonic злато), continuing Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰólh₃-tom ('the yellow/gleaming metal', from the same root *ǵʰelh₃- as жёлтый 'yellow' and зелёный 'green'), directly cognate with English gold and German Gold.

зомби.etymology: Borrowed in the 20th century from English zombie (or French zombi), from Haitian Creole zonbi, of West-Central African (Bantu) origin (compare Kikongo nzambi 'spirit, god' and Kimbundu nzumbi 'ghost, spirit of the dead').

зона.etymology: Borrowed via German Zone and French zone from Latin zōna ('belt, girdle; geographical zone'), from Ancient Greek ζώνη ('belt, girdle'); the Russian slang sense 'prison camp' arose from the guarded perimeter zone of Soviet labor camps.

зонт.etymology: Back-formation in 19th-century Russian from зонтик ('umbrella, parasol'), which was borrowed in the Petrine era (originally as maritime naval zondek) from Dutch zonnedek ('sun-canopy stretched over a ship's deck', from zon 'sun' + dek 'deck, cover'). Because Russian speakers re-analyzed the final -ик of зонтик as the native diminutive suffix -ик (as in столик or дворик), they extracted зонт as the base noun for a full-sized umbrella!
зонт.notes: One of Russian's most famous linguistic back-formations: **зонтик** came first (from Dutch *zonnedek*), and **зонт** was created later by removing *-ик*.

зоопарк.etymology: Twentieth-century syllabic abbreviation (stump compound) of зоологический парк ('zoological park'), combining зоо- (from Ancient Greek ζῷον 'living being, animal') + парк ('park', via French parc from Medieval Latin parricus).

зоя.etymology: Russian feminine given name Зоя, borrowed via Church Slavonic and Byzantine Greek from Ancient Greek Ζωή (Zōḗ, literally 'life', from ζάω 'to live', the same root as English zoology). Originally adopted by Hellenistic Jews to translate the Hebrew name Ḥawwā (Eve, 'living').

зрелище.etymology: Borrowed from or modeled on Old Church Slavonic зьрѣлище ('spectacle, theater'), derived from зьрѣти ('to look at, behold', from Proto-Slavic *zьrěti) + the place/action noun suffix -лище.

зрение.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic зьрѣниѥ ('sight, vision'), verbal noun from зьрѣти ('to look, see, behold', from Proto-Slavic *zьrěti).

зритель.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic зьритель / Old Church Slavonic зьритель ('beholder, observer, spectator'), formed with the agent suffix -тель from зреть ('to look at, behold', from Proto-Slavic *zьrěti).

зря.etymology: Historically the fossilized present active participle (gerund) of the archaic verb зреть ('to look, see', Old East Slavic зьрѣти, Proto-Slavic *zьrěti). In the phrase не зря ('not looking blindly, not without reason'), зря shifted by back-formation or from 'just looking on idly / at random without thinking' to its modern meaning 'in vain, for nothing, pointlessly'.

history.meaning: at random, without thinking → in vain, for nothing

зуб.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic зубъ (and Old Church Slavonic зѫбъ), from Proto-Slavic *zǫbъ ('tooth'), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵómbʰos ('peg, row of teeth, tooth', from *ǵembʰ- 'to bite, snap'; exact cognate with Ancient Greek γόμφος 'peg, molar', Sanskrit jámbha- 'tooth, tusk', Lithuanian žam̃bas 'sharp edge', and English comb).

зубок.etymology: Diminutive of зуб ('tooth'), inherited from Old East Slavic зубъ, from Proto-Slavic *zǫbъ, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵómbʰos ('tooth, peg') + diminutive suffix -ок.

зуд.etymology: Deverbal noun from зудеть ('to itch; to buzz, drone'), from East Slavic зудъ, of expressive/onomatopoeic Proto-Slavic origin (*zǫdъ / *zǫděti, originally 'to buzz like a biting insect, sting, itch').

зять.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic зять ('son-in-law, sister's husband'), from Proto-Slavic *zętь, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵenh₁-ti-s ('kinsman by marriage/birth'; cognate with Lithuanian žéntas 'son-in-law' and Sanskrit jñātí 'kinsman').

и.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic и, from Proto-Slavic *i ('and, also, even'). Vasmer traces it to an old Indo-European demonstrative and connective particle *ei ('there, then, and so'; compare Lithuanian ir̃ 'and, also' and Ancient Greek εἰ 'if, so').

игнорировать.etymology: Borrowed via German ignorieren from Latin ignōrāre ('not to know, take no notice of, disregard'), related to ignārus ('unaware', from negative in- + Old Latin gnārus 'knowing', PIE *ǵneh₃-), adapted with -ировать.

иголка.etymology: Formed in Russian with the diminutive suffix -ка (and a fleeting -о- breaking up the consonant cluster) from игла ('needle', inherited from Old East Slavic игъла, Proto-Slavic *jьgъla 'needle').

history.meaning: needle -> sewing needle, pine needle, spine

игра.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic игра ('game, play, dance, festivity'), from Proto-Slavic *jьgra ('play, game, dance'). Deeper Indo-European etymology is debated (Vasmer discusses proposed connections to Sanskrit éjati 'stirs, moves' and Old Norse eikinn 'wild, lively').

играть.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic играти ('to play, dance, make merry'), a denominative verb from игра ('game, play, music, dance', from Proto-Slavic *jьgra).
играть.notes: Uses **в** + accusative for games and sports (*играть в шахматы*) and **на** + prepositional for musical instruments (*играть на пианино, на скрипке*).

игрок.etymology: Agent noun derived from игра ('game, play', inherited from Old East Slavic игра, from Proto-Slavic *jьgra) + the agent suffix -ок.

игрушечный.etymology: Relational adjective formed in Russian with the suffix -ный (with к -> ч palatalization and fleeting е) from игрушка ('toy, plaything'), itself derived from игра ('game, play', Proto-Slavic *jьgra).

игрушка.etymology: Derived with diminutive/instrument suffix -ушка from игра ('game, play') / играть ('to play'), inherited from Old East Slavic игра, from Proto-Slavic *jьgra ('game, play').

идеально.etymology: Adverb formed from the short neuter of идеальный ('ideal, perfect'), derived from идеал ('ideal', borrowed via German Ideal / French idéal from Late Latin ideālis, built on Ancient Greek ἰδέα 'form, model, idea').

идеальный.etymology: Borrowed in the 18th–19th centuries (adapting German ideal or French idéal with the Russian adjectival suffix -ный), from Late Latin ideālis ('existing in idea or archetype, archetypal'), built on Ancient Greek ἰδέα ('form, look, ideal pattern').

идея.etymology: Borrowed in the 18th century via Polish idea, German Idee, or French idée and Latin idea from Ancient Greek ἰδέα (idéa, 'look, semblance, form, Platonic archetype'), derived from ἰδεῖν ('to see', from the same Indo-European root *weyd- 'to see, know' as Russian видеть).

идиот.etymology: Borrowed via French idiot or German Idiot (and Late Latin idiōta 'uneducated person, layman') from Ancient Greek ἰδιώτης (idiṓtēs, 'private citizen not holding public office; layman, unskilled person'), derived from ἴδιος (ídios, 'one's own, private').

history.meaning: private → private citizen, layman, ignorant person

идиотизм.etymology: Borrowed from French idiotisme ('idiocy; linguistic idiom'), from idiot ('idiot'), via Latin idiōta from Ancient Greek ἰδιώτης ('private person, layman, unlearned person', from ἴδιος 'one's own, private').

идиотка.etymology: Formed in Russian with the feminine suffix -ка from идиот ('idiot'), borrowed via French idiot and German Idiot from Latin idiōta and Ancient Greek ἰδιώτης (idiōtēs, originally 'private person, layman, unlearned person', from ἴδιος 'one's own, private').

идти.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic ити (present иду), from Proto-Slavic *iti, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁éyti ('to go'; compare Latin īre and Lithuanian eĩti). Its past tense шёл, шла, шли comes from a separate suppletive Slavic stem *šьd- (related to ходить).

из.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic изъ / ис, from Proto-Slavic *jьz ('out of, from inside'), closely cognate with Lithuanian ìš ('out of') and connected by Vasmer with Proto-Indo-European *eǵʰs (compare Latin ex and Ancient Greek ἐξ 'out of').

из-за.etymology: Compound Russian preposition formed by joining из ('out from') + за ('behind'): literally 'out from behind' (e.g. солнце вышло из-за туч 'the sun came out from behind the clouds'), which also developed the causal sense 'because of, on account of'.

из-под.etymology: Compound preposition formed in East Slavic by combining из ('out of, from inside', from Proto-Slavic *jьz) + под ('under', from Proto-Slavic *podъ). Governs the genitive case to express motion 'from under' or a container that formerly held something (банка из-под чая 'an empty tea tin').

history.meaning: from under; formerly holding (of a container)

избавиться.etymology: Reflexive form of избавить ('to deliver, save, rid'), inherited from Old East Slavic / Old Church Slavonic избавити, from Proto-Slavic *jьzbaviti (prefix *jьz- 'out of' + *baviti, causative of *byti 'to be').

history.meaning: to free, deliver (cause to be out of)
to get rid of, be freed from

избаловать.etymology: Formed from prefix из- ('thoroughly, to excess') + баловать ('to pamper, indulge, spoil'), inherited from Old East Slavic баловати.

избегать.etymology: Imperfective of избежать ('to avoid, escape'), borrowed from or modeled on Old Church Slavonic избѣгати (with prefix из- 'out of'), from Proto-Slavic *jьzběgati (*jьz- + *běgati 'to run').

избежать.etymology: Borrowed from or modeled on Old Church Slavonic избѣжати ('to flee out of, escape'), formed from prefix из- ('out of, away from') + бѣжати ('to run, flee', from Proto-Slavic *běžati, PIE *bʰegʷ-).

избирком.etymology: Twentieth-century syllabic abbreviation (сложносокращённое слово) of избирательная комиссия ('election commission'), combining избирательный ('electoral', from избирать 'to elect, choose') and комиссия ('commission').

избить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic избити and Proto-Slavic *jьzbiti, formed from the intensive/completive prefix из- ('all over, thoroughly') + бить ('to beat, strike', Proto-Slavic *biti).

избранный.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic избьраныи, past passive participle of избьрати ('to choose out, select, elect', from prefix из- 'out of' + бьрати 'to take', Proto-Slavic *bьrati).

известно.etymology: Impersonal predicate and adverb continuing the short neuter singular of известный ('known, well-known'), borrowed from Old Church Slavonic извѣстьнъ ('certain, reliably known', built on извѣстити 'to inform, make known', from вѣсть 'news, knowledge').

известный.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic извѣстьнъ ('known for certain, well-known, reliable'), derived from извѣсть / вѣсть ('news, knowledge, message', Russian весть), from Proto-Slavic *věstь (built on *věděti 'to know', PIE *weyd-).

извинение.etymology: Verbal noun from извинить ('to excuse, pardon, absolve of blame'), formed from prefix из- ('out of, from') + вина ('guilt, fault, blame', inherited from Proto-Slavic *vina).

извинить.etymology: Formed from prefix из- ('out of, away from') + винить / вина ('to blame / guilt, fault', from Old East Slavic вина, Proto-Slavic *vina): literally 'to release from blame, clear of fault', hence 'to excuse, pardon'.

history.meaning: to free from blame → to excuse, forgive

извинить.notes: The polite imperative **Извините!** ('Excuse me! / Sorry!') literally asks 'clear me of fault!'.

извиниться.etymology: Reflexive form of извинить ('to excuse, clear of fault', built from из- 'out of' + вина 'fault, blame'). Literally 'to clear oneself of fault', hence 'to apologize, say one is sorry'.

извиняться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective of извинить ('to excuse, pardon'), formed from prefix из- ('out of, away from') + винить / вина ('fault, guilt, blame', from Proto-Slavic *vina) + -ся, literally 'to clear oneself of blame'.

издалека.etymology: Prepositional-prefixal adverb formed from preposition из ('from, out of') + the short genitive singular form далека (from далёкий 'far, distant', Proto-Slavic *dalekъ).

издеваться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective formed from из- + девать ('to do, put, make', iterative of деть < Proto-Slavic *děti; compare деяние), originally meaning 'to contrive tricks upon, subject someone to mockery'.

измена.etymology: Deverbal noun from изменить ('to change, alter; to betray, be unfaithful'), formed from prefix из- + менить ('to change, exchange', from мена 'exchange', Proto-Slavic *měna, PIE *mey-).

изменение.etymology: Verbal noun in -ение from изменить ('to change, alter'), built from из- ('out') + менить ('to change, exchange', from мена 'exchange', Proto-Slavic *měniti / *měna).

изменить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic измѣнити (and Old Church Slavonic измѣнити 'to exchange, alter'), formed from из- ('out') + мѣнити ('to change, exchange', from мѣна 'exchange, alternation', Proto-Slavic *měna). With an accusative object (изменить план), it means 'to change, alter'; with a dative object (изменить мужу / родине), it means 'to betray, be unfaithful to, cheat on'.

history.meaning: to change (+ acc.); to betray, cheat on (+ dat.)

измениться.etymology: Perfective reflexive/intransitive verb formed by adding -ся to изменить ('to change, alter'), derived from из- + менить (from Proto-Slavic *měna 'change, exchange').

изменять.etymology: Imperfective of изменить, formed from из- ('out, away from') + менять ('to change, exchange', Proto-Slavic *měniti); with an accusative object it means 'to change, alter', while with a dative person (изменять кому-либо) it means 'to betray, be unfaithful to, cheat on'.

history.meaning: to alter, change; to betray, cheat on

измерить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic измѣрити / Old Church Slavonic измѣрити, formed from the prefix из- ('out, completely') + мерить ('to measure', from мера 'measure', Proto-Slavic *měra).

измерять.etymology: Imperfective partner of измерить ('to measure out'), formed with prefix из- ('out, thoroughly', Church Slavonic variant of вы-) + мерять / мерить ('to measure', derived from мера 'measure', from Proto-Slavic *měra, PIE *meh₁- 'to measure').

измор.etymology: Deverbal noun from изморить ('to starve out, wear down to death'), formed from prefix из- + морить ('to kill, starve, exhaust', causative of мереть 'to die', from Proto-Slavic *moriti, PIE *mer-).

history.meaning: to cause to die, starve, exhaust

изнутри.etymology: Prepositional-prefixal adverb formed from из ('from, out of') + нутри (old genitive/locative of нутрь 'inside, interior', from Old East Slavic нутрь, Proto-Slavic *jьnǫtrь, from PIE *h₁en- 'in').

изображать.etymology: Imperfective of изобразить, borrowed/adapted from Old Church Slavonic изображати ('to form, depict, represent'), built on из- ('out') + образ ('image, likeness, form', Proto-Slavic *obrazъ).

history.meaning: to portray, depict; to pretend to be, put on an act

morphemes.meaning: image, form (from образ with з -> ж)

изобразить.etymology: Borrowed/adapted from Old Church Slavonic изобразити ('to shape, depict, portray', calquing Ancient Greek ἐξεικονίζω), formed from из- ('out') + образ ('image, form, icon', Proto-Slavic *obrazъ) + -ить.

изобрести.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic изобрѣсти ('to find out, discover, invent'), formed from prefix из- + обрѣсти ('to find, come upon', from Proto-Slavic *obrěsti).

изолента.etymology: 20th-century Russian syllabic abbreviation of изоляционная лента ('insulating tape'), combining изоляционный (from изоляция 'insulation', from French isolation) + лента ('tape, ribbon', from German Linte / Latin linteum 'linen strip').
