опять.notes: **Опять** often implies repetition of something familiar or slightly tiresome ('again, once more'), whereas **снова** emphasizes starting afresh.

орать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic орати ('to shout, bellow'), from Proto-Slavic *orati / *orti ('to shout, roar'), of expressive/onomatopoeic origin (distinct from archaic орать 'to plow' < *orati).

орви.etymology: Russian medical initialism (ОРВИ) standing for острая респираторная вирусная инфекция ('acute respiratory viral infection').

организация.etymology: Borrowed via French organisation or German Organisation from Medieval Latin organisatio, derived from Greek ὄργανον (órganon, 'instrument, tool, organ').

организм.etymology: Borrowed from French organisme or German Organismus, formed in modern scientific Latin/French from Ancient Greek ὄργανον (órganon, 'instrument, bodily organ').

организовать.etymology: Borrowed via German organisieren or French organiser (ultimately from Medieval Latinizare / Greek ὄργανον 'instrument, organ'), adapted with the Russian verbal suffix -овать.

ордер.etymology: Borrowed via German Order or Dutch order from French ordre ('order, command, warrant'), ultimately from Latin ōrdō, ōrdinis ('row, rank, order').

орех.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic орѣхъ and Proto-Slavic *orěxъ ('nut, hazelnut, walnut'), with close Baltic cognates in Lithuanian riešutas and Latvian rieksts ('nut').

ореховый.etymology: Derived in Russian from орех ('nut; walnut') with the adjectival suffix -овый: 'made with nuts' or 'made of walnut wood / walnut-coloured'.

орешек.etymology: Diminutive of орех ('nut', inherited from Old East Slavic орѣхъ, from Proto-Slavic *orěxъ) + diminutive suffix -ек (with velar palatalization х > ш).

оригинал.etymology: Borrowed in the Petrine era via German Original / Polish oryginał from Medieval Latin originale ('original document or work'), substantivized neuter of Latin originalis ('from the beginning, original', from origo 'origin, source').

оригинально.etymology: Adverb formed from оригинальный ('original, novel', borrowed via German original or French original from Late Latin orīginālis 'from the origin', from orīgō) + -о.

оригинальный.etymology: Formed with the Russian adjective suffix -ный from оригинал ('original') or borrowed via French original and German original from Late Latin originālis ('existing from the beginning, original'), derived from Latin orīgō ('origin, source, birth', from orīrī 'to rise, begin').

ориентировать.etymology: Borrowed from German orientieren or French orienter ('to orient, originally to position facing the east'), derived from Latin oriēns (genitive orientis, 'rising sun, east').

оркестр.etymology: Borrowed in the 18th century via French orchestre or German Orchester from Latin orchēstra, from Ancient Greek ὀρχήστρα (orkhḗstra, 'area before the stage where the chorus danced', from ὀρχέομαι 'to dance').

оружие.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic оружие (influenced by Old Church Slavonic оружие), from Proto-Slavic *orǫžьje ('implement, weapon'), related to *orǫdьje ('tool, business').

орёл.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic орьлъ, from Proto-Slavic *orьlъ ('eagle'), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃er- ('eagle, large bird', cognate with Lithuanian erelis and Gothic ara).

осада.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic осада ('encirclement, siege'), deverbal noun from осадить ('to sit around, surround, besiege', from о- + садить 'to seat, place', Proto-Slavic *osada).

освежать.etymology: Imperfective verb paired with освежить ('to refresh, freshen up'), formed with prefix о- from свежий ('fresh, cool', from Old East Slavic свѣжии and Proto-Slavic *svěžь).

history.meaning: to make fresh → to refresh, brighten

освободить.etymology: Adopted via Old Church Slavonic освобoдити ('to set free, emancipate'), formed with the prefix о- from свобода ('freedom, liberty', from Proto-Slavic *svoboda, related to свой 'one's own').

освободиться.etymology: Reflexive of освободить ('to free, liberate'), inherited via Old Church Slavonic освободити (from prefix о- + свобода 'freedom, liberty', Proto-Slavic *svoboda) + -ся.

освобождаться.etymology: Reflexive/intransitive form in -ся of освобождать ('to free, clear, release'), imperfective counterpart of освободить, showing the Church Slavonic alternation д → жд built on свобода ('freedom', from Proto-Slavic *svoboda).

history.meaning: to free → to become free, be excused, clear up

освобождение.etymology: Borrowed via Old Church Slavonic освобождениѥ ('liberation, release'), verbal noun from освободити ('to set free', derived from свобода 'freedom', Proto-Slavic *svoboda) with South Slavic *dj > жд.

освоиться.etymology: Reflexive of освоить ('to master, make one's own, assimilate'), derived from prefix о- + свой ('one's own', from Proto-Slavic *svojь) + verbal suffix -ить + -ся.

history.meaning: to settle in, find one's feet

осень.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic осень and Proto-Slavic *esenь / *osenь ('autumn, harvest season'), cognate with Old Prussian assanis ('autumn') and Gothic asans ('harvest, summer work season').
осень.notes: A feminine third-declension noun ending in -ь (поздняя осень 'late autumn').

осетрина.etymology: Derived from осётр ('sturgeon', inherited from Old East Slavic осетръ, from Proto-Slavic *jesetrъ) + meat/flesh suffix -ина.

осетровый.etymology: Adjective formed with -овый from осётр ('sturgeon'), inherited from Old East Slavic осетръ, from Proto-Slavic *jesetrъ ('sturgeon', literally 'the sharp-scaled one', related to *ostrъ 'sharp').

оскорбить.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic оскорбити ('to grieve, afflict'), formed from prefix о- + скорбити ('to grieve, sorrow'), from Proto-Slavic *skъrbiti, derived from *skъrbь ('grief, sorrow, affliction').

оскорбление.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic оскрьбление ('affliction, grief, offense'), verbal noun derived from оскорбити ('to grieve, offend', from *skъrbь 'sorrow') + abstract suffix -ение.

оскорблять.etymology: Imperfective of оскорбить ('to insult, offend, grieve'), borrowed from Old Church Slavonic оскръбити ('to afflict, sadden'), from Proto-Slavic *ob-skъrbiti, from *skъrbь ('grief, sorrow', Russian скорбь).

ослабить.etymology: Formed from о- + слабый ('weak, loose, slack', Proto-Slavic *slabъ, cognate with German schlaff 'slack') + -ить: 'to weaken, loosen, slacken (a screw, tension, or grip)'.

осмелиться.etymology: Formed in Russian with prefix о- + смелиться ('to be bold'), derived from смелый ('bold, brave', from Proto-Slavic *smělъ, participial adjective of *směti 'to dare') + reflexive particle -ся.

history.meaning: to dare, to pluck up courage

осмотр.etymology: Deverbal noun formed by zero-suffixation from осмотреть ('to examine, inspect, look over'), from prefix о- ('around, over') + смотреть ('to look, watch', Old East Slavic смотрѣти, Proto-Slavic *sъmotriti).

осмотреть.etymology: Formed with prefix о- ('around, over') from смотреть ('to look, watch'), inherited from Old East Slavic съмотрити, from Proto-Slavic *sъmotriti.

осмотреться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of осмотреть ('to inspect, look around'), from о- ('around') + смотреть ('to look', Proto-Slavic *sъmotriti).

основа.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic основа ('warp threads stretched on a loom; foundation'), a deverbal noun from основати ('to set up the warp, lay a foundation', from Proto-Slavic *osnova / *snovati).

history.meaning: warp of a loom; foundation, base

основание.etymology: Inherited via Old East Slavic and Old Church Slavonic основаниѥ ('foundation, base, groundwork'), a verbal noun from основати ('to set up the warp threads on a loom, lay a foundation', built on о- + сновать 'to warp threads', from Proto-Slavic *snovati).

основной.etymology: Relational adjective formed from основа ('basis, foundation; originally the warp threads in weaving', from Proto-Slavic *osnova, from *ob- + *snovati 'to warp threads') + adjectival suffix -ной.

особа.etymology: Borrowed in the 17th century via Polish osoba and Ukrainian особа ('person, individual'), formed by univerbation of the prepositional phrase o sobie / о собѣ ('by oneself, apart', from reflexive pronoun *sobě), used to calque Latin persona.

особенно.etymology: Formed as the adverbial derivative in -о of особенный ('special, particular'), derived from особа ('individual person, apart') and the reflexive pronoun себе ('to oneself', as in особняком 'apart by oneself').

особенный.etymology: Extended adjectival form of особый ('special, separate, particular'), formed with the suffix -енный from особа / особь ('individual, person apart'), which goes back to the Old East Slavic prepositional phrase о собѣ ('by oneself, apart, separately', from о + собѣ, the dative/locative of the reflexive pronoun себя 'oneself').

особо.etymology: Adverbial form (short neuter singular) of особый ('special, separate, particular'), formed from the Old East Slavic prepositional phrase о собѣ ('by oneself, apart', from preposition о + dative/locative reflexive pronoun собѣ).

особый.etymology: Inherited from East Slavic особыи ('separate, distinct, special'), formed from the archaic adverb особь ('apart, separately'), which originated from the Old East Slavic prepositional phrase о собѣ ('by oneself', where собѣ is the older East Slavic dative/locative of the reflexive pronoun себя 'oneself', Proto-Slavic *o sobě; compare Polish osobny 'separate').

осознанно.etymology: Adverb derived from the passive participial adjective осознанный ('conscious, realized, deliberate', from осознать 'to realize') + adverbial suffix -о.

осознать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix о- + сознать ('to become conscious of, recognize'), itself formed from prefix со- ('with', calquing Latin con- / Greek συν- in conscientia / συνείδησις) + знать ('to know', Proto-Slavic *znati).

оставаться.etymology: Formed as the imperfective counterpart of остаться ('to stay, remain'), from о- ('around, behind') + ставать (imperfective stem of стать 'to stand, become', Proto-Slavic *stati) + -ся.
оставаться.notes: Present tense drops the -ва- syllable and takes stressed -ю, -ёшь: я остаюсь, ты остаёшься.

оставить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic оставити ('to leave behind, let remain'), from Proto-Slavic *ostaviti, formed from the prefix *o(b)- + *staviti ('to set, place, make stand', causative of *stati 'to stand').

оставлять.etymology: Imperfective verb derived from оставить ('to leave behind, let remain', with labial mutation в → вл before -ять), which combines the prefix о- with ставить ('to set, make stand', causative of стать): literally 'to set aside so that something remains standing'.

остальной.etymology: Formed in Russian with the adjective suffix -ной from older осталой ('left over, remaining'), an archaic -л- participle of остать / остаться ('to stay behind, remain', from о- + стать 'to stand, remain', Proto-Slavic *ostati).

останавливаться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective verb formed from останавливать ('to stop', secondary imperfective of остановить, from prefix о- + становить 'to set upright, place', derived from стан 'stand, camp', Proto-Slavic *stanъ) + reflexive particle -ся.

history.meaning: to stop; to stay at a place

остановить.etymology: Formed in East Slavic from о- + становить ('to set upright, place in a standing position', causative of стать 'to stand', from стан 'camp, station, stature', Proto-Slavic *stanъ): 'to bring to a standstill, stop'.

history.meaning: to set up, bring to a stand

остановиться.etymology: Formed by adding the reflexive-intransitive postfix -ся to остановить ('to bring to a standstill'): 'to come to a halt, stop moving, or stay at an inn/hotel'.

history.meaning: to stop, come to a halt (intransitive)

остаток.etymology: Formed from the stem of остаться / оставаться ('to remain, be left over', from prefix о- + стать 'to stand, become', Proto-Slavic *stati) + nominal suffix -ток.

остаться.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic остатися ('to remain behind, stay'), formed from о- + стать ('to stand, become', Proto-Slavic *stati) + the reflexive suffix -ся.
остаться.notes: Conjugates with the nasal-origin stem *остан-*: *я останусь, ты останешься, они останутся*.

остеохондропатия.etymology: International medical term from New Latin osteochondropathia, compounded from Ancient Greek ὀστέον (ostéon, 'bone') + χόνδρος (khóndros, 'cartilage, gristle') + -πάθεια (-pátheia, 'disease, disorder', from πάθος páthos 'suffering').

осторожнее.etymology: Formed with the comparative suffix -ее from осторожный ('careful, cautious, watchful'), derived from Old East Slavic осторого ('guarding, watchfulness around oneself'), built on о- ('around') + сторожить ('to guard, watch over', Proto-Slavic *storžiti, cognate with стража).
осторожнее.notes: Frequently used as a polite warning: Пожалуйста, осторожнее! ('Please be more careful!').

осторожно.etymology: Adverb formed from the short neuter of осторожный ('careful, cautious, wary'), built on Old Russian осторога ('watchfulness, guard, caution'), from the native East Slavic root сторож- (Proto-Slavic *storžь 'watchman, guard', from *stergti 'to guard, watch over', modern Russian стеречь).

осторожность.etymology: Abstract noun in -ость from осторожный ('cautious, careful'), derived from остеречь / сторожить ('to guard, watch over'), from Proto-Slavic *storgti ('to guard, watch').

осторожный.etymology: Formed with prefix о- and adjectival suffix -ный from сторож ('guard, watchman') / сторожить ('to watch over, guard'), from Proto-Slavic *storgti ('to watch, guard', showing East Slavic pleophony -оро-): literally 'keeping watch all around, circumspect, careful'.

остров.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic островъ ('island'), from Proto-Slavic *ostrovъ, formed from prefix *ob- ('around') + *strovъ ('current, stream', ablaut derivative of *struja 'stream', PIE *srew- 'to flow'), literally 'land flowed around by water'.

острота.etymology: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ostrota, abstract noun formed from острый ('sharp, poignant, spicy', from Proto-Slavic *ostrъ, PIE *h₂ek̂-ro- 'sharp') + abstract quality suffix -ота.

острый.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic острыи ('sharp, pointed, keen'), from Proto-Slavic *ostrъ, continuing the ancient Proto-Indo-European root *h₂eḱ- ('sharp, pointed'), cognate with Latin ācer ('sharp, keen'), Ancient Greek ἄκρος ('topmost, pointed'), and English edge.

остывать.etymology: Formed as the imperfective of остыть / остынуть ('to cool down, lose heat'), from о- + стыть ('to grow cold, congeal', Proto-Slavic *styti, from the same root as студёный 'icy cold' and стужа 'hard frost').

остыть.etymology: Prefixed perfective verb formed from о- + стыть ('to grow cold, chill, freeze'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *styti (*stynǫti, 'to cool down, freeze'), from the same root as стужа ('bitter cold') and студёный ('icy cold').

history.meaning: to cool down, go cold (literally or emotionally)

осьминог.etymology: Compound noun formed from осьми- (combining/genitive form of archaic осемь 'eight', from Proto-Slavic *osmь) + нога ('leg, foot', Proto-Slavic *noga), created as a loan translation of Ancient Greek ὀκτάπους ('eight-footed').

осёл.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic осьлъ, from Proto-Slavic *osьlъ, an early borrowing from Gothic asilus ('donkey'), which was itself borrowed from Latin asellus ('little donkey', diminutive of asinus).

от.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic отъ ('away from, from'), from Proto-Slavic *otъ, cognate with Lithuanian at- / ata- ('away, back') and Sanskrit áti ('beyond, past').
от.notes: Always governs the genitive case: ключ от комнаты ('key to/from the room'), далеко от вокзала ('far from the station').

отбивать.etymology: Imperfective of отбить ('to beat back, repel; to pound/tenderize meat'), formed from от- ('off, back, away') + бивать, the iterative stem of бить ('to beat, strike', inherited from Old East Slavic бити, Proto-Slavic *biti).

history.meaning: to beat back, repel; to tenderize (meat)

отбирать.etymology: Imperfective verb formed from prefix от- ('away from') + -бирать (iterative stem of брать 'to take', from Proto-Slavic *birati / *bьrati, PIE *bʰer- 'to carry, take').

history.meaning: to take away, to pick out

отбить.etymology: Perfective verb formed from prefix от- ('away, back, off') + бить ('to beat, strike', from Old East Slavic бити, Proto-Slavic *biti); the culinary sense 'to tenderize' refers to pounding meat with a mallet.

отблагодарить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix от- (indicating reciprocation or repayment) + благодарить ('to thank', from Old Church Slavonic благодарити, a calque of Greek εὐχαριστεῖν from благо 'good' + даръ 'gift').

отбой.etymology: Deverbal noun formed with o-grade root vocalism (-бой) from отбить ('to beat off, repel; to beat a signal on a drum or bell', from prefix от- + бить, Proto-Slavic *biti).

history.meaning: to beat off; to sound a signal

отборный.etymology: Adjective formed from отбор ('selection, picking out', deverbal noun from отобрать / отбирать 'to select, pick out', from от- + брать) + adjectival suffix -ный.

отбороздить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with completive prefix от- ('to finish doing') + бороздить ('to furrow; figuratively to plough the seas', derived from борозда 'furrow', from Proto-Slavic *borzda).

отвалить.etymology: Formed with prefix от- ('away') from валить ('to roll, topple, throng'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *valiti ('to roll, tumble'); in colloquial speech 'to move away, back off'.

history.meaning: to roll away; (colloq.) to back off

отвар.etymology: Deverbal noun formed by zero-suffixation from отварить ('to boil, decoct'), from prefix от- + варить ('to boil, cook', from Old East Slavic варити, Proto-Slavic *variti).

отведать.etymology: Formed with prefix от- from ведать ('to know, experience'), inherited from Old East Slavic вѣдати, from Proto-Slavic *vědati ('to know'), shifting from 'to find out by trying' to 'to taste, sample'.

отвезти.etymology: Prefixed perfective verb formed from от- ('away, to a destination') + везти ('to transport, convey by vehicle'), inherited from Old East Slavic везти, from Proto-Slavic *vezti, from Proto-Indo-European *weǵʰ- ('to convey in a vehicle'; cognate with English wagon, way, and Latin vehere).

history.meaning: to drive, take (someone/something somewhere by vehicle)

отвергать.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic отъвръгати ('to cast away, reject'), imperfective of отъврѣщи, from Proto-Slavic *otъ-vьrgti ('to throw away'), from *vьrgti ('to throw').

отвернуться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of отвернуть ('to turn away, unscrew'), formed with prefix от- ('away') from вернуть ('to turn'), from Proto-Slavic *vьrtěti ('to turn').

отвести.etymology: Formed with prefix от- ('away') from вести ('to lead'), inherited from Old East Slavic вести (веду), from Proto-Slavic *vesti ('to lead').

ответ.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic отъвѣтъ ('answer, reply, counsel, account'), from Proto-Slavic *otъvětъ, formed from *otъ- ('back, in return') + *větъ ('speech, counsel, declaration'; compare совет 'advice, council' and привет 'greeting').

ответить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic отъвѣтити, from Proto-Slavic *otъvětiti ('to answer, reply'), formed from the prefix *otъ- ('back, in return') and *větiti ('to speak solemnly, counsel, address', from *větъ 'counsel, pact', preserved in совет 'advice, council' and привет 'greeting').

ответный.etymology: Relational adjective formed with the suffix -ный from ответ ('answer, reply, response'), which derives from ответить ('to answer', built from от- 'back' + Old East Slavic вѣтъ 'counsel, speech, word', Proto-Slavic *větъ).

ответственность.etymology: Abstract noun formed with the suffix -ость from ответственный ('responsible, accountable, answerable'), derived from ответ ('answer, reply; account', from ответить 'to answer', Proto-Slavic *otъvětъ). Coined in the late 18th century (recorded from 1789 by Karamzin) as a semantic calque of French responsabilité and German Verantwortung ('being answerable for').

ответственный.etymology: Adjective formed from ответственность / ответствовать ('to answer for, be responsible'), derived from ответ ('answer, reply'), from Proto-Slavic *otъ-větъ ('reply, counsel').

отвечать.etymology: Imperfective partner of ответить ('to answer, reply'), inherited (with Church Slavonic ч < *tj) from Old East Slavic отъвѣчати / отъвѣщати, formed from prefix от- ('back, in return') + вѣтъ ('counsel, speech, pact', from Proto-Slavic *větъ, preserved in совет 'advice, council' and привет 'greeting').

history.meaning: to answer, reply; to be responsible for

отвлекать.etymology: Imperfective verb (showing Church Slavonic non-pleophonic vocalism -влек-) formed with prefix от- ('away') + влекать (iterative of влечь 'to draw, pull', from Old Church Slavonic влѣщи, Proto-Slavic *velkti), literally 'to draw away'.

отвлекаться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective verb formed from отвлекать ('to distract, draw away', from от- + влекать, Proto-Slavic *velkti) + reflexive particle -ся.

отвлечь.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix от- ('away') + влечь ('to draw, drag', borrowed from Old Church Slavonic влѣщи, from Proto-Slavic *velkti; compare native East Slavic волочь), literally 'to pull one's attention away'.

отвод.etymology: Deverbal noun from отводить / отвести ('to lead away, divert, reject'), formed from prefix от- ('away') + водить ('to lead', from Proto-Slavic *voditi).

отводить.etymology: Imperfective verb formed from prefix от- ('away') + водить ('to lead, conduct', iterative of вести, from Old East Slavic водити, Proto-Slavic *voditi).

history.meaning: to take, lead away; to deflect

отвратительно.etymology: Adverb from отвратительный ('disgusting, repulsive'), derived from отвратить ('to turn away, avert, repel'), an Old Church Slavonicism from Proto-Slavic *otъ-vortiti ('to turn away').

отвратительный.etymology: Adjective derived from отвратить ('to turn away, avert, repel', a Church Slavonicism with non-pleophonic -врат- from Proto-Slavic *vortiti) + suffix -тельный, originally meaning 'causing one to turn away in revulsion'.

отвращение.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic отъвращение ('turning away, aversion, revulsion'), verbal noun from отъвратити ('to turn away, avert', from prefix отъ- + вратити, Proto-Slavic *vortiti).

отвязаться.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed from отвязать ('to untie, unbind', from prefix от- 'away, un-' + вязать 'to tie, bind', Proto-Slavic *vęzati) + reflexive particle -ся.

history.meaning: to come untied; to leave someone alone

отвёртка.etymology: Formed in Russian from отвёртывать / отвернуть ('to unscrew, turn back', from от- 'away, un-' + вертеть 'to turn, twist') + the tool suffix -ка: literally 'an unscrewing or screw-turning tool'.

отговорить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix от- ('away from') + говорить ('to speak, talk', from Old East Slavic говорити, Proto-Slavic *govoriti), literally 'to talk someone away from an intention'.

отговорка.etymology: Noun in -ка formed from отговориться ('to talk one's way out of, make an excuse') / отговорить, from от- ('away') + говорить ('to speak', from Proto-Slavic *govoriti).

отгул.etymology: Deverbal noun formed by zero-suffixation from отгулять ('to take compensatory time off, finish strolling or celebrating'), from prefix от- + гулять ('to stroll, be off work, make merry').

отдавать.etymology: Imperfective counterpart of отдать ('to give back, return, hand over'), formed from the prefix от- ('away, back') and давать ('to give', iterative of дать, from Proto-Slavic *davati, PIE *deh₃- 'to give').

history.meaning: to hand over, give back, return

отдать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic отъдати ('to give back, hand over'), from Proto-Slavic *otъdati, combining the prefix *otъ- ('away, back') with *dati ('to give').

отдача.etymology: Noun formed from отдать / отдавать ('to give back, return', from prefix от- + дать 'to give', Proto-Slavic *dati) + archaic nominal suffix -ча (from Proto-Slavic *-dādja).

отдел.etymology: Formed as a prefixal-stem noun from отделить ('to separate off, allocate a section', from от- 'off, from' + делить 'to divide, share', Proto-Slavic *děliti): 'a distinct section, division, or department'.

отделаться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of отделать ('to finish off'), formed with prefix от- ('away, off') from делать ('to do, make'), from Proto-Slavic *dělati, acquiring the sense 'to rid oneself of, get off lightly'.

history.meaning: to get off, get away with

отделение.etymology: Verbal noun formed from отделить ('to separate, divide off', from prefix от- + делить 'to divide, share', Proto-Slavic *děliti) + suffix -ение.

отделить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix от- ('away, off') + делить ('to divide, share', from Old East Slavic дѣлити, Proto-Slavic *děliti, derived from *dělъ 'part, share').

отдельно.etymology: Adverb formed from отдельный ('separate'), derived from отделить ('to separate, divide off'), from от- ('away') + делить ('to divide', from Proto-Slavic *děliti).

отдельный.etymology: Adjective formed with -ный from отделить / отдел ('separation, division'), from prefix от- ('away') + делить ('to divide, part'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *děliti.

отдохнуть.etymology: Inherited from East Slavic отъдъхнути, formed from от- ('off, back') + дохнуть ('to draw breath', Proto-Slavic *dъxnǫti, from the root of дух 'breath, spirit' and дышать 'to breathe'): literally 'to catch one's breath after exertion', hence 'to rest'.

history.meaning: to rest, take a break, holiday

отдых.etymology: Deverbal noun formed by zero-suffixation from отдыхать / отдохнуть ('to rest, catch one's breath'), from prefix от- + дыхать ('to breathe', from Proto-Slavic *dyxati, root *dъx- / *dux- 'breath').

отдыхать.etymology: Imperfective of отдохнуть ('to rest, catch one's breath'), formed from the prefix от- ('away, relief') + the Slavic root *dux- / *dyx- / *dъx- ('breath, breathe'; compare дышать 'to breathe' and дух 'breath, spirit'): literally 'to breathe out and recover one's breath after exertion'.

history.meaning: to catch one's breath → to rest

отель.etymology: Borrowed in the 19th century from French hôtel ('mansion, hotel'), from Old French hostel ('lodging, inn'), which goes back to Medieval Latin hospitāle ('guest house'), from Latin hospes ('host, guest').

отец.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic отьць (and Old Church Slavonic отьць, vocative отче), from Proto-Slavic *otьcь ('father'), formed with the affectionate/diminutive suffix *-ьcь from *otъ ('father'), from Proto-Indo-European nursery word *átta ('daddy, father'; compare Ancient Greek ἄττα, Latin atta, Gothic atta, and Hittite attas).

отзыв.etymology: Formed as a zero-suffixed noun from отзывать / отозвать ('to call back; to respond to a call'), from от- ('back, in response') + звать / -зывать ('to call'). From 'an answering call or echo' it developed the sense of a spoken or written response, review, or testimonial.

отказ.etymology: Deverbal noun from отказать ('to refuse, renounce'), formed from prefix от- ('away') + казать ('to say, declare, show', from Proto-Slavic *kazati).

отказать.etymology: Inherited from Old Russian отказати ('to answer back, renounce, refuse'), formed with prefix от- ('away, back') from казать ('to say, show', from Proto-Slavic *kazati).

history.meaning: to refuse, to turn down; to fail (of brakes/organs)

отказаться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of отказать ('to refuse, renounce'), formed from от- ('away') + казать ('to say, declare', Proto-Slavic *kazati) + -ся.

отказываться.etymology: Formed as the imperfective reflexive of отказаться ('to refuse, decline, give up'), from от- ('away from') + казать ('to show, declare, speak', Proto-Slavic *kazati) + -ся: literally 'to speak oneself away from an offer or claim'.
отказываться.notes: Takes от + genitive for a noun (отказываться от помощи 'to decline help') or an infinitive.

откачивать.etymology: Secondary imperfective verb formed from откачать ('to pump out; colloquially to resuscitate, originally by rocking or pumping water out of a drowning victim'), from prefix от- + качать ('to rock, pump', Proto-Slavic *kačati) + -ивать.

откладывать.etymology: Secondary imperfective verb formed from prefix от- ('aside, away') + кладывать (frequentative of класть 'to lay, put', from Proto-Slavic *klasti), serving as the imperfective partner of отложить.

history.meaning: to put aside, postpone; to save

откладываться.etymology: Reflexive and passive verb formed from откладывать ('to put aside, postpone', from от- + класть, Proto-Slavic *klasti) + reflexive particle -ся.

history.meaning: to be postponed; to be deposited

отклеить.etymology: Formed with prefix от- ('away, off') from клеить ('to glue, stick'), derived from клей ('glue'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *kъlejь ('gum, resin, glue').

отключать.etymology: Secondary imperfective of отключить ('to disconnect, switch off, cut off'), formed from separative prefix от- ('away from, off') + stem of ключ ('key, hook, latch, switch'), from Proto-Slavic *kľučь ('hook, wooden bolt'), cognate with Latin clāvis ('key') from Proto-Indo-European *kleh₂u- ('hook, peg').

history.meaning: to unhook, disconnect, shut off supply

отключать.notes: While выключать means flipping a room switch or appliance off, отключать highlights disconnecting a line, breaker, or building utility (отключать электричество, отключать отопление).

отключить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with the prefix от- ('off, away, disconnecting') and ключить (built on ключ 'key, switch', from Proto-Slavic *kľučь 'hook, key, bolt'), on the model of включить ('to switch on') and выключить ('to switch off'). Means 'to disconnect, cut off (power, water, or a phone), switch off'.

history.meaning: to disconnect, cut off, switch off

отключиться.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed from отключить ('to disconnect, switch off', coined by prefix substitution after включить 'to switch on, include', from ключ 'key', Proto-Slavic *kľučь) + reflexive particle -ся.

history.meaning: to disconnect, turn off, pass out

отключка.etymology: Colloquial deverbal noun formed from отключиться ('to switch off; colloquially to black out, lose consciousness', from от- + ключить + -ся) + nominal suffix -ка.

открутить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix от- ('off, away') + крутить ('to twist, turn', from Old East Slavic крутити, Proto-Slavic *krǫtiti).

открывать.etymology: Imperfective of открыть ('to uncover, open'), formed from the prefix от- ('away, off') + крыть ('to cover, roof', Proto-Slavic *kryti) + imperfective -вать: literally 'to take the cover off'.

открываться.etymology: Reflexive and intransitive counterpart of открывать ('to open'), formed from открыть ('to uncover, open') + imperfective suffix -ва- + reflexive marker -ся.

history.meaning: to open (by itself), come open, open for business

открытие.etymology: Formed with the verbal-noun suffix -ие from открыть ('to open, uncover, discover', from от- 'away, off' + крыть 'to cover'): both 'an opening ceremony' and 'a discovery' (parallel to French découverte and English discovery, literally 'an uncovering').

открытка.etymology: Coined in late nineteenth-century Russian as a colloquial ellipsis of открытое письмо ('open, unsealed letter', calquing German offener Brief / Postkarte) with the suffix -ка.

открыто.etymology: Adverb formed from открытый ('open, frank'), past passive participle of открыть ('to open, uncover'), from от- ('away, un-') + крыть ('to cover', from Proto-Slavic *kryti).

открытый.etymology: Originally the past passive participle of открыть ('to uncover, open', from от- 'off' + крыть 'to cover', Proto-Slavic *kryti), fully lexicalized as the everyday adjective meaning 'open, uncovered, public'.

открыть.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic отъкрыти ('to uncover, reveal, open'), formed from the privative/separative prefix от- ('away, off') + крыть ('to cover', from Proto-Slavic *kryti): literally 'to take the cover off', which became the general Russian verb 'to open' (a door, window, bottle, or book) and 'to discover'.

открыться.etymology: Formed in Russian from открыть ('to open, uncover') + the reflexive/intransitive suffix -ся: 'to open by itself, swing open, or open for business'.

откуда.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic отъкуда, formed from the ablative prefix от- ('from') + куда ('where, whither', Proto-Slavic *kǫda, built on the interrogative stem *k-): 'from where?, whence?, how come?'.

откусить.etymology: Perfective verb formed from prefix от- ('off, away from') + кусить ('to bite', Proto-Slavic *kǫsiti 'to bite, tear off a piece', related to *kǫsъ 'morsel, piece'). In Russian the same Proto-Slavic root gave кусок ('piece, slice'), кусочек ('little bite'), and вкус ('taste, flavour', originally 'a tasting bite').

history.meaning: to bite → to bite off a piece
to take a bite, bite off

отлежать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix от- (indicating numbness or injury caused by prolonged action) + лежать ('to lie', from Old East Slavic лежати, Proto-Slavic *ležati).

history.meaning: to make numb by lying on

отлежаться.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed with prefix от- (indicating recovery by completing an action) + лежать ('to lie', from Proto-Slavic *ležati) + reflexive particle -ся.

history.meaning: to rest up in bed, recover by lying down

отличать.etymology: Imperfective verb derived from отличить ('to distinguish, single out'), from prefix от- ('apart, out') + личить ('to mark by appearance', from лик / лицо 'face, appearance', Proto-Slavic *likъ).

отличаться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective verb formed from отличать ('to distinguish, tell apart', from от- + лик 'face, feature') + reflexive particle -ся.

отличить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic отъличити ('to distinguish, make distinct'), formed from prefix от- ('apart, away') + личити (from лик / лицо 'face, appearance', Proto-Slavic *likъ).

отличиться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of отличить ('to distinguish, single out'), derived from отличный / сличить, built on лик / лицо ('face, appearance, mark'), from Proto-Slavic *likъ.

отличник.etymology: Formed from отличный ('excellent, distinguished', from отличие 'distinction', from отличить) + agent suffix -ник; popularized in Soviet schools and workplaces for someone earning the highest grade («отлично»).

отлично.etymology: Adverb and predicate form of отличный ('excellent, outstanding', originally 'distinct, standing apart from the ordinary'), formed from отличить ('to distinguish', from от- 'apart from' + лик / лицо 'face, appearance'): literally 'in a way that stands out by its face or mark'.

отличный.etymology: Derived from отличить ('to distinguish, set apart by face or mark', built on от- 'apart from' + лик / лицо 'face, appearance') with the suffix -ный: originally 'distinct, standing out from the rest', which developed into 'outstanding, excellent'.

отложить.etymology: Formed with prefix от- ('aside, away') from ложить ('to lay, put'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *ložiti (causative of *ležati 'to lie').

history.meaning: to put aside, to put down; to postpone

отломиться.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed from отломить ('to break off', from prefix от- 'off' + ломить 'to break', Proto-Slavic *lomiti) + reflexive particle -ся; colloquially 'for a share/perquisite to come one's way'.

history.meaning: to break off; (colloq.) to come one's way

отлучаться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective verb formed from отлучать ('to separate, exclude', borrowed from Old Church Slavonic отълучати, from prefix отъ- + лучити 'to separate', Proto-Slavic *lučiti) + -ся.

отлучиться.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed from отлучить ('to separate, exclude', from Old Church Slavonic отълучити, Proto-Slavic *otъlučiti) + reflexive particle -ся ('to absent oneself briefly').

history.meaning: to step away, leave for a while

отмахнуться.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed from от- ('away') + махнуть ('to wave, flap once', semelfactive of махать 'to wave', Proto-Slavic *maxati) + -ся: literally 'to wave one's hand to brush away a fly or an unwanted thought/question'.

отменить.etymology: Formed from от- ('away, back') + менить ('to change, exchange', Proto-Slavic *měniti, from мена 'exchange, change'): literally 'to change back, revoke', hence 'to cancel, abolish, call off'.

history.stage: Old Church Slavonic / Old East Slavic

отмениться.etymology: Reflexive and passive perfective verb formed from отменить ('to cancel, revoke, abolish', from prefix от- + менить 'to change, exchange', from мена 'exchange', Proto-Slavic *měna) + -ся.

отменять.etymology: Imperfective verb formed from prefix от- ('away, back') + менять ('to change, exchange', from Old East Slavic мѣняти, Proto-Slavic *měňati, derived from *měna 'exchange').

отменяться.etymology: Reflexive/passive form in -ся of отменять ('to cancel, abolish, revoke'), imperfective of отменить, formed from prefix от- ('away') + мена / менить ('to change, exchange', Proto-Slavic *měniti).

отмерить.etymology: Formed with the prefix от- ('off from a whole') + мерить ('to measure'), derived from мера ('measure', from Old East Slavic мѣра and Proto-Slavic *měra).

отметить.etymology: Prefixed perfective verb formed from от- ('off') + метить ('to mark, aim at'), derived from мета ('mark, target, sign', Old East Slavic мѣта, Proto-Slavic *měta). From 'to mark off on a list or calendar' developed the senses 'to note, mention' and 'to celebrate (a holiday, birthday, or milestone)'.

history.meaning: to mark off, note; to celebrate

отмечать.etymology: Imperfective verb formed from отметить ('to mark, note; to celebrate'), from prefix от- + метить ('to mark, aim', from мета 'mark, sign, target', Proto-Slavic *měta); 'to celebrate' evolved from 'to mark a special date'.

отнести.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic отънести ('to carry away, take to a place'), formed from the prefix от- ('away, to a destination') + нести ('to carry on foot', from Proto-Slavic *nesti, PIE *h₁neḱ-).

отнестись.etymology: Reflexive form in -сь of отнести ('to carry away, refer, attribute'), formed with prefix от- from нести ('to carry'), from Proto-Slavic *nesti; the sense 'to relate to, treat' is a semantic calque on German sich verhalten / sich beziehen.

относиться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of относить ('to carry away, refer'), imperfective of отнестись; the sense 'to relate to, treat' is a semantic calque on German sich beziehen / sich verhalten, built on нести ('to carry', Proto-Slavic *nesti).

history.meaning: to treat, to relate to; to belong to

отношение.etymology: Verbal noun formed from относить / отнести ('to carry away; to refer, relate') and относиться ('to relate to, treat'), a compound of от- ('from, away') + носить ('to carry'). In the 18th century it calqued French relation and German Verhältnis ('relation, attitude; in plural, interpersonal relationships').

отныне.etymology: Formed by univerbation of the Old East Slavic and Old Church Slavonic prepositional phrase отъ нынѣ ('from now'), from preposition от ('from', Proto-Slavic *otъ) + ныне ('now', Proto-Slavic *nyně).

отобрать.etymology: Prefixed perfective verb formed from ото- (variant of от- 'away from' before the cluster бр-) + брать ('to take', inherited from Old East Slavic бьрати, Proto-Slavic *bьrati). Depending on context, it means either 'to take away by force, confiscate' or 'to select, pick out from a group'.

history.meaning: to take away or pick out
to take away, confiscate; to select

отогнать.etymology: Formed with prefix ото- ('away') from гнать ('to drive, chase'), inherited from Old East Slavic гънати, from Proto-Slavic *gъnati ('to drive, pursue').

отодвинуть.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix ото- ('away, aside', variant of от- before consonant clusters) + двинуть ('to move, shift', semelfactive of двигать, from Proto-Slavic *dvignǫti).

отойти.etymology: Formed from ото- (variant of от- 'away from' before clusters) + идти ('to go, walk', Proto-Slavic *iti): 'to walk away, step back, move a short distance off'.

history.meaning: to step away, move back, come loose

отойти.notes: Past tense uses the suppletive root шед-/шл-: отошёл, отошла, отошли.

отомстить.etymology: Perfective counterpart of мстить ('to take vengeance, avenge'), inherited from Old East Slavic отъмьстити, formed from the prefix от- / ото- ('back, in return') and мьстити ('to avenge'), a denominative verb from мьсть / месть ('vengeance, retribution'), from Proto-Slavic *mьstь (originally 'recompense, exchange, return payment', cognate with Sanskrit mithás 'mutually, alternately' and Gothic maipms 'gift').

history.meaning: retribution, payback → to pay back, avenge
to take revenge, get back at (+ dat.)

отопление.etymology: Verbal noun formed from отопить ('to heat a building or room'), built from prefix о- ('around, throughout') + топить ('to stoke a stove, heat', the o-grade causative *topiti of the Proto-Slavic heat root *tep-, seen in тёплый 'warm' and тепло 'warmth').

history.meaning: to make warm, heat a stove
to heat a building → heating system, heating

оторванный.etymology: Past passive participle of оторвать ('to tear off, rip away'), formed from prefix от- / ото- ('off, away') + рвать ('to tear', from Proto-Slavic *rъvati).

оторвать.etymology: Formed with prefix ото- ('away, off') from рвать ('to tear, pluck'), inherited from Old East Slavic ръвати, from Proto-Slavic *rъvati ('to tear, pull out').

отпереть.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic отъперети ('to unbar, unlock'), formed from prefix от- ('un-, away') + переть ('to press, prop, bar', from Proto-Slavic *perti, PIE *per-); contrast запереть ('to lock, bar').

отпилить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix от- ('off, away') + пилить ('to saw', derived from пила 'saw', Proto-Slavic *pila, an early borrowing from Germanic *fīlō 'file, saw').

отпирать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic отъпирати ('to unbar, unlock'), from Proto-Slavic *otъpirati, iterative-imperfective counterpart of *otъperti ('to draw back a bar, unbolt'), built from *otъ- ('away') + *perti ('to press, prop with a wooden beam', from Proto-Indo-European *per- / *sper- 'beam, prop').
отпирать.notes: Preserves the ancient Slavic vowel alternation -пер- / -пир- (отпереть — отпирать) and pairs directly with запирать ('to lock with a key or bolt').

отплатить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix от- ('back, in return') + платить ('to pay', from Old East Slavic платити, Proto-Slavic *platiti, originally 'to pay with pieces of linen cloth *platъ').

отползать.etymology: Imperfective verb formed with prefix от- ('away') + ползать ('to crawl, creep', iterative of ползти, from Old East Slavic пълзати, Proto-Slavic *pьlzati).

отправитель.etymology: Agent noun formed with the suffix -тель from отправить ('to send off, dispatch'), built on prefix от- ('away, off') + править ('to direct, steer, send', from Proto-Slavic *praviti).

history.meaning: to dispatch, send → sender (on a letter or parcel)

отправить.etymology: Formed from the prefix от- ('away') + править ('to direct, steer, set straight', from правый 'right, straight', Proto-Slavic *pravъ): literally 'to direct or dispatch on its way'.

отправиться.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed from отправить ('to send, dispatch, direct', from prefix от- + править 'to direct, steer', from правый 'straight, right', Proto-Slavic *praviti) + -ся ('to direct oneself, set off').

отправлять.etymology: Imperfective verb formed from отправить ('to send, dispatch', from prefix от- + править 'to direct, steer', Proto-Slavic *praviti) + imperfective suffix -ять.

отправляться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective verb formed from отправлять ('to send, dispatch', from от- + править) + reflexive particle -ся.

отпраздновать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with completive prefix от- + праздновать ('to celebrate', derived from праздник 'holiday' / праздный 'festive, idle', borrowed from Old Church Slavonic праздньствовати, from Proto-Slavic *porzdьnъ 'empty, idle').

отпроситься.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed with prefix от- ('away, off') + просить ('to ask, request', from Old East Slavic просити, Proto-Slavic *prositi) + reflexive particle -ся, literally 'to ask oneself away from duty'.

history.meaning: to ask for time off, ask permission to leave

отпуск.etymology: Deverbal noun formed by zero-suffixation from отпустить ('to let go, release, grant leave', from prefix от- + пустить 'to let go', Old East Slavic отъпустити, Proto-Slavic *pustiti).

отпускать.etymology: Imperfective of отпустить ('to let go, release, allow to leave'), formed from от- ('away') + пускать ('to let go, release', inherited from Old East Slavic пускати, Proto-Slavic *puskati).

отпустить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic отъпустити ('to let go, release, remit'), formed from the prefix от- ('away, off') and пустить ('to let go, allow, release', from Proto-Slavic *pustiti, originally 'to make empty/free', from *pustъ 'empty, free', Russian пустой).

отрабатывать.etymology: Secondary imperfective verb formed from отработать ('to work off a debt or shift; to practice to perfection'), from prefix от- + работать ('to work', from работа, Proto-Slavic *orbota) + suffix -ывать.

отработать.etymology: Formed with prefix от- ('completing a duty or paying back') from работать ('to work'), derived from работа ('work'), from Proto-Slavic *orbota.

history.meaning: to work off (a debt), to put in (hours); to practice

отравить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic отравити ('to poison'), originally formed from prefix о- + травити ('to consume, waste, poison with herbs', later reanalyzed with prefix от-), from трава ('grass, herb, potion', Proto-Slavic *trava, related to *truti 'to consume, poison').

отравиться.etymology: Perfective reflexive verb formed from отравить ('to poison'), built from о- + травить ('to poison; originally to graze cattle on grass, consume with herbs/potions'), a denominative verb from трава ('grass, herb, medicinal or poisonous plant', inherited from Old East Slavic трава, Proto-Slavic *trava, from *truti 'to consume, wear away').

history.meaning: grass, herb → to feed on herbs / treat with herbal poison
to get poisoned, suffer food poisoning

отравление.etymology: Verbal noun formed from отравить ('to poison', Old East Slavic отравити) + abstract action suffix -ение.

отразить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix от- ('back, off') + разить ('to strike, smite', from Old East Slavic разити, Proto-Slavic *raziti); originally 'to beat back an attack', extended in the 18th century to 'to reflect light or represent' as a semantic calque of Latin reflectere / French réfléchir.

history.meaning: to repel; to reflect; to include in a report

отрастить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix от- ('out, forth') + растить ('to grow, cultivate', causative verb with Church Slavonic vocalism ра- from Proto-Slavic *orstiti, from *orsti 'to grow').

отреагировать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with Russian perfectivizing prefix от- + реагировать ('to react'), borrowed via German reagieren from Medieval Latin reagere ('to act back, react', from re- 'back' + agere 'to do, act').

отрезать.etymology: Formed from the prefix от- ('off, away') and резать ('to cut, slice', from Old East Slavic рѣзати, Proto-Slavic *rězati). Stress distinguishes aspect: perfective **отрезать** ('to cut off, slice off') vs. imperfective **отрезать**.

отречься.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed from от- ('away from') + the Slavic verb речь ('to speak, say, declare', Old East Slavic рещи, Old Church Slavonic решти, Proto-Slavic *rekti) + -ся: literally 'to speak oneself away from, disavow, renounce (a throne, faith, or person)'.

history.meaning: to declare oneself apart from, renounce

history.stage: Old East Slavic / Old Church Slavonic

отрицание.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic отърицание ('renunciation, denial, negation'), verbal noun from отърицати, iterative of отърещи ('to say no, renounce', with third palatalization *k > *c from *rekti 'to speak').

отрицать.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic отърицати ('to renounce, repudiate, deny'), imperfective of отърещи ('to renounce, refuse'), from prefix отъ- ('away') + -рицати (iterative of рещи 'to say, speak', Proto-Slavic *rekti).

отрубить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix от- ('off, away') + рубить ('to chop, hew', from Old East Slavic рубити, Proto-Slavic *rǫbiti, from *rǫbъ 'cut, edge').

отрывать.etymology: Secondary imperfective verb formed from оторвать ('to tear off, pull away'), from prefix от- ('off, away') + рывать (iterative stem of рвать 'to tear', from Proto-Slavic *rъvati).

отрываться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective verb formed from отрывать ('to tear off, detach', from от- + рвать, Proto-Slavic *rъvati) + reflexive particle -ся; colloquially extended to 'to cut loose, have a wild time'.

history.meaning: to break away, tear loose; (colloq.) to party hard

отряд.etymology: Deverbal noun formed by zero-suffixation from отрядить ('to detach, detail, appoint a group for a mission'), from prefix от- ('off, out') + рядить ('to arrange, equip, order', from ряд 'row, order', Proto-Slavic *rędъ).

отсрочка.etymology: Deverbal noun formed from отсрочить ('to postpone, defer, extend a deadline', from prefix от- + срок 'appointed time, deadline', Old East Slavic сърокъ, Proto-Slavic *sъrokъ) + nominal suffix -ка.

отставать.etymology: Imperfective of отстать ('to fall behind, come off'), formed with prefix от- ('away, behind') from ставать / стать ('to stand, become'), from Proto-Slavic *stati.

отставка.etymology: Deverbal noun formed from отставить ('to set aside; to dismiss or discharge from state or military service', from prefix от- + ставить 'to place, set', Proto-Slavic *staviti) + suffix -ка.

history.meaning: to set aside, discharge from service

отстаивать.etymology: Secondary imperfective verb formed from отстоять ('to defend, stand one's ground for'), from prefix от- + стоять ('to stand', Proto-Slavic *stojati) + imperfective suffix -ивать.

отстать.etymology: Prefixed perfective verb formed from от- ('away from, behind') + стать ('to stand, come to a stop, become', inherited from Old East Slavic стати, Proto-Slavic *stati): literally 'to stand back, lag behind', and figuratively 'to stop pestering someone, leave alone'.

history.meaning: to step back, fall behind, desist
to fall behind; to leave alone

отстать.notes: In the imperative, Отстань! (plural/formal Отстаньте!) is the standard everyday way to say 'Leave me alone!' or 'Back off!'.

отстегнуть.etymology: Perfective semelfactive verb formed with prefix от- ('un-, off') + стегнуть ('to fasten, button, stitch', from Proto-Slavic *stegnǫti).

отстирать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix от- ('off, out') + стирать ('to wash laundry', originally iterative of стереть 'to rub off, wipe', from prefix съ- + тереть 'to rub', Proto-Slavic *terti).

отстоять.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix от- + стоять ('to stand', from Old East Slavic стояти, Proto-Slavic *stojati, PIE *stā-), literally 'to stand firm to the end in defense of something'.

history.meaning: to stand at a distance; to defend by standing

отстранить.etymology: Formed with the Church Slavonic root vocalism -стран- (corresponding to native East Slavic сторон- 'side') from от- ('away') + страна ('side', Old Church Slavonic страна, Proto-Slavic *storna): literally 'to push to the side, remove from a post or duty'.

history.meaning: to suspend (from duty), remove, push aside

отстранять.etymology: Imperfective verb formed from отстранить ('to push aside, remove from office'), a Church Slavonicism with non-pleophonic -стран- (compare native сторона 'side'), from prefix от- + страна ('side, region', Proto-Slavic *storna).

отступать.etymology: Imperfective verb formed with prefix от- ('back, away') + ступать ('to step, tread', from Old East Slavic ступати, Proto-Slavic *stǫpati).

отступить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix от- ('back, away') + ступить ('to step, tread', from Old East Slavic ступити, Proto-Slavic *stǫpiti).

history.meaning: to step back, retreat, back down

отсутствие.etymology: Formed on the Church Slavonic model as a loan translation of Latin absentia (from ab- 'away' + esse 'to be'), from prefix от- ('away') + суть ('they are', 3rd person plural of быти) + abstract suffix -ствие.

отсчитать.etymology: Formed with the prefix от- ('off, away from a whole') + считать ('to count'), built on Proto-Slavic *čitati: 'to count off, measure out by counting'.

отсчёт.etymology: Deverbal noun formed from отсчитать / отсчитывать ('to count off, count from a starting point'), from prefix от- + счёт ('count, reckoning', from Proto-Slavic *sъčetъ, root *čьt- 'to count, read').

отсюда.etymology: Formed in Russian from the ablative prefix от- ('from') + сюда ('here, hither', Old East Slavic сюда / сюды, built on the proximal demonstrative stem *sь 'this'): 'from here'.

оттенок.etymology: Formed with prefix от- and diminutive/nominal suffix -ок from тень ('shadow, shade'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *těnь ('shadow, shade'), as a semantic calque on French nuance.

оттуда.etymology: Formed in East Slavic from the ablative preposition от ('from') + туда ('thither, there', from Old East Slavic туду / туда, built on the distal demonstrative stem *t- 'that').

отужинать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with completive prefix от- + ужинать ('to have supper/dinner', from ужин 'evening meal, originally midday meal', derived from Old East Slavic югъ / угъ 'south, midday sun', Proto-Slavic *jugъ).

history.meaning: to dine, to finish having dinner

отфритюрить.etymology: Colloquial culinary coinage formed with Russian perfectivizing prefix от- + фритюр ('deep-frying fat', borrowed from French friture 'frying, deep-frying oil', from Latin frīctūra, from frīgere 'to fry') + verbal suffix -ить.

отходить.etymology: Formed with prefix от- ('away') from ходить ('to walk, go'), inherited from Old East Slavic ходити, from Proto-Slavic *xoditi.

отходы.etymology: Plural noun derived from отходить ('to move away, separate off during processing'), from prefix от- + ходить ('to go', Proto-Slavic *xoditi), denoting residual material or waste.

отцовский.etymology: Relational adjective formed from отцов ('father's', possessive adjective from отец 'father', Old East Slavic отьць, Proto-Slavic *otьcь) + adjectival suffix -ский.

отцовство.etymology: Abstract noun formed from отцов ('father's', from отец 'father', Proto-Slavic *otьcь) + abstract state suffix -ство.

отчаянно.etymology: Adverb derived from отчаянный ('desperate, reckless', originally past participle of отчаяться 'to lose hope, despair', borrowed from Old Church Slavonic отъчаяти 'to give up hope', from отъ- + чаяти 'to expect, hope', Proto-Slavic *čajati) + suffix -о.

отчество.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic отьчьство ('patronymic; father's estate or lineage'), formed from отьчь ('father's, paternal', from отьць 'father', Proto-Slavic *otьcь) + suffix -ьство.

отчислить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix от- ('off, away from') + числить ('to count, list on an official roster', from число 'number', Proto-Slavic *čislo), literally 'to strike someone's name off the rolls'.

history.meaning: to reckon, include on a roll
to expel, to dismiss, to deduct

отчитывать.etymology: Secondary imperfective verb formed from отчитать ('to finish reading; to lecture or reprimand someone severely, originally like reading out a formal reprimand'), from prefix от- + читать ('to read', Proto-Slavic *čitati).

отчитываться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective verb formed from отчитывать / отчитаться ('to give a formal account or reckoning', associated with отчёт 'report, account', from читать / считать 'to count, read') + reflexive particle -ся.

отчёт.etymology: Deverbal noun from отчитать / отсчитать ('to count out, reckon, give an accounting'), formed from от- ('out, off') + the Proto-Slavic root *čьt- ('to count, reckon, read', from *čisti, 1sg. *čьtǫ; compare считать 'to count' and читать 'to read').

rootFamily.gloss: to report back, give an account

отшить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix от- ('off, away') + шить ('to sew', from Old East Slavic шити, Proto-Slavic *šiti); literally 'to detach by unstitching or finish sewing', colloquially 'to brush off, reject'.

history.meaning: to sew off; (colloq.) to brush off, send packing

отъезд.etymology: Deverbal noun formed by zero-suffixation from отъехать / отъезжать ('to ride or drive away, depart'), from prefix от- ('away') + езда / ездить ('riding, driving', Proto-Slavic *ězdъ).

отъехать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix от- ('away, off') + ехать ('to go by vehicle, ride', from Old East Slavic ѣхати, Proto-Slavic *ěxati).

отыграть.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix от- ('back; to completion') + играть ('to play', from Old East Slavic играти, Proto-Slavic *jьgrati).

history.meaning: to win back; to finish playing

отыграться.etymology: Perfective reflexive formed with prefix от- ('back, in return') and -ся from играть ('to play'), from Proto-Slavic *jьgrati ('to play'), meaning 'to win back what was lost in play'.

history.meaning: to tie the score, recoup, fight back

отыгрываться.etymology: Imperfective of отыграться ('to win back, get even'), formed with suffix -ыва- from от- ('back') + играть ('to play', Proto-Slavic *jьgrati) + -ся.

history.meaning: to win back, to get even

офигеть.etymology: Colloquial slang perfective verb formed with prefix о- + фиг ('fig sign, nothing', euphemistic substitute for an obscene root, borrowed via Polish figa / German Feige from Latin fīcus 'fig') + inchoative suffix -еть.

офис.etymology: Borrowed from English office (first recorded in 19th-century Russian descriptions of British and American business, and generalized across everyday Russian in the late 20th century), from Old French office and Latin officium ('service, duty, post', from *opificium 'work-doing').

офицер.etymology: Borrowed in the late 17th / Petrine era via German Offizier from Middle French officier ('office-holder, military officer'), from Medieval Latin officiārius (from Latin officium 'duty, service, office').

history.meaning: holder of an office, military commander

официально.etymology: Adverbial form in -о of официальный ('official'), borrowed via German offiziell / French officiel or Polish oficjalny from Late Latin officiālis ('belonging to duty or office', from Latin officium 'service, duty, office').

официальный.etymology: Borrowed via Polish oficjalny or German offiziell / French officiel from Late Latin officiālis ('belonging to duty or magistracy, official'), derived from Latin officium ('duty, service, public office').

официант.etymology: Borrowed in the 18th–19th century via German Offiziant or Polish oficjant ('subordinate official, functionary, attendant') from Medieval Latin officiāns (genitive officiantis), present participle of officiāre ('to perform a duty or service'), from Latin officium ('service, duty, office'). In Russian, the word narrowed from a minor civil or church attendant to a restaurant waiter.

официантка.etymology: Feminine noun in -ка formed from официант ('waiter'), borrowed via German Offiziant (originally 'subordinate official, server at table or Mass') from Medieval Latin officiāns, officiantis (present participle of officiāre 'to perform a duty/service').

оформить.etymology: Formed in Russian from о- + форма ('form, official format, layout', borrowed via Polish forma and German Form from Latin fōrma 'shape, mold, form') + the verbal suffix -ить: literally 'to give proper form to, draw up or register officially'.

history.meaning: form → to formalize, register, draw up officially

оформлять.etymology: Imperfective partner of оформить ('to register officially, draw up paperwork, design'), formed with the imperfective suffix -ять from о- + форма ('form', from Latin fōrma).

history.meaning: to formalize, draw up → to process paperwork, register (impf)

morphemes.meaning: form (форма, with labial epenthesis м → мл)

ох.etymology: Primary expressive interjection inherited across East and West Slavic (compare Ukrainian ох, Polish och) and parallel to German ach / och, directly imitating a heavy sigh or groan of relief, fatigue, or dismay.

history.meaning: exclamation of sighing, dismay, or relief

охапка.etymology: Noun formed with prefix о- ('around') + dialectal хапать ('to grab, clasp in one's arms', from Proto-Slavic *xapati) + suffix -ка, literally 'as much as one can clasp in both arms'.

history.meaning: to embrace, clasp in one's arms

охватить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix о- ('around') + хватить ('to grasp, seize', from Old East Slavic хватити, Proto-Slavic *xvatiti).

охота.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic охота ('wish, desire, inclination; hunting'), formed with prefix о- from the root of хотеть ('to want, desire', Proto-Slavic *xotěti); 'hunting' developed from 'eager pursuit done for pleasure'.

охотник.etymology: Agent noun in -ник derived from охота ('wish, eagerness; hunting'), from хотеть ('to want, desire'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *xotěti ('to want').

охотно.etymology: Adverb formed from охотный ('willing, eager', derived from охота 'desire, inclination', from хотеть 'to want') + adverbial suffix -о.

охрана.etymology: Derived from охранить ('to guard, protect'), showing the South Slavic / Church Slavonic root vocalism -хран- (compare native East Slavic -хорон- in хоронить) from Proto-Slavic *xorniti ('to guard, keep safe') with the prefix о-.

охранник.etymology: Agent noun formed from охрана ('protection, guarding, security', deverbal noun from охранить / охранять) + agent suffix -ник.

охранять.etymology: Imperfective verb with Church Slavonic non-pleophonic vocalism -хран- (compare native хоронить / оборона), formed from prefix о- + хранити ('to guard, keep safe', Old Church Slavonic хранити, Proto-Slavic *xorniti).

охрипнуть.etymology: Inchoative perfective verb formed with prefix о- and suffix -ну-ть from the stem хрип- ('raspy, hoarse sound', Proto-Slavic *xripъ / *xripěti 'to rasp, wheeze, speak hoarsely'). Notice that in the past tense the suffix -ну- drops out after the consonant п, yielding masculine охрип, feminine охрипла.

оценивать.etymology: Secondary imperfective verb formed from оценить ('to value, appraise, rate'), from prefix о- + ценить ('to price, value', from цена 'price, value', Proto-Slavic *cěna) + imperfective suffix -ивать.

оценить.etymology: Prefixed perfective verb formed from о- + ценить ('to value, price, appreciate'), a denominative verb from цена ('price, value, worth', inherited from Old East Slavic цѣна, from Proto-Slavic *cěna, from PIE *kʷoyneh₂ 'price, recompense').

history.meaning: price, worth → to set a price on, value

оценка.etymology: Formed in Russian with the noun suffix -ка from оценить ('to set a price on, appraise, evaluate'), built on о- + цена ('price, value', Proto-Slavic *cěna): 'an appraisal, school grade, or rating'.

history.meaning: to value, rate -> valuation, rating, grade

очаг.etymology: Borrowed from a Turkic language (compare Tatar учак, Crimean Tatar ocaq, Turkish ocak 'hearth, fireplace'), from Proto-Turkic *ōčak ('hearth, fire pit'), derived from *ōt ('fire').

очаровать.etymology: Prefixed perfective verb formed from о- + чаровать ('to bewitch, cast a spell'), derived from чары ('magic spells, charms, sorcery', Old East Slavic чаръ, from Proto-Slavic *čarъ 'magic, sorcery').

очевидно.etymology: Adverb and predicative short neuter form of очевидный ('obvious, evident'), a compound formed from очи ('eyes', dual of око, Proto-Slavic *oko) + видный ('visible', from вид 'sight', Proto-Slavic *vidъ), calquing Latin ēvidēns or German augenscheinlich.

очень.etymology: Developed in Middle Russian (replacing older вельми and гораздо in the sense 'very') from dialectal очунь ('very, truly'), which Vasmer links to очнуться / очутиться ('to come to one's senses, wake up fully', built on око 'eye' or чуять 'to feel'): originally 'wide awake, sensibly, acutely', then generalized as the intensifier 'very'.

очередник.etymology: Formed with agent suffix -ник from очередной / очередь ('turn, line, waiting list'), inherited from East Slavic очередь (compare Old Church Slavonic чрѣда), from Proto-Slavic *čerda ('herd, row, turn, order').

очередной.etymology: Relational adjective formed from очередь ('turn, line, sequence', Old East Slavic очередь, from prefix о- + череда 'turn, order, file', Proto-Slavic *čerda) + suffix -ной.

очередь.etymology: Inherited from East Slavic очередь ('succession, turn in rotation'), showing native East Slavic pleophony (-ере-) from Proto-Slavic *očerdь, built on *ob- + *čerda ('herd, row, regular succession, turn', compare Old Church Slavonic чрѣда and Russian череда).

очистить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix о- ('around, completely') + чистить ('to clean', from чистый 'clean, pure', Old East Slavic чистъ, Proto-Slavic *čistъ).

history.meaning: to clear, to clean, to peel

очистки.etymology: Plural noun formed from очистить / очищать ('to peel, pare, clean', from prefix о- + чистить 'to clean', Proto-Slavic *čistiti) + nominal suffix -ки.

очищать.etymology: Imperfective verb (showing Church Slavonic -щ- from Proto-Slavic *stj) formed from очистить ('to clean, purify, peel', Old Church Slavonic очищати, from о- + чистить, Proto-Slavic *čistiti).

очищенный.etymology: Past passive participial adjective formed from очистить ('to clean, peel, purify', from prefix о- + чистить, Proto-Slavic *čistiti).

очкарик.etymology: Colloquial expressive noun formed in 20th-century Russian with the compound suffix -арик (on the pattern of words like сухарик, комарик) from очки ('glasses, spectacles'), itself the plural diminutive of archaic око ('eye', Old East Slavic око, Proto-Slavic *oko, PIE *h₃ekʷ-).

очки.etymology: Plural of очко, the diminutive of archaic Russian око ('eye', from Proto-Slavic *oko, PIE *h₃ekʷ-). Attested from the 16th–17th centuries in the plural sense 'little eyepieces, spectacles'.

очко.etymology: Diminutive of око ('eye', from Old East Slavic око, Proto-Slavic *oko, PIE *h₃ekʷ-); the gaming sense 'point, score' arose from the pips ('little eyes') marked on dice and playing cards.

очнуться.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic очьнутисѧ ('to wake up, come to'), formed with prefix об-/о- from *čьnǫti / *čuti ('to feel, perceive, be awake'), from Proto-Slavic *čuti.

history.meaning: to come to one's senses, to wake up

ошейник.etymology: Prepositional-prefixal noun formed from о- ('around') + шея ('neck', Old East Slavic шия, Proto-Slavic *šija) + suffix -ник, literally 'that which goes around the neck'.

ошеломлённый.etymology: Past passive participle of ошеломить ('to stun, daze'), literally 'to strike on the helmet', formed from о- + шелом ('helmet', archaic East Slavic form of шлем), from Proto-Slavic *šelmъ.

ошибаться.etymology: Imperfective of ошибиться ('to make a mistake'), literally 'to strike past the mark, miss in hitting', formed with prefix о- ('around, past') + шибить ('to strike, throw') + -ся, from Proto-Slavic *šibati.

history.meaning: to make a mistake, be mistaken

ошибиться.etymology: Formed in Russian from о- ('past the mark, amiss') + Old Russian шибить ('to strike, hurl, fling', Proto-Slavic *šibiti) + -ся: originally a physical metaphor meaning 'to strike past the target, miss one's blow', which became 'to make a mistake, be wrong'.

history.meaning: to miss a blow, miss the mark -> to make a mistake

ошибиться.notes: Past tense drops the -и- in the masculine singular: он ошибся, она ошиблась.

ошибка.etymology: Formed in Russian from ошибиться ('to make a mistake', originally 'to miss one's mark in striking or throwing'), built from prefix о- ('around, past the mark') + dialectal/older шибить ('to strike, hurl, fling', from Proto-Slavic *šibiti) + noun suffix -ка.

history.meaning: to strike past the mark, miss → to err

ошибочка.etymology: Diminutive in -очка of ошибка ('mistake, error'), deverbal noun from ошибиться ('to miss the mark, err'), from о- + шибить ('to hit, strike').

ошибочно.etymology: Adverb formed from ошибочный ('erroneous, mistaken'), adjective from ошибка ('mistake'), derived from ошибиться ('to miss the mark, err', from о- + шибить).

ошибочный.etymology: Adjective derived from ошибка ('mistake, error', deverbal noun from ошибиться 'to miss a blow, err', from prefix о- + шибить 'to strike, hurl', Proto-Slavic *šibiti) + adjectival suffix -ный.

оштрафовать.etymology: Perfective formed with prefix о- from штрафовать ('to fine'), derived from штраф ('fine, penalty'), borrowed in the Petrine era from German Strafe ('punishment, fine').

ощипывать.etymology: Imperfective of ощипать ('to pluck all around'), formed with prefix о- ('around') from щипать ('to pinch, pluck'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *ščipati ('to pinch, nip, pluck').

ощутить.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic ощутити ('to feel, perceive, notice', with South Slavic щ from *tj), formed from prefix о- + *čutiti (compare Old East Slavic очутити, related to чуять / чувство 'sense, feel', Proto-Slavic *čuti).

ощущение.etymology: Verbal noun from ощутить / ощущать ('to feel, sense, perceive'), borrowed from Old Church Slavonic оштутити (with щ < *tj), from Proto-Slavic *ob-čutiti, built on *čuti ('to feel, perceive').

па-пам.etymology: Onomatopoeic interjection imitating a two-note brass fanfare or drum flourish used to announce a comic reveal or surprise ('ta-da!').

падать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic падати and Proto-Slavic *padati ('to fall'), the imperfective-iterative counterpart of пасть (*pasti 'to fall', preserved in упасть and попасть), from Proto-Indo-European *ped- ('to step, stumble, fall').

падение.etymology: Verbal noun formed from пасть / падать ('to fall', from Old East Slavic пасти, Proto-Slavic *pasti, PIE *ped-) + abstract suffix -ение (modeled on Old Church Slavonic падение).

пазл.etymology: Borrowed in the late 20th century from English puzzle (short for jigsaw puzzle, from Early Modern English pusle 'to bewilder, confound').

пакет.etymology: Borrowed in the early eighteenth century via German Paket or French paquet ('small bundle, parcel, packet'), a diminutive of Middle Dutch or Middle French pac ('bundle, pack', cognate with English pack and packet).

history.meaning: bag (paper or plastic carrier bag); packet, parcel

пакет.notes: In everyday Russian, пакет is the standard word for a paper or plastic shopping bag.

пакетик.etymology: Diminutive in -ик of пакет ('packet, bag'), borrowed via German Paket or French paquet from Middle Dutch pak ('bundle, pack').

палата.etymology: Borrowed into Old East Slavic палата ('palace, stone hall, council chamber') from Byzantine Greek παλάτιον (palátion), from Latin palātium ('imperial palace on the Palatine Hill in Rome', source of English palace). From 'vaulted hall in a public building' came both 'parliamentary chamber' and 'hospital ward / room'.

history.meaning: imperial residence on the Palatine Hill

палец.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic пальць and Proto-Slavic *palьcь, formed with the diminutive suffix *-ьcь from *palъ ('thumb, thick digit', often compared by etymologists with Latin pollex 'thumb'). In East Slavic, палец expanded from 'thumb' to mean any finger or toe.
палец.notes: Notice how Czech palec still means specifically 'thumb', whereas Russian палец means any finger (and 'thumb' is большой палец). Drops the fleeting е in oblique cases: палец -> пальца.

палка.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic палъка, derived from палица ('club, staff, cudgel'), from Proto-Slavic *palica / *pala ('stick, staff, club').

палочка.etymology: Diminutive in -очка of палка ('stick, rod'), from Proto-Slavic *palica / *pala ('staff, stick').

пальма.etymology: Borrowed via German Palme or Polish palma from Latin palma ('palm of the hand; palm tree, palm frond as a symbol of victory', so named from the spread-finger shape of its fronds).

history.meaning: palm of the hand; palm tree

пальто.etymology: Borrowed in the 19th century from French paletot ('overcoat'), from Middle French paltoke ('short cloak or tunic'), widely traced via Middle English paltok or Spanish palletoque to Latin palla ('long outer cloak'). Like other French borrowings in -о, it is indeclinable in Russian.
пальто.notes: Indeclinable neuter noun: в тёплом пальто, без пальто.

пальчик.etymology: Diminutive in -чик of палец ('finger, toe'), inherited from Old East Slavic пальць ('thumb; finger'), from Proto-Slavic *palьcь ('thumb, big toe').

памятник.etymology: Inherited via Old East Slavic памятникъ and Old Church Slavonic памѧтьникъ ('memorial, monument, record'), formed from память ('memory') + the suffix -ник: 'that which preserves memory, a monument'.

history.stage: Old Church Slavonic / Old East Slavic

памятник.notes: Takes the dative case for the person commemorated: памятник Пушкину ('monument to Pushkin').

память.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic память (Old Church Slavonic памѧть) and Proto-Slavic *pamętь ('memory, remembrance'), a nominal compound of the archaic nominal prefix *pa- + *mętь ('thought, mind', from Proto-Indo-European *men- 'to think, remember', cognate with Latin mēns and English mind).

панда.etymology: Borrowed via French panda (introduced by Georges Cuvier in 1825 for the red panda), likely from Nepali पोंया (põyā) / Newar निल्या पोंया ('bamboo-eater').

панель.etymology: Borrowed in the nineteenth century via German Paneel or French panneau (Old French panel) from Vulgar Latin *pannellum ('rectangular piece of cloth or wooden wainscoting'), diminutive of Latin pannus ('piece of cloth, pane').

паника.etymology: Borrowed via French panique or German Panik from Ancient Greek panikón (deîma) ('sudden, groundless terror sent by the woodland god Pan'), who was believed to startle travellers and herds in lonely mountain glens.

history.meaning: of the god Pan; sudden terror in the wild

паниковать.etymology: Formed from паника ('panic', borrowed via French panique and German Panik from Ancient Greek πανικός 'pertaining to the god Pan, who inspired sudden groundless terror') + verbal suffix -овать.

панихида.etymology: Borrowed via Old East Slavic and Old Church Slavonic панихида from Byzantine Greek παννυχίς, accusative παννυχίδα ('all-night vigil', from πᾶς 'all' + νύξ 'night'), later specialized in Orthodox liturgy for a memorial service for the dead.

папа.etymology: International nursery kinship word formed by reduplicating the bilabial syllable па- (pa-pa); reinforced in eighteenth- and nineteenth-century Russian family speech by French papa.
папа.notes: Masculine noun in Russian (мой папа 'my dad'), while declining with feminine -а endings.

папаша.etymology: Colloquial and familiar kinship noun formed from папа ('dad, papa', from nursery reduplication *pa-pa / French papa) + expressive suffix -ша.

папин.etymology: Possessive adjective in -ин formed from папа ('dad, father'), borrowed in the 18th–19th centuries from French papa (or nursery Lallwort *papa).

папка.etymology: Borrowed into Russian (with the feminine suffix -ка) from German Pappe ('pasteboard, cardboard'), so called because a document folder was traditionally made of stiff pasteboard covers.

папочка.etymology: Homonymous diminutive: in the sense 'daddy', formed from папа ('dad') + affectionate suffix -очка; in the sense 'folder', formed from папка ('cardboard file folder', borrowed from German Pappe 'pasteboard, cardboard') + diminutive suffix -очка.

пар.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic паръ / пара ('steam, vapor, breath'), from Proto-Slavic *parъ / *para ('steam, warm vapor'), related to парить ('to steam').

пара.etymology: Borrowed in the 17th century via Polish para from Middle High German pār (modern German Paar 'pair, couple'), ultimately from Latin pāria ('equal things, a pair'), neuter plural of pār ('equal, matching').
пара.notes: Colloquially used with a genitive plural noun for 'a couple of, a few': *пара минут* ('a couple of minutes'), *пара слов* ('a couple of words').

парадный.etymology: Adjective derived from парад ('parade, ceremonial display', borrowed in the early 18th century via German Parade from French parade, from Spanish parada, ultimately from Latin parāre 'to prepare, adorn') + suffix -ный.

парализовать.etymology: Borrowed from French paralyser ('to paralyze', formed from paralysie 'paralysis', via Latin paralysis from Ancient Greek παράλυσις 'palsy, disabling at the side', from παραλύω 'to loosen, disable') + verbal suffix -овать.

паранойя.etymology: Borrowed via German Paranoia / New Latin paranoia from Ancient Greek παράνοια ('madness, derangement, delusion', from παρά 'beside, amiss' + νόος / νοῦς 'mind, intellect').

парашют.etymology: Borrowed from French parachute, coined in 1785 by Jean-Pierre Blanchard from Italian/Greek-style para- ('defense against', from Italian parare 'to ward off') + French chute ('fall').

history.meaning: device to slow a fall, parachute

пардон.etymology: Borrowed from French pardon ('forgiveness, excuse me'), deverbal noun from pardonner ('to forgive'), from Vulgar Latin *perdonare (from per- + donare 'to give').

парень.etymology: Attested in Russian from the 17th century. Most etymologists (following Sobolevsky and Vasmer) derive парень from dialectal парь ('lad') or directly from Old East Slavic паробокъ / паробьць ('servant lad, youth', compare Polish parobek and Ukrainian парубок), formed with the archaic prefix па- and робъ ('servant, child, worker') and reshaped with the suffix -ень.
парень.notes: In modern colloquial Russian, парень means both 'guy, lad' and 'boyfriend' (мой парень). Its plural is irregular in everyday speech: **ребята** (or **парни**).

пари.etymology: Borrowed from French pari ('bet, wager'), deverbal noun from parier ('to bet'), from Latin pariāre ('to make equal, match stakes'), from par ('equal').

париж.etymology: Borrowed via Polish Paryż (compare Italian Parigi) from French Paris, from Late Latin Parisii, named after the Gaulish Celtic tribe (Parisii) whose chief settlement was Lutetia Parisiorum.

париться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of парить ('to steam, beat with a birch besom in a steam bath'), derived from пар ('steam, vapor'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *parъ ('steam, heat').

history.meaning: to steam oneself in a bathhouse; (slang) to sweat over

парк.etymology: Borrowed in the 18th century via French parc and German Park (or English park) from Medieval Latin parricus ('enclosed tract of land'), of West Germanic origin ('fenced enclosure, pen').

парковаться.etymology: Reflexive verb formed from парковать ('to park a vehicle', borrowed in the 20th century from English park / German parken, from park 'enclosed ground, vehicle depot') + reflexive particle -ся.

парковка.etymology: Deverbal noun formed from парковать ('to park a vehicle', borrowed from English park) + nominal suffix -ка.

пармезан.etymology: Borrowed from French parmesan ('of Parma; Parmesan cheese'), from Italian parmigiano ('from Parma, a city in Emilia-Romagna, Italy').

паровозик.etymology: Formed with the diminutive suffix -ик from паровоз ('steam locomotive'), a nineteenth-century Russian compound coined by N. I.
