победить.etymology: Adopted via Old Church Slavonic побѣдити ('to conquer, vanquish, defeat'), formed from по- and бѣдити ('to compel, force, overcome'), a denominative verb from бѣда ('calamity, distress, compulsion', modern Russian беда, from Proto-Slavic *běda 'necessity, distress', cognate with Gothic baidjan 'to compel' and Latin fīdō).
победить.notes: Famous in Russian grammar for lacking a standard 1st-person singular future form (*побежу / *победю are avoided in standard speech in favor of **я одержу победу** or **я смогу победить**).

побежать.etymology: Inceptive perfective formed with prefix по- ('setting off') from бежать ('to run'), inherited from Old East Slavic бѣжати, from Proto-Slavic *běžati ('to run, flee').

history.meaning: to start running, to run off

побеждать.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic побѣждати (imperfective of побѣдити 'to conquer, vanquish', with жд < *dj), derived from бѣда ('trouble, compulsion, plight', Proto-Slavic *běda), originally meaning 'to overcome by force'.

побелеть.etymology: Perfective inchoative verb formed with prefix по- + белеть ('to become white, pale', derived from белый 'white', Old East Slavic бѣлыи, Proto-Slavic *bělъ).

побеспокоить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix по- + беспокоить ('to disturb, bother', derived from беспокойный 'restless, uneasy', from без 'without' + покой 'peace, rest', Proto-Slavic *pokojь).

побеспокоиться.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed from побеспокоить ('to trouble, bother', from по- + без + покой 'peace, rest') + reflexive particle -ся.

history.meaning: to take the trouble, worry a bit

побитый.etymology: Past passive participle of побить ('to beat, batter, strike down'), formed with prefix по- from бить ('to beat, hit'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *biti.

побить.etymology: Prefixed perfective verb inherited from Old East Slavic побити, formed from по- + бить ('to beat, strike', from Proto-Slavic *biti, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeyH- 'to strike').

history.meaning: to beat up; to beat (a record)

поблагодарить.etymology: Perfective formed with prefix по- from благодарить ('to thank'), derived from Old Church Slavonic благодарити, a calque on Greek εὐχαριστεῖν (from благо 'good' + дарить 'to give, grant').

побледнеть.etymology: Perfective formed with prefix по- from бледнеть ('to grow pale'), derived from бледный ('pale'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *blědъ ('pale, wan').

поближе.etymology: Formed by adding the attenuative prefix по- ('a little more, somewhat') to ближе ('closer, nearer', comparative of близкий / близко, from Proto-Slavic *blizъ).

поблизости.etymology: Adverb formed by univerbation of preposition по + dative/locative singular близости of близость ('nearness, proximity', from близкий / близ 'near', Proto-Slavic *blizъ).

побоище.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic побоище ('battlefield, great slaughter, carnage'), formed from побой / побить ('to beat down, slay', from prefix по- + бить 'to strike, beat', Proto-Slavic *biti) + augmentative/locative suffix -ище (*-išče).

history.meaning: site of a battle or slaughter

поболтать.etymology: Delimitative perfective verb formed with prefix по- ('for a while') + болтать ('to shake, stir, dangle; colloquially to wag one's tongue, chat', from an expressive Slavic root *bъltati).

history.meaning: to stir, dangle; to chat, chatter

побольше.etymology: Formed in Russian by adding the attenuative/distributive prefix по- ('a bit, somewhat, as much as possible') to больше ('more, bigger', comparative of большой and много).

history.meaning: a bit more, a bit bigger, plenty

побрить.etymology: Prefixed perfective verb formed from по- + брить ('to shave'), inherited from Old East Slavic брити, from Proto-Slavic *briti ('to shave, cut with a razor'), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰreyH- ('to cut, shear'; cognate with Sanskrit bhrīṇāti).

побриться.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed with prefix по- + брить ('to shave', from Old East Slavic брити, Proto-Slavic *briti, PIE *bʰreyH- 'to cut with a sharp edge') + reflexive particle -ся.

побывать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix по- + бывать ('to be repeatedly, visit', iterative of быть 'to be', from Proto-Slavic *byvati).

побыть.etymology: Delimitative perfective verb inherited from Old East Slavic побыти ('to stay awhile, remain briefly'), from Proto-Slavic *pobyti, combining prefix *po- ('for a short while') with *byti ('to be'), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰuH- ('to become, grow, be').

history.meaning: to stay for a bit, spend a little time

побыть.notes: Like быть, its future and imperative use the stem побуд- (я побуду в тишине, побудь со мной пять минут).

повар.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic поваръ ('cook'), formed from prefix по- + the root вар- of варить ('to boil, cook', from Proto-Slavic *variti, causative of *vьrěti 'to boil, bubble', built on *varъ 'boiling heat, boiling water').

поварской.etymology: Adjective formed with suffix -ской from повар ('cook, chef'), inherited from Old East Slavic поваръ, derived from по- + варить ('to boil, cook', from Proto-Slavic *povarъ).

поварёнок.etymology: Formed with the young-person or apprentice suffix -ёнок (from Proto-Slavic *-ę, genitive *-ęte) from повар ('cook'), inherited from Old East Slavic поваръ, built on по- + варить ('to boil, cook', Proto-Slavic *variti).
поварёнок.notes: Like other -ёнок nouns, its plural drops -ок and takes -ата: поварёнок → поварята.

поведение.etymology: Verbal noun from повести (себя) ('to conduct oneself'), formed from по- + вести ('to lead, conduct', Proto-Slavic *vesti), calquing French conduite or German Aufführung / Benehmen.

повезти.etymology: Perfective verb formed with the inceptive prefix по- and везти ('to convey, carry by vehicle, pull a cart or sleigh', inherited from Old East Slavic везти, Proto-Slavic *vezti, from PIE *weǵʰ- 'to convey in a vehicle', cognate with Latin vehō and English wagon / way). From the image of a horse or fortune 'pulling one's cart smoothly along', the impersonal dative construction мне повезло ('it carried me well') became the standard Russian expression for 'I got lucky'.

history.meaning: to take by vehicle; (impersonal + dat. повезло) to be lucky

rootFamily.gloss: to carry by vehicle; to be lucky (impf.)

повелитель.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic повелитель ('ruler, sovereign, commander'), agent noun formed from повелѣти ('to command, order', from по- + велѣти 'to command, will', Proto-Slavic *velěti) + suffix -тель.

поверить.etymology: Formed from the perfectivizing prefix по- + верить ('to believe, trust', Proto-Slavic *věriti, derived from вера 'faith, belief', Proto-Slavic *věra, cognate with Latin vērus 'true').
поверить.notes: Takes the dative case for the person or thing believed: поверить другу ('to believe a friend'), поверить своим глазам ('to believe one's eyes').

повернуть.etymology: Formed from по- + вернуть ('to turn, twist', Proto-Slavic *vьrnǫti, built on the same Indo-European root *wert- 'to turn' as вертеть and поворот): 'to turn (a key, a handle, or around a corner)'.

повернуться.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed with prefix по- + вернуть ('to turn', from Old East Slavic вьрнути, Proto-Slavic *vьrnǫti) + reflexive particle -ся.

повеселее.etymology: Attenuative comparative formed with prefix по- ('a bit, somewhat') + веселее (comparative of весёлый 'cheerful, merry', from Old East Slavic веселыи, Proto-Slavic *veselъ).

повеселиться.etymology: Prefixed perfective verb formed from delimitative по- ('for a while') + веселиться ('to have fun, make merry'), derived from весёлый ('merry, cheerful, joyful', inherited from Old East Slavic веселыи, Proto-Slavic *veselъ).

повесить.etymology: Perfective verb formed from the prefix по- + весить ('to hang, suspend', Proto-Slavic *věsiti), a causative verb built on the root of висеть ('to hang, be suspended', Proto-Slavic *visěti): literally 'to cause to hang'.

повеситься.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed with prefix по- + весить ('to hang, suspend', causative of висеть 'to hang', from Proto-Slavic *věsiti) + reflexive particle -ся.

повести.etymology: Formed with the perfective/inchoative prefix по- ('setting off') + вести ('to lead, conduct', inherited from Old East Slavic вести and Proto-Slavic *vesti).

history.meaning: to lead, take along; to start leading

rootFamily.gloss: to lead in; to wind up
to spend time; to lead through

повестись.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed from повести ('to lead', from prefix по- + вести 'to lead', Proto-Slavic *vesti) + reflexive particle -сь; originally 'to become customary', and in modern colloquial usage 'to let oneself be led on, fall for a trick'.

history.meaning: to become customary; (colloq.) to fall for something

повестка.etymology: Noun in -ка derived from повестить ('to notify, announce, summon'), formed from по- + весть ('news, message, notice', inherited from Proto-Slavic *věstь, from *věděti 'to know').

повесть.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic повѣсть ('narrative, tale, chronicle account, report'), from Proto-Slavic *pověstь (*pověd-tь), formed from повѣдати ('to tell, relate', from prefix по- + *věděti 'to know').

повидать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix по- + видать ('to see', iterative/colloquial counterpart of видеть 'to see', from Proto-Slavic *vidati).

повисеть.etymology: Delimitative perfective verb formed with prefix по- ('for a while') + висеть ('to hang', from Old East Slavic висѣти, Proto-Slavic *visěti).

history.meaning: to hang (for a while); to hold (on the line)

повлиять.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix по- + влиять ('to influence', back-formed in the late 18th or 19th century from влияние 'influence', a loan translation of French influence / Latin influentia, from в- 'in' + лиять 'to pour, flow', Proto-Slavic *lijati).

повод.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic поводъ ('rein, bridle, lead-rope; guidance, cause'), a deverbal noun from поводить / повести ('to lead along', built from по- + водить / вести 'to lead', Proto-Slavic *povodъ). From the literal 'bridle rein' by which a horse is led (still used in на поводу у кого-то), the word developed the figurative meaning 'that which leads to an action: a pretext, occasion, or reason'.

поводырь.etymology: Agent noun formed from поводить ('to lead about by the hand or rein', from prefix по- + водить 'to lead', Proto-Slavic *voditi; compare повод 'rein, lead') + expressive agent suffix -ырь.

поворачивать.etymology: Formed as the imperfective counterpart of повернуть ('to turn'), built from по- + -ворач- (lengthened East Slavic pleophonic stem of воротить 'to turn', from Proto-Slavic *vortiti, with т -> ч) + -ивать.

поворачиваться.etymology: Formed by adding the reflexive-intransitive postfix -ся to поворачивать ('to turn'): 'to turn oneself around, turn one's body or head'.

поворот.etymology: Inherited East Slavic noun formed from повернуть / поворачивать ('to turn'), showing regular East Slavic pleophony -оро- from Proto-Slavic *po- + *vortъ ('a turn, bend', from *vьrtěti 'to turn, spin', PIE *wert-).

повредить.etymology: Formed with perfective prefix по- from вредить ('to harm, injure'), borrowed from Old Church Slavonic врѣдити (compare native East Slavic вередить), from Proto-Slavic *verdъ ('harm, sore, injury').

повреждение.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic поврѣждение ('harm, injury, damage'), verbal noun from поврѣдити ('to harm, injure', showing non-pleophonic -вред- from Proto-Slavic *verditi, from *verdъ 'harm, sore').

повторение.etymology: Verbal noun formed from повторить ('to repeat, do a second time', from Old Church Slavonic / Old East Slavic повторити, derived from второй 'second', Proto-Slavic *vъtorъ) + abstract suffix -ение.

повторить.etymology: Adopted via Old Church Slavonic and Old East Slavic повторити ('to do a second time, repeat'), a denominal verb built from по- + вторый ('second', modern Russian второй, Proto-Slavic *vъtorъ): literally 'to second, do a second time'.

history.stage: Old Church Slavonic / Old East Slavic
history.meaning: to do a second time, repeat

повториться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of повторить ('to repeat, do a second time'), inherited from Old East Slavic повторити, formed from по- + второй (Old East Slavic въторыи 'second', Proto-Slavic *vъtorъ).

history.meaning: to do a second time, repeat

повторять.etymology: Formed as the imperfective counterpart of повторить ('to repeat', built on второй 'second') by replacing -ить with the imperfective suffix -ять.

повторяться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective verb formed from повторять ('to repeat', from повторить, derived from второй 'second', Proto-Slavic *vъtorъ) + reflexive particle -ся.

повыпендриваться.etymology: Delimitative perfective verb formed with prefix по- ('for a while, a bit') + выпендриваться ('to show off, put on airs', expressive colloquial Russian verb formed with prefix вы- and suffix -иваться, of uncertain slang origin, often linked to dialectal пендря 'fop, dandy').

history.meaning: to show off, put on airs

повысить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix по- + высить ('to raise, elevate', derived from высокий / высь 'high / height', from Proto-Slavic *vysiti, from *vysъ 'height').

повышать.etymology: Imperfective verb (with palatalization *sj > ш) formed from повысить ('to raise, elevate', from prefix по- + высить, Proto-Slavic *vysiti).

повышаться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective verb formed from повышать ('to raise, increase', from по- + высить, Proto-Slavic *vysiti) + reflexive particle -ся.

повыше.etymology: Attenuative comparative formed with prefix по- ('a bit, somewhat') from выше ('higher'), comparative of высокий ('high'), from Proto-Slavic *vyše.

повышение.etymology: Verbal noun formed from повысить ('to raise, promote', from по- + высить, Proto-Slavic *vysiti) + abstract action suffix -ение.

повязка.etymology: Deverbal noun formed from повязать / повязывать ('to tie around, bind', from prefix по- + вязать 'to tie, bind', Proto-Slavic *vęzati) + nominal suffix -ка.

погаснуть.etymology: Formed from the perfectivizing prefix по- + гаснуть ('to go out, be extinguished', Proto-Slavic *gasnǫti, inchoative of *gasiti 'to extinguish', cognate with Lithuanian gesiti 'to put out a fire').

history.meaning: to go out, die down (of a light or flame)

погаснуть.notes: Past tense drops the suffix -ну-: свет погас ('the light went out'), свеча погасла ('the candle went out').

погибнуть.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic погибнути ('to perish, be lost'), formed with perfective prefix по- from гибнуть ('to perish', originally 'to bend double, sink down', from Proto-Slavic *gybnǫti).

history.meaning: to perish, to die (in an accident/war)

погладить.etymology: Formed from the perfectivizing prefix по- + гладить ('to make smooth, stroke, iron', Proto-Slavic *gladiti, derived from гладкий 'smooth', Proto-Slavic *gladъkъ).
погладить.notes: Means both 'to stroke/pet' (погладить кошку) and 'to iron' (погладить рубашку), because both actions smooth a surface.

погнать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with inchoative prefix по- + гнать ('to drive, chase', from Old East Slavic гънати, Proto-Slavic *gъnati, PIE *gʷʰen- 'to strike, drive').

history.meaning: to drive off, chase; погнали = let's go

погнуть.etymology: Formed with the perfective prefix по- + гнуть ('to bend, curve'), inherited from Old East Slavic гънути and Proto-Slavic *gъbnǫti (with loss of *b before *n; compare сгиб 'crease, fold').

history.meaning: to bend (slightly or out of shape)

поговаривать.etymology: Attenuative-frequentative imperfective verb formed with prefix по- ('occasionally, quietly') + говаривать (frequentative of говорить 'to speak, talk', from Proto-Slavic *govoriti).

поговорить.etymology: Formed from the delimitative/perfective prefix по- ('for a while') + говорить ('to speak, talk', originally 'to chatter, make noise', from говор 'talk, murmur', Proto-Slavic *govorъ): 'to have a talk, chat for a while'.

погода.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic погода and Proto-Slavic *pogoda ('favourable weather, seasonable time; weather'), formed from по- + год ('suitable time, right season; year', Proto-Slavic *godъ, related to годный 'fit, suitable' and ждать / погодить 'to wait'). Originally погода meant specifically 'good, fair weather' (contrasted with непогода 'bad weather'), before generalizing in Russian to any weather.

погодить.etymology: Formed with prefix по- ('for a little while') from годить ('to wait, bide one's time'), derived from год ('fitting time, period, year'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *goditi (from *godъ).

history.meaning: to bide time, wait for the right moment

погонять.etymology: Verb (imperfective 'to urge on, drive' or delimitative perfective 'to drive around for a while') formed with prefix по- + гонять ('to drive, chase repeatedly', iterative of гнать, from Proto-Slavic *goniti / *gaňati).

history.meaning: to urge on; to put through one's paces

погорячиться.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed with prefix по- + горячиться ('to get heated, lose one's temper', derived from горячий 'hot, ardent', from гореть 'to burn', Proto-Slavic *gorěti).

history.meaning: to lose one's temper, get carried away

пограничник.etymology: Agent noun in -ник formed from пограничный ('border, frontier'), derived from по- ('along') + граница ('border'), from Proto-Slavic *granь ('boundary mark, edge').

погреться.etymology: Delimitative reflexive formed with prefix по- ('a little, for a while') and -ся from греть ('to warm, heat'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *grěti.

погром.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic погромъ ('devastation, rout, destruction by thunder or war'), deverbal noun from погромить ('to smash, devastate', from prefix по- + громить 'to smash, thunder', from гром 'thunder', Proto-Slavic *gromъ).

погружать.etymology: Imperfective verb (with palatalization *zj > ж) formed from погрузить ('to plunge, immerse, sink', from prefix по- + грузить 'to sink, submerge, load', from Proto-Slavic *grǫziti).

погубить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic погубити ('to destroy, ruin, slay'), formed from по- + губить ('to ruin, destroy'), from Proto-Slavic *gubiti, the old causative counterpart of *gybnǫti (Russian гибнуть 'to perish', literally 'to cause to perish').

history.meaning: to ruin, destroy, bring to ruin

погулять.etymology: Delimitative perfective verb formed with prefix по- ('for a while') + гулять ('to walk, stroll, make merry', from East Slavic гуляти).

history.meaning: to go for a walk; to have some fun

под.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic подъ ('under, beneath'), from Proto-Slavic *podъ (originally also a noun meaning 'bottom, floor, hearthstone', still used as под in печной под 'oven floor'), continuing a Proto-Indo-European formation built on *ped- / *pod- ('foot, ground underneath').
под.notes: Takes the instrumental case for static position (под столом 'under the table') and the accusative for motion (под стол 'under the table').

подавать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic подавати, from Proto-Slavic *podavati, the imperfective of *podati (Russian подать 'to hand over, serve, present'), formed from *po- + *dati ('to give').

history.meaning: to hand, present → to serve, give

подаваться.etymology: Reflexive and passive imperfective verb formed from подавать ('to give, hand over, serve food', imperfective of подать, from prefix по- + давать 'to give', Proto-Slavic *davati) + reflexive particle -ся.

history.meaning: to be served; to move or lean forward

подавиться.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed with prefix по- + давить ('to press, squeeze, choke', from Old East Slavic давити, Proto-Slavic *daviti) + reflexive particle -ся.

подальше.etymology: Formed in Russian by adding the attenuative prefix по- ('a bit, somewhat') to дальше ('further, farther', comparative of далёкий and далеко).

history.meaning: a bit further away, well away

подано.etymology: Short neuter singular past passive participle of подать ('to serve food or drink, bring up a carriage', from prefix по- + дать 'to give', Old East Slavic подати, Proto-Slavic *podati), used predicatively in announcements such as «Кушать подано!».

подарить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with the prefix по- and дарить ('to give as a gift, bestow'), a denominative verb from дар ('gift'), inherited from Old East Slavic даръ and Proto-Slavic *darъ ('gift', from the PIE root *deh₃- 'to give', as in дать 'to give' and Greek δῶρον 'gift').

history.meaning: to bestow, grant as a gift

подарок.etymology: Derived in East Slavic with the noun suffix -ок from подарить ('to give as a gift, present'), itself built from по- + дарить ('to bestow', from дар 'gift', Proto-Slavic *darъ, from *dati 'to give').
подарок.notes: Drops the fleeting -о- in all oblique forms: подарок -> подарка, подарки.

подать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic подати and Proto-Slavic *podati ('to hand over, reach out, serve'), formed from по- + дать ('to give', Proto-Slavic *dati).

history.meaning: to serve (food); to hand, pass; to submit

подать.notes: Conjugates with the archaic reduplicated stem of дать: я подам, ты подашь, он подаст, они подадут.

подача.etymology: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *podača, a feminine action noun formed with the suffix *-jа (yielding -ча after dental/stem *podat-) from *podati ('to serve, hand over, deliver').

history.meaning: to hand over, serve → act of serving or delivering
serving, plating (of food); serve (in sport); supply

подбодрить.etymology: Prefixed perfective verb formed from под- ('up, slightly, in support') + бодрить ('to invigorate, cheer'), derived from бодрый ('brisk, cheerful, alert', inherited from Old East Slavic бъдрыи, Proto-Slavic *bъdrъ, from PIE *bʰewdʰ- 'to be awake, alert').

history.meaning: cheerful, brisk → to invigorate → to cheer up, encourage

подбросить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix под- ('up from underneath; along the way; secretly') + бросить ('to throw, toss', from Proto-Slavic *brositi).

history.meaning: to toss up; to give a lift; to plant/slip

подвал.etymology: Formed in East Slavic from подвалить ('to heap or bank earth under a wall; to build beneath a rampart or foundation'), combining под- ('under') + вал ('earthen bank, rampart, foundation beam', from валить). Originally the space beneath a fortification rampart or house foundation, it became the standard word for a cellar or basement.

history.meaning: space under a foundation bank or wall

подвезти.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix под- ('up to, along the way') + везти ('to convey by vehicle', from Old East Slavic везти, Proto-Slavic *vezti, PIE *weǵʰ-).

подвернуть.etymology: Formed in Russian from под- ('under') + вернуть ('to turn, twist', Proto-Slavic *vьrnǫti): 'to tuck or roll up from underneath (sleeves or trouser hems)' or 'to twist/sprain (one's ankle or foot: подвернуть ногу)'.

history.meaning: to tuck, roll up; to twist (an ankle)

подвесить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix под- ('up from underneath') + весить ('to hang, suspend', causative of висеть 'to hang', from Proto-Slavic *věsiti).

подвести.etymology: Formed with prefix под- ('up to, under') from вести (веду, 'to lead'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *vesti; the idiom 'to let someone down, fail' arose from 'to lead someone into a trap or under a blow'.

history.meaning: to lead under or up to
to bring up to; to let down, fail

подвинуть.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix по- + двинуть ('to move, shift', semelfactive of двигать, from Proto-Slavic *dvignǫti).

подвинуться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of подвинуть ('to move slightly, shift'), formed with prefix по- from двинуть ('to move'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *dvignǫti ('to lift, move').

подводить.etymology: Imperfective verb formed with prefix под- ('up to, under') + водить ('to lead', iterative of вести, from Proto-Slavic *voditi); the sense 'to let down' developed from 'to lead someone into trouble or under a blow'.

history.meaning: to lead up to; to sum up; to let down

подвозить.etymology: Imperfective verb formed with prefix под- ('up to, along the way') + возить ('to convey by vehicle', iterative of везти, from Proto-Slavic *voziti).

подвох.etymology: Colloquial noun connected with dialectal подвохать ('to plot, contrive secretly') or formed as an expressive alteration of подвод ('leading into a trap, trickery', deverbal from подводить 'to lead into trouble, let down').

history.meaning: leading into a trap / to contrive secretly

подглядывать.etymology: Imperfective verb formed with the prefix под- ('from under, secretly on the sly') + глядывать (iterative of глядеть 'to look, gaze', from Proto-Slavic *ględati).

подготавливать.etymology: Secondary imperfective verb formed from подготовить ('to prepare in advance', from prefix под- + готовить 'to prepare', from готовый 'ready', Proto-Slavic *gotovъ) + imperfective suffix -ивать.

подготовить.etymology: Perfective verb formed in Russian from the prefix под- ('up to a required state, in advance') + готовить ('to prepare, make ready'), which is built on the adjective готовый ('ready', Proto-Slavic *gotovъ).

history.meaning: to prepare in advance, get ready

подготовиться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of подготовить ('to prepare'), formed with prefix под- from готовить ('to prepare, make ready'), derived from готовый ('ready'), from Proto-Slavic *gotovъ.

подгузник.etymology: Prepositional-prefixal noun formed from под- ('under') + dialectal/archaic гузно ('buttocks, rump, rear end', from Proto-Slavic *guzьno / *guzъ 'rump, protuberance') + suffix -ник, literally 'cloth worn under the bottom'.

поддаваться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective verb formed from поддавать ('to yield under pressure; in games, to intentionally let an opponent take pieces', from prefix под- + давать 'to give', Proto-Slavic *davati) + reflexive particle -ся.

history.meaning: to give away pieces; to add steam/force
to give in, yield (to); to let someone win

поддержать.etymology: Prefixed perfective verb formed from под- ('under, from beneath') + держать ('to hold', inherited from Old East Slavic дьржати, Proto-Slavic *dьržati): literally 'to hold up from underneath', developing the figurative sense 'to support, back up' (paralleling Latin sustinēre and French soutenir).

history.meaning: to hold up; to support, back

поддерживать.etymology: Imperfective verb formed with the suffix -ивать from поддержать ('to hold up from underneath, support'), built on prefix под- ('under') + держать ('to hold', from Old East Slavic дьржати and Proto-Slavic *dьržati).

history.meaning: to hold up from below → to support, back up, maintain

поддержка.etymology: Deverbal noun formed with the suffix -ка from поддержать / поддерживать ('to hold up from underneath, support'), built from под- ('under') + держать ('to hold'). In the 18th–19th centuries it also absorbed the figurative sense of French soutenir / support ('moral, political, or financial backing').

поддеть.etymology: Formed with the prefix под- ('under, from beneath') + деть ('to put, place, catch', from Old East Slavic дѣти and Proto-Slavic *děti): literally 'to slip or hook something underneath in order to lift or pry it up'.

поддон.etymology: Formed with prefix под- ('under') from дно (stem дон-, 'bottom'), inherited from Old East Slavic дъно, from Proto-Slavic *dъno ('bottom').

подействовать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix по- + действовать ('to act, operate, work', derived from действо 'action, deed', from Old Church Slavonic дѣиство, from дѣяти 'to do, act', Proto-Slavic *dějati).

поделать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix по- + делать ('to do, make', from Old East Slavic дѣлати, Proto-Slavic *dělati, derived from *dělo 'deed, work').

history.meaning: to do (especially in что поделаешь 'what can one do')

поделить.etymology: Perfective formed with prefix по- from делить ('to divide, share'), inherited from Old East Slavic дѣлити, from Proto-Slavic *děliti ('to divide, part').

history.meaning: to divide, to split, to share out

поделиться.etymology: Perfective reflexive formed with prefix по- and -ся from делить ('to divide, share'), inherited from Old East Slavic дѣлити, from Proto-Slavic *děliti.

поделка.etymology: Noun in -ка derived from поделать ('to make, craft'), formed with prefix по- from делать ('to do, make'), from Proto-Slavic *dělati.

подержать.etymology: Formed from the delimitative prefix по- ('for a little while') + держать ('to hold, keep', Old East Slavic дьржати, Proto-Slavic *dьržati): 'to hold for a moment or a while'.
подержать.notes: Do not confuse подержать ('to hold for a while', prefix по-, single -д-) with поддержать ('to support, back up', prefix под-, double -дд-).

подешевле.etymology: Attenuative comparative formed with prefix по- ('a bit, somewhat') + дешевле (comparative of дешёвый 'cheap', from Old East Slavic дешевыи).

поджаренный.etymology: Past passive participle of поджарить ('to fry or toast lightly, brown'), formed from attenuative/bottom prefix под- ('slightly; from underneath') + жарить ('to fry, roast, toast', derived from жар 'heat, glowing coals', Proto-Slavic *žarъ).

history.meaning: to toast, brown → toasted, lightly browned

поджарый.etymology: Adjective formed from prefix под- ('from underneath, slightly') + жар / жарить ('heat / to roast, dry out by heat', Proto-Slavic *žarъ), originally describing a horse or hunting dog with a taut, 'dried-up' belly free of fat.

поджать.etymology: Formed with prefix под- ('under, inward') from жать (жму, 'to press, squeeze'), inherited from Old East Slavic жати (жьму), from Proto-Slavic *žęti ('to press, squeeze').

поджигать.etymology: Imperfective verb formed with prefix под- ('from underneath') + -жигать (iterative stem of жечь 'to burn', from Old East Slavic жьгати / жечи, Proto-Slavic *žьgati / *žegti).

history.meaning: to set fire to from underneath

подиум.etymology: Borrowed via German Podium and French podium from Latin podium ('elevated platform, balcony, plinth', from Ancient Greek πόδιον 'little foot, base, pedestal', diminutive of πούς, genitive ποδός 'foot').

подкаблучник.etymology: Colloquial noun formed with prefix под- ('under'), каблук ('shoe heel', borrowed via Turkic kabluq 'heel'), and agent suffix -ник, from the phrase быть под каблуком ('to be under one's wife's heel').

history.meaning: heel of a boot or shoe

подкачать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix под- + качать ('to pump; to rock, shake', from Proto-Slavic *kačati); literally 'to pump up a bit more', and colloquially 'to let people down, fail to measure up' (especially in не подкачай!).

history.meaning: to pump up; (colloq.) to let down, fall short

подкашиваться.etymology: Formed as the imperfective reflexive of подкоситься ('to be cut from underneath, buckle, give way'), built from под- ('under, at the base') + косить ('to mow, cut down with a scythe', from коса 'scythe', Proto-Slavic *kosa): a vivid metaphor comparing knees or legs giving way from exhaustion or shock to grass cut at the stem by a scythe (ноги подкашиваются).

history.meaning: to cut from underneath -> to buckle, give way (of legs)

morphemes.meaning: mow, cut down (косить, о -> а and с -> ш)

подкашиваться.notes: Almost always used of legs or knees: от усталости ноги подкашиваются ('one's legs are buckling from tiredness').

подкинуть.etymology: Perfective semelfactive verb formed with prefix под- ('up from underneath; along the way; secretly') + кинуть ('to throw, toss', from Old East Slavic кинути, Proto-Slavic *kynǫti).

history.meaning: to toss up; to give a lift; to plant or slip

подкладка.etymology: Deverbal noun formed from подкладывать / подкласть ('to lay underneath, line a garment', from prefix под- 'under' + класть 'to lay, put', Proto-Slavic *klasti) + nominal suffix -ка.

подключить.etymology: Perfective verb formed by prefix substitution with под- ('up to, in addition') after включить ('to switch on, include', derived from ключ 'key, clasp', Proto-Slavic *kľučь).

history.meaning: to connect; to bring in, pull strings

подкова.etymology: Deverbal noun from Russian подковать ('to shoe a horse, to nail iron beneath a hoof'), composed of под- ('under') and ковать ('to forge, hammer metal'). The verb descends from Proto-Slavic *kovati ('to forge, strike'), from the Proto-Indo-European root *kewh₂- ('to hew, strike, forge'). The Slavic root is directly cognate with English hew and Latin cūdere ('to strike, beat').

cognates.meaning: to chop or strike with a tool (from PIE *kewh₂-)

подкрутить.etymology: Formed in Russian from the prefix под- ('a little more, tighter') + крутить ('to twist, turn', from Proto-Slavic *krǫtiti 'to twist, wind', related to крутой 'tightly twisted, steep'): literally 'to give an extra turn to tighten'.

history.meaning: to tighten a bit, screw tighter

подкупать.etymology: Imperfective verb formed with prefix под- ('secretly, underhandedly') + купать (imperfective stem of купить 'to buy', from Proto-Slavic *kupiti).

history.meaning: to bribe; to win over, disarm

подкупить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix под- ('secretly, underhandedly') + купить ('to buy', from Old East Slavic купити, Proto-Slavic *kupiti).

подлец.etymology: Personal noun formed from подлый ('base, vile, mean', borrowed via Polish podły 'lowly, common, base', from Proto-Slavic *podьlъ, derived from *podъ 'under, below', originally meaning 'of humble rank') + agent suffix -ец.

подлизываться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective formed with prefix под- ('up to') and -ся from лизать ('to lick'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *lizati ('to lick'), comparing a fawning person to a dog licking its master.

подложить.etymology: Formed with prefix под- ('under') from ложить ('to lay, put'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *ložiti ('to lay, place').

history.meaning: to put under, to slip under

подлый.etymology: Borrowed in the 17th century from Polish podły ('base, lowly, ignoble, cheap'), derived from pod ('under, beneath', Proto-Slavic *podъ); originally 'of low social rank, common' (подлое сословие), later 'base, vile'.

подменить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix под- ('in place of, surreptitiously') + менить ('to change, exchange', from мена 'exchange', Proto-Slavic *měniti).

history.meaning: to stand in for, cover for; to swap secretly

подмести.etymology: Formed from под- ('under, along the floor') + мести ('to sweep, fling', Proto-Slavic *mesti, present stem мет-): 'to sweep the floor clean with a broom'.
подмести.notes: Conjugates with the dental stem мет-: я подмету, ты подметёшь; past tense подмёл, подмела.

подмешивать.etymology: Secondary imperfective verb formed from подмешать ('to mix in, adulterate, slip into food or drink', from prefix под- + мешать 'to mix, stir', Proto-Slavic *měšati) + imperfective suffix -ивать.

history.meaning: to mix in, slip (into food or drink)

подмигнуть.etymology: Perfective semelfactive verb formed with prefix под- ('surreptitiously, toward') + мигнуть ('to blink, wink', from Proto-Slavic *mignǫti, PIE *meygʷʰ- 'to blink, twinkle').

поднести.etymology: Formed with the prefix под- ('up to, close to') + нести ('to carry, bring', inherited from Old East Slavic нести and Proto-Slavic *nesti).

history.meaning: to bring close, hold up to

поднимать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic подъимати (Proto-Slavic *podъjimati), formed from под- ('from under, upward') + -нимать (the imperfective stem of ять / взять 'to take', Proto-Slavic *jęti / *imati, with an epenthetic н- generalized from prefixes originally ending in a nasal, such as сън-имати -> снимать): literally 'to take from underneath', hence 'to lift, raise'.

подниматься.etymology: Formed by adding the reflexive-intransitive postfix -ся to поднимать ('to lift, raise'): 'to raise oneself, rise, climb, or go upstairs'.

поднос.etymology: Formed in Russian as a prefixal-stem instrument noun from подносить / поднести ('to carry up to, present, serve to guests', from под- 'up to, under' + носить / нести 'to carry'): 'a flat tray used to carry and serve food or drinks'.

поднять.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic подъяти / подъняти ('to lift from underneath'), from Proto-Slavic *podъjęti, combining the prefix *podъ- ('under, from below') with the verb *jęti ('to take, grasp', PIE *h₁em-; compare взять and принять). The -н- arose by reanalysis of historic prepositional combinations and spread across the paradigm.
поднять.notes: Future tense uses the stem *подним-*: *я подниму, ты поднимешь, они поднимут*.

подняться.etymology: Formed from поднять ('to lift, raise') + the reflexive/intransitive suffix -ся: literally 'to raise oneself', hence 'to rise, climb, or go upstairs'.

подобный.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic and Old Church Slavonic подобьнъ ('fitting, similar'), derived from подоба ('likeness, suitability, manner'), from по- + доба ('fitting time, proper way', Proto-Slavic *doba).

подобрать.etymology: Formed with prefix подо- ('from under, up') from брать ('to take, gather'), inherited from Old East Slavic бърати, from Proto-Slavic *bьrati.

history.meaning: to pick up; to select, to find a match

подогнать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix подо- (variant of под- 'up to, close') + гнать ('to drive', from Old East Slavic гънати, Proto-Slavic *gъnati).

history.meaning: to bring (a car) round; to fit, adjust; (colloq.) to procure

подогнуть.etymology: Formed with prefix подо- ('under') from гнуть ('to bend'), inherited from Old East Slavic гънути, from Proto-Slavic *gъbnǫti ('to bend, fold').

history.meaning: to tuck in, hem, bend under

подождать.etymology: Formed in Russian as the standard perfective of ждать ('to wait') by prefixing подо- (the prevocalic/cluster variant of под-). The base verb comes from Old East Slavic жьдати (Proto-Slavic *žьdati); the lost weak yer ь in жьдати triggered the vowel o in the prefix подо-.

подозреваемый.etymology: Substantivized present passive participle of подозревать ('to suspect', from Old Church Slavonic подъзрѣвати, from подъ- 'from under' + зрѣти 'to look', Proto-Slavic *zьrěti).

подозревать.etymology: Borrowed from or modeled on Old Church Slavonic подъзрѣвати ('to look askance from underneath, suspect', a loan translation of Latin suspicere 'to look up/under at, suspect', from sub- 'under' + specere 'to look'), from подо- ('under') + зреть ('to look', Proto-Slavic *zьrěti).

подозреваться.etymology: Passive/reflexive form in -ся of подозревать ('to suspect'), borrowed from Old Church Slavonic подозрѣвати ('to look askance/from under at, suspect'), from под- ('under') + зрѣти ('to look', Proto-Slavic *zьrěti).

подозрение.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic подъзьрѣниѥ ('suspicion, looking askance'), verbal noun from подъзьрѣти ('to peer at from underneath, suspect', from подъ- 'under' + зьрѣти / зреть 'to look, gaze', Proto-Slavic *zьrěti), formed as a calque of Latin suspīciō (from sub- 'from under' + specere 'to look') / Ancient Greek ὑποψία.

подозрительно.etymology: Adverbial and predicate form in -о of подозрительный ('suspicious'), derived from подозревать / подозрение ('to suspect / suspicion'), an Old Church Slavonic-modelled formation built on под- ('under, from beneath') + зрѣти ('to look, peer', from Proto-Slavic *zьrěti, calquing Latin suspicere 'to look up at from beneath, suspect').

подозрительный.etymology: Adjective formed from подозрение / подозревать ('to suspect'), borrowed from Old Church Slavonic подозрѣти ('to look from under at, suspect'), from под- ('under') + зрѣти ('to look, see', Proto-Slavic *zьrěti).

подойти.etymology: Perfective verb formed from the prefix под- / подо- ('under, up to, near') and идти ('to go, walk'), continuing Old East Slavic подъити and Proto-Slavic *podъjьti ('to approach, walk up to').

history.meaning: to walk under or up to
to approach, come up to; to suit

подоконник.etymology: Transparent Russian spatial compound built from под- ('under, at the base of') + окно ('window') + -ник: the sill or ledge set directly beneath the window frame.

подольше.etymology: Attenuative comparative formed with prefix по- ('a bit, somewhat') + дольше (comparative of долгий 'long', from Old East Slavic дългыи, Proto-Slavic *dьlgъ).

подонок.etymology: Singular noun back-formed from plural подонки ('dregs, sediment at the bottom of a cask; figuratively the dregs of society'), formed from под- ('under, at the bottom') + дно ('bottom', stem дон-, Proto-Slavic *dъno) + suffix -ок.

history.meaning: sediment, dregs at the bottom; dregs of society

подорвать.etymology: Formed with prefix подо- ('from under') from рвать ('to tear, blast'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *rъvati ('to tear, rend').

подошва.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic подъшьва ('sole of a shoe or foot'), from Proto-Slavic *podъšьva, formed from prefix *podъ- ('under') + *šьva ('that which is sewn', from *šiti 'to sew'), literally 'what is sewn underneath'.

history.meaning: sole of a boot or foot
shoe sole; foot of a mountain

подпереть.etymology: Formed with the prefix под- ('under, from beneath') + переть ('to press, push, prop', from Old East Slavic перети and Proto-Slavic *perti).

history.meaning: to prop up, brace, shore up

подписать.etymology: Formed from под- ('under, at the bottom of') + писать ('to write', Proto-Slavic *pisati): 'to write one's name underneath a document, to sign' (parallel to Latin subscribere and German unterschreiben).

rootFamily.gloss: to sign one's name (in a register)

подписаться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of подписать ('to sign, write underneath'), formed from под- ('under') + писать ('to write', from Proto-Slavic *pisati).

history.meaning: to sign, put one's signature; subscribe

подписка.etymology: Deverbal noun formed with the suffix -ка from подписать ('to sign underneath, subscribe'), built from под- ('under') + писать ('to write', Proto-Slavic *pьsati). Like Latin subscriptiō ('writing underneath'), подписка means both a periodical 'subscription' and a 'signed legal undertaking' (most famously in подписка о невыезде 'a signed undertaking not to leave town while under investigation').

подписчик.etymology: Agent noun formed from подписаться / подписываться ('to sign underneath, subscribe to a periodical', from prefix под- 'under' + писать 'to write', Proto-Slavic *pьsati) + agent suffix -чик.

подписывать.etymology: Imperfective verb formed with the suffix -ывать from подписать ('to sign, write underneath'), built on prefix под- ('under, at the bottom of a document') + писать ('to write', from Proto-Slavic *pьsati).

подпись.etymology: Deverbal feminine noun formed from подписать ('to sign, write underneath'), built from prefix под- ('under') + писать ('to write'): literally 'an under-writing' (a structural parallel to Latin subscriptiō and German Unterschrift).

подполковник.etymology: Compound military rank formed from prefix под- ('under, deputy to', calquing German Oberstleutnant / French lieutenant-colonel) + полковник ('colonel, commander of a regiment', from полк 'regiment, host', Proto-Slavic *pъlkъ).

подпольный.etymology: Prepositional-prefixal adjective formed from под- ('under') + пол ('floor', Proto-Slavic *polъ; compare подполье 'cellar space beneath the floorboards') + adjectival suffix -ный.

history.meaning: space under the floor; revolutionary underground

подпускать.etymology: Imperfective verb formed with prefix под- ('up close') + пускать ('to let go, allow', from Old East Slavic пускати, Proto-Slavic *puskati).

history.meaning: to let near, allow to approach

подработать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix под- ('additionally, on the side') + работать ('to work', from работа 'work', Proto-Slavic *orbota).

подработка.etymology: Deverbal noun formed from подработать / подрабатывать ('to earn extra on the side', from под- + работать) + nominal suffix -ка.

history.meaning: to earn extra on the side

подраться.etymology: Reciprocal perfective verb formed with prefix по- + драться ('to fight, brawl', originally 'to tear at each other', reflexive of драть 'to tear, flay', from Proto-Slavic *dьrati).

history.meaning: to fight, have a brawl, scuffle

подробно.etymology: Adverb formed from подробный ('detailed'), originally 'divided into small pieces/particles', derived from по- + дробь ('small piece, fraction'), from Proto-Slavic *drobъ ('small fragment, crumb').

подробность.etymology: Abstract noun in -ость formed from подробный ('detailed, minute'), derived from по- + дробь ('small particle, fragment', from Proto-Slavic *drobъ).

подробный.etymology: Adjective formed with prefix по- from дробный / дробить ('divided into small parts / to break into small pieces', from дробь 'small pieces, fraction', Proto-Slavic *drobь), literally 'broken down item by item'.

подросток.etymology: Derived in Russian from подрасти / подросток ('one who is growing up', formed from prefix под- 'up from under, somewhat' + расти / рост 'to grow, growth', Proto-Slavic *orsti) + noun suffix -ок.

history.meaning: to grow up somewhat; young growth

подруга.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic подруга ('female companion, friend, wife'), feminine counterpart of подругъ ('companion'), formed from по- + друг ('friend, other', from Proto-Slavic *drugъ).

подружиться.etymology: Prefixed perfective verb formed from по- + дружиться / дружить ('to be friends'), derived from друг ('friend', inherited from Old East Slavic другъ, Proto-Slavic *drugъ).

подружка.etymology: Diminutive noun formed from подруга ('female friend', from Old East Slavic подруга, Proto-Slavic *podruga, feminine counterpart of *podrugъ / *drugъ 'companion, friend') + diminutive suffix -ка.

подряд.etymology: Adverbialized prepositional phrase formed from под ('under, along') + ряд ('row, order, sequence'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *rędъ ('row, order').

подсиживать.etymology: Secondary imperfective verb formed from подсидеть ('to lie in wait for; figuratively to scheme against a colleague in order to take their seat or post'), from prefix под- ('under, in ambush') + сидеть ('to sit', Proto-Slavic *sěděti).

history.meaning: to ambush; to scheme for someone's post
to scheme to take someone's job

подсказать.etymology: Prefixed perfective verb formed from под- ('quietly, on the side, in support') + сказать ('to say, tell', from Old East Slavic съказати, Proto-Slavic *sъkazati): originally 'to whisper a forgotten line to a student or actor', and hence 'to prompt, suggest, give a tip'.

history.meaning: to whisper a prompt, suggest, tell

подсказка.etymology: Formed with the noun suffix -ка from подсказать ('to prompt, whisper an answer, give a hint'), built on под- ('under, quietly on the side') + сказать ('to say, tell', from Proto-Slavic *sъkazati).

history.meaning: to prompt, hint → clue, hint, prompt

morphemes.meaning: quietly from below / on the side

подсказывать.etymology: Secondary imperfective verb formed from подсказать ('to whisper a prompt, suggest', from prefix под- 'quietly, in support' + сказать 'to say, tell', Proto-Slavic *sъkazati) + imperfective suffix -ывать.

подслушать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix под- ('secretly, surreptitiously') + слушать ('to listen', from Old East Slavic слушати, Proto-Slavic *slušati).

подслушивать.etymology: Imperfective of подслушать ('to eavesdrop, overhear'), formed from под- ('secretly, from near or underneath') + слушать ('to listen', inherited from Old East Slavic слушати, Proto-Slavic *slušati, related to слух 'hearing').

подсобка.etymology: Colloquial univerbation formed with the suffix -ка from подсобное помещение ('auxiliary room, utility/storage room'), from подсобный ('auxiliary, helping'), derived from the verb подсобить ('to help out, lend a hand', built on под- + older собь 'one's own self or property', related to себя).

history.meaning: utility/auxiliary room → back room, storage room

подсознание.etymology: Coined in late 19th-century psychology as a loan translation of French subconscient / German Unterbewusstsein, formed from prefix под- ('under, sub-') + сознание ('consciousness', from сознать).

подстава.etymology: Colloquial deverbal noun formed from подставить ('to set someone up, frame, expose to a blow', from prefix под- 'under' + ставить 'to place, set', Proto-Slavic *staviti).

history.meaning: to place under; to frame, set up

подставить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix под- ('under') + ставить ('to place, put, set upright', from Old East Slavic ставити, Proto-Slavic *staviti); the colloquial sense 'to frame, betray' comes from placing someone under a blow (подставить под удар).

history.meaning: to put under; (colloq.) to set up, frame

подставка.etymology: Formed in Russian with the object suffix -ка from подставить ('to set or place underneath as a support', from под- 'under' + ставить 'to stand, place'): 'a stand, base, coaster, or holder'.

подставлять.etymology: Imperfective verb formed from подставить ('to place under; to frame or expose to danger', from под- + ставить, Proto-Slavic *staviti) + imperfective suffix -ять.

history.meaning: to place under; to set up
to set up, expose; to put under

подстраховать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix под- ('in support, as backup') + страховать ('to insure, belay against risk', derived from страх 'fear, risk', Proto-Slavic *straxъ, modeled on German versichern / French assurer).

подстроить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix под- ('alongside; secretly, cunningly') + строить ('to build, arrange, contrive', from Old East Slavic строити, Proto-Slavic *strojiti).

history.meaning: to build onto; to set up, engineer maliciously

подсудимый.etymology: Substantivized adjective formed from под ('under [the jurisdiction of]') + суд ('court, trial', from Proto-Slavic *sǫdъ) + participial/adjectival suffix -имый.

подсунуть.etymology: Formed with prefix под- ('under, surreptitiously') from сунуть ('to shove, thrust, slip'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *sunǫti ('to push, thrust').

history.meaning: to slip under, to palm off on someone

подсчёт.etymology: Deverbal noun formed from подсчитать / подсчитывать ('to count up, tally at the bottom', from prefix под- 'under, up' + считать / счёт 'count', Proto-Slavic *sъčetъ).

подсыпать.etymology: Verb formed with prefix под- ('in addition; surreptitiously') + сыпать ('to pour, strew, sprinkle dry material', from Old East Slavic сыпати, Proto-Slavic *sypati).

подтвердить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix под- ('in support') + твердить ('to make firm, affirm', from твёрдый 'firm, solid, hard', Old East Slavic твьрдыи, Proto-Slavic *tvьrdъ, calquing Latin cōnfirmāre 'to make firm').

подтверждать.etymology: Borrowed with Old Church Slavonic жд (< *dj) from подътверждати (imperfective of подтвердить 'to confirm, corroborate'), formed from под- ('under, supporting') + твердить / твёрдый ('firm, solid', Proto-Slavic *tvьrdъ).

подтянуть.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix под- ('up, tighter') + тянуть ('to pull, draw', from Old East Slavic тягнути, Proto-Slavic *tęgnǫti).

подумать.etymology: Formed from the perfectivizing/delimitative prefix по- + думать ('to think', Old East Slavic думати, from дума 'thought, counsel', an early Proto-Slavic borrowing from Proto-Germanic *dōmaz 'judgment, thought', cognate with English doom and deem).

history.meaning: to think, give some thought to

подуть.etymology: Formed with the perfective and inchoative prefix по- added to дуть ('to blow'). The base verb descends from Old East Slavic дути and Proto-Slavic *dǫti ('to blow, swell'), ultimately from the Proto-Indo-European root *dʰewH- ('to blow, smoke, rise in a cloud'). It is related to Russian дым ('smoke') and дух ('spirit, breath').

history.meaning: to blow briefly, begin to blow

подушка.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic подушька (Proto-Slavic *podušьka, from *poduxa). Etymologists trace it to *duxъ 'breath, air' via the idea of something puffed up or stuffed with down, though popular tradition has long reinterpreted it as под ухо ('under the ear').

подхватить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix под- ('up from below') + хватить ('to grasp, seize, catch', from Old East Slavic хватити, Proto-Slavic *xvatiti).

history.meaning: to pick up, catch; to join in

подход.etymology: Deverbal noun formed by zero-suffixation from подходить ('to walk up to, approach', from prefix под- + ходить 'to go, walk', Proto-Slavic *xodъ / *xoditi).

подходить.etymology: Formed from prefix под- ('up to, close to') + ходить ('to walk, go'). Means both literally 'to walk up to, approach' (подходить к окну) and figuratively 'to fit, suit, be right for' (этот ключ подходит 'this key fits').

history.meaning: to walk up to, approach; to suit, fit

подходящий.etymology: Present active participle of подходить ('to approach; to fit, suit'), formed from под- ('up to') + ходить ('to go', from Proto-Slavic *xoditi).

подчинение.etymology: Verbal noun from подчинить ('to subordinate, place under someone's rank'), formed from под- ('under') + чин ('rank, order'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *činъ ('order, rank, arrangement').

подчиняться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective verb formed from подчинять ('to subordinate, place under someone's rank or authority', from prefix под- 'under' + чин 'rank, order', Proto-Slavic *činъ) + reflexive particle -ся.

подчинённый.etymology: Substantivized past passive participle of подчинить ('to subordinate, place under someone's command', from prefix под- 'under' + чин 'rank, order', Proto-Slavic *činъ).

подчищать.etymology: Imperfective verb (with palatalization *stj > щ) formed from подчистить ('to clean up thoroughly, erase traces', from prefix под- + чистить 'to clean', Proto-Slavic *čistiti).

подшутить.etymology: Formed with prefix под- ('slightly, slyly') from шутить ('to joke, jest'), derived from шут ('jester, fool'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *šutъ.

history.meaning: to play a prank, to tease

подъезд.etymology: Deverbal noun from подъехать / подъезжать ('to drive up to'), formed from под- ('up to') + езд (from ехать / ездить 'to ride, drive', Proto-Slavic *ězdъ), originally 'carriage approach to a building entrance'.

подъезжать.etymology: Imperfective of подъехать ('to drive up to, approach'), formed with prefix под- ('up to') from езжать / ездить ('to ride, drive'), from Proto-Slavic *ězditi.

подъехать.etymology: Formed from the prefix под- ('up to, approaching closely', spelled with hard sign ъ before iotated е) + ехать ('to go by vehicle, ride', from Proto-Slavic *jěxati): 'to drive or ride right up to a place'.

подъём.etymology: Deverbal noun from поднять / поднимать (older подъять, Old East Slavic подъѩти 'to lift up, raise', from подъ- 'under, up' + Proto-Slavic *jęti / *jьm- 'to take'), showing the regular East Slavic vocalization of *-jьmъ to -ём.

history.meaning: lifting, ascent, upswing; reveille ('rise and shine!')

rootFamily.gloss: to go up, rise, get up

подыграть.etymology: Formed with prefix под- ('accompanying, supporting') from играть ('to play'), inherited from Old East Slavic играти, from Proto-Slavic *jьgrati ('to play').

history.meaning: to accompany on an instrument; to play along

подышать.etymology: Delimitative perfective verb formed with prefix по- ('for a while') + дышать ('to breathe', from Old East Slavic дышати, Proto-Slavic *dyšati).

history.meaning: to breathe (for a while), get some air

поединок.etymology: Borrowed in the 17th century via Polish pojedynek ('single combat, duel'), formed from po- + jedyn / един ('one, single', Proto-Slavic *jedinъ) + suffix -ek / -ок, literally 'one-on-one fight'.

поезд.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic поѣздъ ('a riding out, wedding or princely cortege'), a deverbal noun from поехать / ездить ('to ride, travel'). In the 19th century it was adopted for a railway train, parallel to French train and German Zug.

поездить.etymology: Delimitative perfective verb formed with prefix по- ('for a while') + ездить ('to ride, travel by vehicle', from Old East Slavic ѣздити, Proto-Slavic *ězditi).

history.meaning: to ride around, travel (for a while)

поездка.etymology: Formed in Russian with the action-noun suffix -ка from поездить / поехать ('to travel, take a ride'), built on ездить / ехать ('to ride, travel by vehicle', from Proto-Slavic *ězditi / *ěxati).

поезжать.etymology: Formed with prefix по- ('setting off') from езжать, iterative of ездить ('to ride, go by vehicle'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *ězditi (used in modern Russian primarily in the imperative поезжай).

history.meaning: to go, to drive, to set off

поесть.etymology: Formed with prefix по- ('some, a meal') from есть (ем, 'to eat'), inherited from Old East Slavic ѣсти, from Proto-Slavic *ěsti ('to eat', from PIE *h₁ed-).

history.meaning: to eat, to have a meal

поехать.etymology: Perfective verb formed by adding the inceptive prefix по- ('setting off, starting an action') to ехать ('to go by vehicle, ride'), inherited from Old East Slavic ѣхати, from Proto-Slavic *ěxati ('to ride, travel').

history.meaning: to go by vehicle, set off

пожалеть.etymology: Perfective verb formed with the prefix по- and жалеть ('to feel sorry for, pity; to regret, spare'), derived from жаль ('pity, sorrow'), inherited from Old East Slavic жаль ('grief, sorrow, compassion; grave mound') and Proto-Slavic *žalь ('sharp pain, grief', cognate with Lithuanian gėla 'sharp pain').

history.meaning: to take pity on; to regret

rootFamily.gloss: it's a pity; feel sorry for

пожаловать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic пожаловати ('to show favour, grant, deign to visit'), formed from по- + жаловать ('to favour, hold dear, reward', related to жаль 'pity, affection'). Today used chiefly in the traditional hospitality greeting Добро пожаловать! ('Welcome!', literally 'deign to come in kindness!') and in пожалуйста ('please').

history.meaning: to grant favour, deign to visit
to come as an honoured guest, welcome

пожалуй.etymology: Fossilized 2nd-person singular imperative (пожалуй 'be so gracious as to grant!') of пожаловать ('to grant, bestow favor, show mercy'), formed from по- + жаловать ('to favor, feel affection/pity for', from Proto-Slavic *žalovati, related to жаль). Just as пожалуй + ста ('be so kind, sir') fused into пожалуйста ('please'), bare пожалуй grammaticalized as a parenthetical discourse particle meaning 'if you please → I suppose, perhaps, probably'.

history.meaning: be so gracious as to grant!

пожалуйста.etymology: Formed by fusing older пожалуй (imperative of пожаловать, 'be so kind, grant a favour', related to жаловать) with the old deferential enclitic particle -ста. While the first half clearly asks for gracious favour, Vasmer notes that the exact origin of the particle -ста (linked variously to сударь or old forms of стать/быть) remains debated.
пожалуйста.notes: Covers 'please', 'you're welcome', and 'here you go' when handing something over.

пожар.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic пожаръ ('conflagration, blaze'), formed with prefix по- from жар ('glowing heat, embers'), from Proto-Slavic *požarъ (lengthened-grade derivative of *gorěti 'to burn').

пожарить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix по- + жарить ('to fry, roast', derived from жар 'heat, glowing embers', from Proto-Slavic *žarъ, long-grade derivative of *gorěti 'to burn').

пожарный.etymology: Relational adjective (and substantivized noun meaning 'firefighter') formed with the suffix -ный from пожар ('destructive fire, conflagration'), inherited from Old East Slavic пожаръ, built on по- + жар ('glowing heat, embers', Proto-Slavic *žarъ, related by palatalization to гореть 'to burn').

пожать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic пожати ('to press, squeeze'), formed with prefix по- + жать ('to press, squeeze', from Proto-Slavic *žęti, 1sg *žьmǫ, PIE *gʷem- 'to press together').

пожелание.etymology: Verbal noun formed from пожелать ('to wish', from prefix по- + желать 'to wish, desire', Old East Slavic желати, Proto-Slavic *želati) + abstract suffix -ние.

пожелать.etymology: Prefixed perfective verb formed from по- + желать ('to wish, desire'), inherited from Old East Slavic желати / желѣти, from Proto-Slavic *želati / *želěti ('to wish, long for').

пожениться.etymology: Reciprocal perfective verb formed with prefix по- + жениться ('to marry, take a wife', derived from жена 'wife, woman', Proto-Slavic *žena, PIE *gʷḗn).

пожертвовать.etymology: Perfective formed with prefix по- from жертвовать ('to sacrifice, donate'), derived from жертва ('sacrifice, offering'), borrowed from Old Church Slavonic жрьтва (from Proto-Slavic *žьrtva 'sacrifice, praise').

history.meaning: to sacrifice, to give up; to donate

поживать.etymology: Attenuative-frequentative imperfective verb formed with prefix по- + живать (frequentative of жить 'to live', from Proto-Slavic *živati / *žiti).

history.meaning: to be getting on, be doing

пожилой.etymology: Formed in Russian from the past/participial stem of пожить ('to have lived for a good while', from по- + жить 'to live') with stressed adjectival ending -ой: literally 'having lived a fair span of years, advanced in age'.
пожилой.notes: **Пожилой** is a polite, respectful everyday word for an older or elderly person (*пожилой человек*, *пожилая дама*).

morphemes.meaning: for a while, a fair amount

пожить.etymology: Prefixed perfective verb formed from the delimitative prefix по- ('for a while') + жить ('to live'), inherited from Old East Slavic жити, from Proto-Slavic *žiti ('to live'), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷih₃w- (cognate with Latin vīvere and English quick).

history.meaning: to live for a while, stay

позаботиться.etymology: Perfective formed with prefix по- from заботиться ('to care for, worry about'), derived from забота ('care, concern, anxiety'), related to зобать ('to peck, eat, gnaw at').

history.meaning: to take care of, look after

позавидовать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix по- + завидовать ('to envy', derived from зависть / завидеть 'envy / to look askance at', from prefix за- + видеть 'to see, look', Proto-Slavic *zaviděti, a semantic parallel to Latin invidēre).

позавтракать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix по- + завтракать ('to eat breakfast', derived from завтрак 'breakfast', originally заутрок 'meal taken in the early morning *za utra', from утро 'morning').

позавчера.etymology: Formed in Russian from the compound prefix поза- ('behind, beyond, before', from по- + за) + вчера ('yesterday', Old East Slavic вьчера, originally an old genitive/locative of вечер 'evening', Proto-Slavic *večerъ): literally 'the day behind yesterday'.

позади.etymology: Formed in East Slavic from the prefix/preposition по- + зади (locative singular of задъ 'back, rear part', from Proto-Slavic *zadъ): literally 'along/at the back of, behind'.

позаниматься.etymology: Delimitative perfective verb formed with prefix по- ('for a while') + заниматься ('to occupy oneself with, study, exercise', from занимать 'to occupy', Proto-Slavic *zajьmati).

позапрошлый.etymology: Formed in Russian by prefixing поза- ('behind, beyond the immediately preceding one', from по- + за) to прошлый ('past, last'): 'the one before last' (позапрошлый год 'the year before last', позапрошлая неделя 'the week before last').

позвать.etymology: Formed from the perfectivizing prefix по- + звать ('to call, invite', Old East Slavic зъвати, Proto-Slavic *zъvati, cognate with Sanskrit hváyati 'calls, invokes').
позвать.notes: Future tense inserts a fleeting -о- in the root: я позову, ты позовёшь, они позовут.

позволение.etymology: Verbal noun formed from позволить ('to allow, permit', borrowed in the 17th century via Polish pozwolić, from po- + wolić / wola 'will', Proto-Slavic *voľa) + abstract suffix -ение.

позволить.etymology: Adopted into early modern East Slavic and Russian via Polish pozwolić ('to permit, grant consent'), formed from po- + zwolić ('to agree, consent', from z- + wola 'will'), ultimately from Proto-Slavic *voľa ('will, wish, choice') and Proto-Indo-European *welh₁- ('to wish, choose').
позволить.notes: Takes the dative of the person allowed (позвольте вам помочь, 'let me help you') and forms позволить себе ('to afford' or 'to allow oneself').

позволять.etymology: Imperfective of позволить ('to allow, permit'), borrowed in the 17th century via Polish pozwolić ('to permit, consent'), formed from po- + wolić (from wola 'will', Proto-Slavic *voľa).

позвонить.etymology: Formed as the perfective counterpart of звонить ('to ring, call by phone') with the prefix по-. The base verb comes from Old East Slavic звонити ('to ring a bell, resound'), built on звон ('ringing sound', from Proto-Slavic *zvonъ).

history.meaning: to ring, make a phone call (perfective)

позвоночник.etymology: Anatomical noun formed from позвонок ('vertebra', derived from звено 'chain link, segment', Proto-Slavic *zveno) + collective/structural suffix -ник, literally 'column of vertebral links'.

поздний.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic поздьнии / позьнии ('late'), formed with adjectival suffix -ний from поздо / поздно ('late', Proto-Slavic *pozdь, from PIE *pos-dʰh₁-o-, extended from *pos 'after, behind').

поздно.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic поздьно (and Old Church Slavonic поздьно, whence the -зд- spelling beside native East Slavic dialectal позно), adverb of поздний ('late'), from Proto-Slavic *pozdь / *pozdьnъ, built on the spatial/temporal root *po- ('after, behind'; compare после and Latin post).
поздно.notes: The middle consonant *-д-* is silent in pronunciation (pronounced [позна]).

поздновато.etymology: Attenuative adverb formed from поздно ('late', Proto-Slavic *pozdьno) + attenuative suffix -овато ('somewhat, a bit too').

поздороваться.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed with prefix по- + здороваться ('to greet, wish good health', derived from здоровый 'healthy' / здорово! 'hello!', from Proto-Slavic *sъdorvъ).

поздравить.etymology: Adopted with the South Slavic / Church Slavonic stem здрав- (compare native East Slavic здоров- in здоровый) from поздравити, originally meaning 'to wish someone good health (здравие)', built on по- + здравый ('healthy, sound', Proto-Slavic *sъdorvъ): from wishing health on a feast day or birthday, it generalized to 'to congratulate'.

history.meaning: to wish good health -> to congratulate

поздравить.notes: Takes the accusative of the person and с + instrumental for the occasion: поздравить друга с днём рождения ('to wish a friend a happy birthday').

поздравление.etymology: Verbal noun formed from поздравить ('to congratulate, wish good health', containing Church Slavonic non-pleophonic -здрав- from Proto-Slavic *sъdorvъ 'healthy') + suffix -ение.

поздравлять.etymology: Formed as the imperfective counterpart of поздравить ('to congratulate', literally 'to wish good health') with the suffix -лять (including labial epenthesis в -> вл).

позеленеть.etymology: Perfective inchoative verb formed with prefix по- + зеленеть ('to become green', derived from зелёный 'green', Old East Slavic зеленыи, Proto-Slavic *zelenъ).

позже.etymology: Comparative degree ('later') of поздний / поздно ('late'), formed from the stem позд- (Old East Slavic поздо / поздьнъ, Proto-Slavic *pozdъ, built on *po- 'after') with palatalization before the comparative suffix *-je.

позиция.etymology: Borrowed in the Petrine era via Polish pozycja and German Position from Latin positiō, accusative positiōnem ('placing, situation, position', from pōnere, past participle positus 'to place, put').

позлить.etymology: Formed with prefix по- ('for a while, a bit') from злить ('to anger, make mad'), derived from злой ('angry, evil, wicked'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *zъlъ.

history.meaning: to anger, to tease, to annoy

познакомить.etymology: Perfective formed with prefix по- from знакомить ('to acquaint, introduce'), derived from знакомый ('acquainted, familiar'), from знать ('to know', Proto-Slavic *znati).

познакомиться.etymology: Perfective reflexive verb formed with the prefix по- from знакомиться ('to get acquainted'), derived from знакомый ('familiar, acquainted'), originally a passive participle in -м- from Old East Slavic знакъ ('sign, mark') and знати / знать ('to know', from Proto-Slavic *znati, PIE *ǵneh₃-).

позор.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic позоръ ('spectacle, public view; later public pillorying, shame, disgrace'), from Proto-Slavic *pozorъ, formed from prefix *po- + *zorъ (o-grade of *zьrěti 'to look, gaze'); the sense 'disgrace' arose from exposing offenders to public view.

позорить.etymology: Denominal verb formed from позор ('shame, disgrace, originally public spectacle', from Proto-Slavic *pozorъ) + verbal suffix -ить.

позориться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective verb formed from позорить ('to disgrace, put to shame', from позор 'disgrace') + reflexive particle -ся.

поиграть.etymology: Delimitative perfective formed with prefix по- ('for a while') from играть ('to play'), inherited from Old East Slavic играти, from Proto-Slavic *jьgrati ('to play').

поиск.etymology: Deverbal noun from поискать ('to search for, seek'), built on по- + искать ('to look for, seek', inherited from Old East Slavic искати, from Proto-Slavic *jьskati, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eys- 'to seek', cognate with English ask and German heischen).

поискать.etymology: Delimitative perfective formed with prefix по- ('for a while, a bit') from искать (ищу, 'to seek, look for'), inherited from Old East Slavic искати, from Proto-Slavic *jьskati.

history.meaning: to look for, to search a bit

поить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic поити ('to give to drink, water livestock'), from Proto-Slavic *pojiti, o-grade causative of *piti ('to drink', PIE *peh₃(y)-).

history.meaning: to cause to drink, give to drink
to give to drink; to ply with drinks

поймать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic поимати ('to take, seize, catch'), formed from the perfective prefix по- and имати ('to take, grasp, catch', from Proto-Slavic *jьmati, iterative of *jęti 'to take', with initial *jь- coalescing after the vowel of по- into пой-).

morphemes.meaning: take, seize (from Old East Slavic имати)

поймать.notes: Forms an aspectual pair with **ловить** (impf. 'to try to catch, be catching') / **поймать** (pf. 'to catch').

пойти.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic поити, from Proto-Slavic *pojiti ('to set off walking, start going'), formed from the inchoative/perfective prefix *po- + *iti (Russian идти 'to go on foot').
пойти.notes: Uses the suppletive past tense stem *пошёл, пошла, пошли* and future *пойду, пойдёшь*.

пока.etymology: Shortened in East Slavic from older покамѣстъ ('for the time being, while, until'), formed from the distributive preposition по + the pronominal stem ка- ('which, what': originally 'up to what point / while'). The colloquial farewell Пока! ('Bye! / See you for now!') developed in the 20th century as an ellipsis of Пока до свидания ('Goodbye for now').

history.meaning: up to what point, while, for now

показ.etymology: Deverbal noun formed by zero-suffixation from показать ('to show, display', from prefix по- + казать 'to show', Old East Slavic показати, Proto-Slavic *pokazati).

показание.etymology: Verbal noun formed from показать ('to show, declare, testify', from Old East Slavic показати, Proto-Slavic *pokazati) + abstract suffix -ние.

показатель.etymology: Agent and instrument noun formed from показать ('to show, indicate', from по- + казать, Proto-Slavic *pokazati) + suffix -тель.

показать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic показати and Proto-Slavic *pokazati ('to show, point out, instruct'), formed from по- + казать ('to show, declare', Proto-Slavic *kazati).
показать.notes: Future tense shows з -> ж palatalization: я покажу, ты покажешь.

показаться.etymology: Formed from показать ('to show', from по- + казать 'to show, point out', Proto-Slavic *kazati) + the reflexive suffix -ся: literally 'to show oneself', whence both 'to come into view, appear' and 'to seem, strike someone as'.
показаться.notes: With a dative experiencer (*мне показалось, что...*) it means 'it seemed to me that...'.

показывать.etymology: Formed in Russian as the imperfective counterpart of показать ('to show') with the productive imperfective suffix -ывать.

покалечить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix по- + калечить ('to cripple, maim', derived from калека 'cripple', Old East Slavic калѣка, traditionally derived either from калики перехожие 'wandering pilgrims wearing sandals *kaligy' from Byzantine Greek καλίγια / Latin caliga, or from Turkic qalïq 'maimed, defective').

покатать.etymology: Delimitative perfective verb formed with prefix по- ('for a while') + катать ('to roll, take for a drive or ride', iterative of катить, from Proto-Slavic *katati).

history.meaning: to roll, take for a ride

покататься.etymology: Reflexive delimitative perfective verb formed from покатать ('to take for a ride', from по- + катать, Proto-Slavic *katati) + reflexive particle -ся.

покер.etymology: Borrowed in the late 19th or 20th century from English poker (the American card game attested from the 1830s, probably influenced by French poque and German Poch, bluffing card games).

покидать.etymology: Imperfective verb formed with prefix по- + кидать ('to throw, cast; in prefixed forms, to cast behind, abandon', from Proto-Slavic *kydati).

покинуть.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic покинути ('to cast away, drop, forsake'), formed from по- + кинуть ('to throw, cast', from Proto-Slavic *kynǫti). From 'to throw down or cast aside' developed the standard modern meaning 'to leave, vacate, abandon'.

поклониться.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic поклонитися and Proto-Slavic *pokloniti sę ('to bend oneself down, bow in greeting or reverence'), formed from по- + клонить ('to incline, bend', Proto-Slavic *kloniti) + -ся.

поклонник.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic поклонникъ ('worshipper, pilgrim who bows in reverence; later suitor, admirer, fan'), formed from поклон / поклониться ('bow / to bow down', from клонить 'to incline, bow', Proto-Slavic *kloniti) + suffix -ник.

поклонница.etymology: Feminine counterpart of поклонник ('worshipper; admirer, fan', from поклониться 'to bow down', Proto-Slavic *pokloniti sę), formed with feminine agent suffix -ница.

покой.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic покои and Proto-Slavic *pokojь ('rest, peace, quiet'), a prefixal noun built on *po- + *kojь / *počiti ('to rest, lie still', from Proto-Indo-European *kʷey- 'to rest, be quiet', cognate with Latin quiēs and English quiet).
покой.notes: Notice how in Polish (pokój) and Czech (pokoj) the sense 'resting chamber' became the everyday word for 'room', a sense preserved in older Russian царские покои ('royal apartments').

поколение.etymology: Derived in Old East Slavic / Old Church Slavonic поколѣние ('generation, tribe, lineage') from по- + колѣно ('knee; joint, node of a stem; degree of kinship, generation'), from Proto-Slavic *kolěno.

покончить.etymology: Perfective verb formed with prefix по- + кончить ('to finish, end', derived from конец 'end', Old East Slavic коньць, Proto-Slavic *konьcь).

history.meaning: to put an end to, be done with

покорить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic and Old Church Slavonic покорити ('to subjugate, humble, conquer'), formed from prefix по- + корити ('to humble, reproach, subject', from Proto-Slavic *koriti).

покориться.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed from покорить ('to subjugate, conquer', from Old East Slavic покорити, Proto-Slavic *pokoriti) + reflexive particle -ся ('to humble oneself, submit').

покормить.etymology: Formed with perfective prefix по- from кормить ('to feed, nourish'), derived from корм ('fodder, food'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *kъrmъ ('food, fodder').

покорный.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic and Old Church Slavonic покорьныи ('humble, submissive, obedient'), formed from покора / покорить ('submission / to subjugate', Proto-Slavic *pokorьnъ) + suffix -ный.

покорённый.etymology: Past passive participial adjective formed from покорить ('to conquer, subjugate; figuratively to charm, win over', Proto-Slavic *pokoriti).

покоцать.etymology: Perfective slang verb formed with prefix по- + коцать ('to nick, scratch, chip, beat'), borrowed into Russian colloquial/argot speech from Ukrainian коцати / southern dialectal коцать ('to peck, chop, beat', of expressive onomatopoeic origin).

покрасить.etymology: Formed in Russian by adding the perfectivizing prefix по- to красить ('to paint, dye', Proto-Slavic *krasiti).

покраска.etymology: Derived in Russian from покрасить ('to paint') with the action-noun suffix -ка: 'the act or process of painting, a coat/job of paint'.

покраснеть.etymology: Perfective inchoative verb formed with prefix по- + краснеть ('to become red, blush', derived from красный 'red, originally beautiful', from Proto-Slavic *krasьnъ).

покрасоваться.etymology: Delimitative perfective verb formed with prefix по- ('for a while') + красоваться ('to display one's beauty, flaunt oneself', derived from краса 'beauty', Proto-Slavic *krasa).

покрепче.etymology: Formed in Russian by adding the attenuative/comparative prefix по- ('a bit more, somewhat') to крепче ('stronger, firmer'), the comparative of крепкий ('strong, sturdy', from Proto-Slavic *krěpъkъ).

history.meaning: stronger → a bit stronger, nice and strong

покрепче.notes: Frequently used when ordering or making tea or coffee (*сделайте чай покрепче* 'make the tea a bit stronger') or tying a knot.

покровительство.etymology: Abstract noun formed from покровитель ('protector, patron', derived from покров 'cover, veil, protection', especially the Intercession and Veil of the Theotokos, from покрыть 'to cover', Proto-Slavic *pokrovъ) + suffix -ство.

покупатель.etymology: Formed in Russian from покупать ('to buy') with the agent-noun suffix -тель: 'one who buys, a buyer, customer, or shopper'.

покупать.etymology: Formed in East Slavic as the imperfective counterpart of купить ('to buy'), from по- + купать (iterative of купить, Proto-Slavic *kupiti, an early Proto-Slavic borrowing from Gothic kaupōn 'to trade, traffic', itself from Latin caupō 'merchant, innkeeper', the same source as German kaufen and English cheap).

покупка.etymology: Noun in -ка formed from покупать ('to buy'), derived with prefix по- from купать / купить ('to buy'), an early Proto-Slavic *kupiti borrowing from Gothic kaupōn ('to trade, traffic', ultimately from Latin caupō 'innkeeper, peddler').

покурить.etymology: Prefixed perfective verb formed from delimitative по- ('for a little while') + курить ('to smoke', originally 'to make smoke, burn incense, fumigate', inherited from Old East Slavic курити, Proto-Slavic *kuriti).

покусать.etymology: Perfective verb formed with distributive/completive prefix по- + кусать ('to bite', from Old East Slavic кусати, Proto-Slavic *kǫsati).

history.meaning: to bite (badly or in several places)

покушать.etymology: Delimitative perfective verb formed with prefix по- + кушать ('to eat, taste', from Old East Slavic кушати 'to taste, try', Proto-Slavic *kušati, an early borrowing from Gothic kausjan 'to taste, test').

history.meaning: to have a bite to eat

покушение.etymology: Verbal noun formed from покуситься / покушаться ('to attempt, make an attempt on', from prefix по- + куситься 'to try, test', from Proto-Slavic *kusiti 'to taste, test, try', an early borrowing from Gothic kausjan) + suffix -ение.
