путник.etymology: Derived with the agentive suffix -ник from путь ('way, road, journey'), inherited from Old East Slavic путь and Proto-Slavic *pǫtь ('path, way'). The Slavic noun descends from the Proto-Indo-European root *pent- ('to tread, go, pass; path, bridge'). It is directly cognate with Latin pōns ('bridge'), Ancient Greek πάτος (pátos, 'path'), and English find.

cognates.meaning: to come upon by treading a path (from PGmc *finþaną < PIE *pent-)

путь.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic путь and Proto-Slavic *pǫtь 'way, road, journey', from Proto-Indo-European *pontohs 'crossing, path', cognate with Latin pons ('bridge') and Sanskrit pantha ('road, path').
путь.notes: Unique masculine noun in Russian: it is masculine (добрый путь!), yet declines like a feminine -ь noun except in the instrumental singular (путём).

путёвка.etymology: Noun in -ка formed from путёвый / путевой ('relating to a road, journey, or dispatch'), derived from путь ('way, road, journey'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *pǫtь ('path, way').

пух.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic пухъ ('down, fluff, puff'), from Proto-Slavic *puxъ ('breath, puff, fluff, swelling'), of onomatopoeic/expressive origin from Proto-Indo-European *pew- / *pux- ('to blow, puff, swell', cognate with пухнуть 'to swell').

пушистый.etymology: Adjective formed with suffix -истый from пух ('down, fluff, soft fur'), inherited from Old East Slavic пухъ, from Proto-Slavic *puxъ ('breath, puff, soft down', of onomatopoeic origin).

пчелиный.etymology: Possessive/relational adjective formed with the animal suffix -иный from пчела ('bee'), inherited from Old East Slavic бъчела and Proto-Slavic *bъčela ('bee', an expressive root connected with buzzing).

пыль.etymology: Inherited from East Slavic пыль ('fine floating dust'), derived from the Proto-Slavic root *pyl- / *pux- ('to blow, billow, puff up into the air', related to пылать 'to blaze' and пух 'down, fluff', or cognate with Latin pulvis 'dust').
пыль.notes: Takes the stressed locative -и after в: весь в пыли ('covered in dust').

пыльный.etymology: Derived in Russian from пыль ('dust') with the adjectival suffix -ный: 'dusty, covered with dust'.

пытать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic пытати ('to ask, inquire, investigate, test; to interrogate under torture'), from Proto-Slavic *pytati ('to inquire, search into, probe'). While its reflexive derivative пытаться kept the mild sense 'to try, attempt' (and Ukrainian питати means simply 'to ask'), non-reflexive пытать in Russian specialized in legal history (from judicial interrogation on the rack) to mean 'to torture'.

history.meaning: to ask, investigate; to question under torture

пытаться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of пытать ('to test, try, question'), inherited from Old East Slavic пытати ('to ask, investigate, strive') and Proto-Slavic *pytati.

history.meaning: to test → to try, attempt, endeavour

пьющий.etymology: Present active participle of пить ('to drink; to drink alcohol habitually', inherited from Old East Slavic пити, from Proto-Slavic *piti, from PIE *peh₃(y)- 'to drink').

пьяница.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic пияница ('drunkard'), formed with common-gender agent suffix -ица from пьяный (Old East Slavic пияныи 'drunk'), from Proto-Slavic *pьjanica (from *piti 'to drink').

пьянка.etymology: Colloquial noun in -ка formed from пьяный ('drunk, intoxicated'), inherited from Old East Slavic пияныи / пьяныи, from Proto-Slavic *pьjanъ ('drunk', old participle from *piti 'to drink').

пьянство.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic пияньство, formed with abstract suffix -ство from пьяный ('drunk'), from Proto-Slavic *pьjanъ (from *piti 'to drink').

пьяный.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic пияныи ('drunk, intoxicated'), from Proto-Slavic *pьjanъ, historically an archaic passive/stative participle in *-nъ formed from *piti ('to drink', Russian пить; compare Sanskrit pīyáte 'is drunk'), meaning 'having drunk deeply'.

пюре.etymology: Borrowed in the 19th century from French purée ('mashed vegetables or pulse, purée'), feminine past participle of Old French purer ('to purify, strain, squeeze through a sieve'), from Late Latin purare ('to purify'), from purus ('pure').

пятеро.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic пятеро, from Proto-Slavic collective numeral *pętero ('group of five'), derived from *pętь ('five', Russian пять) + collective numeral suffix *-ero (from PIE *-ero-).

пятка.etymology: Formed as the diminutive (now standard everyday form) of пята ('heel', Old East Slavic пята, Proto-Slavic *pęta 'heel'), derived from the nasal root *pęti ('to stretch, brace, kick', compare Lithuanian pentis 'heel; back of an axe blade').

rootFamily.gloss: heel (archaic/idiomatic, as in с головы до пят 'from head to toe')

пятнадцатый.etymology: Ordinal numeral formed from пятнадцать ('fifteen'), which is a contraction of the Old East Slavic phrase пѧть на десѧте ('five upon ten', from Proto-Slavic *pętь na desęte).

пятнадцать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic пять на десяте ('five upon ten'), a Proto-Slavic teen-numeral phrase (*pętь na desęte) that fused into a single word as the unstressed second part eroded to -надцать.

пятнашка.etymology: Colloquial noun derived from пятнадцать ('fifteen', from Old East Slavic пять на десяте 'five on ten') + colloquial suffix -шка, denoting fifteen units (such as 15 rubles, 15 thousand, or the 15-puzzle).

пятница.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic пятница (Old Church Slavonic пѧтьница), formed from пятый / пять ('fifth / five'). Slavic weekday names count cleanly from Monday: вторник (2nd), среда (middle), четверг (4th), пятница (5th).

пятничный.etymology: Formed in Russian from пятница ('Friday', derived from пятый 'fifth' — the fifth day of the week after Sunday, with ц -> ч before -ный) + the adjectival suffix -ный.

пятно.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic пятно ('brand mark, scar, spot'), from Proto-Slavic *pętьno ('mark, stamp, spot'), connected by Vasmer either with *pęta ('heel, footprint impression') or *pęti ('to stretch, strike, brand').

пяточка.etymology: Affectionate double diminutive derived from пятка ('heel', diminutive of пята 'heel', inherited from Old East Slavic пята, from Proto-Slavic *pęta 'heel, spur') + suffix -очка.

пятый.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic пятыи ('fifth'), from Proto-Slavic *pętъ, ordinal of *pętь ('five', Russian пять), from Proto-Indo-European *penkʷtós.

пять.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic пять (Old Church Slavonic пѧть), from Proto-Slavic *pętь ('five', originally a feminine abstract noun 'a group of five'), continuing Proto-Indo-European *pénkʷe ('five'), cognate with English five, German fünf, Ancient Greek πέντε, and Sanskrit páñca.

пятьдесят.etymology: Compound numeral inherited from Old East Slavic пять десятъ ('five tens, fifty'), from Proto-Slavic *pętь desętъ, where пять ('five') governed the archaic genitive plural десятъ ('of tens', from десять 'ten').

пятьсот.etymology: Compound numeral inherited from Old East Slavic пять сътъ ('five hundreds'), formed from пять ('five', Proto-Slavic *pętь) + сот (genitive plural of сто 'hundred', Proto-Slavic *sъto).

пятёрка.etymology: Noun formed with suffix -ёрка from пять ('five') / пятеро ('group of five'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *pętь ('five').

history.meaning: the digit five; top school grade; group of five

пёс.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic пьсъ ('dog'), from Proto-Slavic *pьsъ ('dog, hound'), widely connected with Proto-Indo-European *peyk- / *pik- ('spotted, pied', i.e. 'the spotted animal') or *pekʷ- ('livestock watcher').

пёсик.etymology: Diminutive in -ик of пёс ('dog, hound'), inherited from Old East Slavic пьсъ, from Proto-Slavic *pьsъ ('dog').

раб.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic рабъ ('slave, servant', corresponding to native East Slavic робъ with initial ро- from *or-), from Proto-Slavic *orbъ ('orphan, servant, slave'), from PIE *h₃órbʰos ('orphan; person deprived of free status', cognate with Latin orbus and German Arbeit).

работа.etymology: The older Russian form робота could mean work, servitude or bondage. Vasmer connects it with the same historical family as раб, a slave. The everyday modern meaning is work; the older senses explain a history of compelled labour.

sources.title: M. Vasmer, Etymological Dictionary — Vinogradov Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences: работа

работа.notes:
- Collocations: *найти работу* (find a job), *уйти с работы* (leave work), *на работе* (at work).
- *За работу!* is an idiomatic call to get started.

работать.etymology: Denominative verb built on работа ('work, labour'), generalizing the South Slavic / Church Slavonic initial ра- (compare Old East Slavic роботати and Czech pracovat / robotovat), ultimately from Proto-Slavic *orbota ('hard labour').

работаться.etymology: Impersonal reflexive verb derived from работать ('to work', from работа 'work', inherited from Old East Slavic робота / Old Church Slavonic работа, from Proto-Slavic *orbota) + -ся, expressing one's disposition or ease in working.

history.meaning: to feel like working, for work to go well/poorly

работающий.etymology: Present active participle of работать ('to work, function, operate', derived from работа 'work', from Proto-Slavic *orbota).

работник.etymology: Formed with the agent suffix -ник from работа ('work, labour') / работать ('to work'), continuing Old East Slavic роботьникъ and Old Church Slavonic работьникъ (with South Slavic initial ра- generalized in standard Russian), from Proto-Slavic *orbotьnikъ.

history.stage: Old East Slavic / Old Church Slavonic

работодатель.etymology: Nineteenth-century compound calque of German Arbeitgeber ('employer', literally 'work-giver'), formed from работа ('work', from Proto-Slavic *orbota) + linking vowel -о- + датель ('giver', from дать 'to give', Proto-Slavic *dati).

работящий.etymology: Colloquial adjective formed on the participial pattern -ящий from работать ('to work'), derived from работа ('work, labor'), from Proto-Slavic *orbota.

рабочий.etymology: Derived from работа ('work, labor', Old Russian робота) with palatalization of т > ч before the adjectival suffix -ий (compare Old Church Slavonic работии / рабочии). Functions both as an relational adjective ('working, work-related') and as a substantivized noun ('worker, laborer').

равиоли.etymology: Borrowed from Italian ravioli (plural of raviolo 'stuffed pasta parcel'), from Northern Italian dialectal raviöl, usually traced to Medieval Latin rabiola / rapa ('turnip, herb filling') or Italian riavvolgere ('to wrap up').

равно.etymology: Adopted with the South Slavic / Church Slavonic initial ра- (compare native East Slavic ро- in ровный 'even, straight') from Old Church Slavonic равьно ('equally, alike'), from Proto-Slavic *orvьno.

history.meaning: equally, equals; all the same (всё равно)

morphemes.meaning: equal, even (Church Slavonic doublet of ровн-)

равно.notes: Used constantly in the idiom мне всё равно ('it's all the same to me / I don't mind') and in arithmetic: два плюс два равно четыре ('two plus two equals four').

равнодушный.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic равьнодушьнъ (originally 'unanimous, of like mind', calquing Greek ἰσόψυχος, from равный 'equal, even' + душа 'soul'; later reinterpreted after French indifférent / German gleichgültig as 'even-minded, unmoved, indifferent').

history.meaning: of equal spirit; later unmoved, indifferent

равномерно.etymology: Adverb formed from равномерный ('uniform, even-measured'), compound of равный ('equal', Old Church Slavonic равьнъ) + мера ('measure', Proto-Slavic *měra).

равный.etymology: Borrowed with Old Church Slavonic initial ра- (compare native East Slavic ровный 'flat, even') from равьнъ ('flat, level, equal'), from Proto-Slavic *orvьnъ ('level, even').

рагу.etymology: Borrowed in the 18th century from French ragoût ('savory stew'), deverbal from ragoûter ('to revive the taste, whet the appetite'), from re- + à + goût ('taste', from Latin gustus).

рад.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic радъ ('glad, willing'), from Proto-Slavic *radъ ('glad, joyful, eager'). Vasmer compares Old English rōt ('glad, cheerful, noble') and Lithuanian rōds ('willing, glad'), though the deeper Indo-European root remains debated.
рад.notes: Used in modern Russian only in the short predicate forms: **рад** (m.), **рада** (f.), **рады** (pl.), governing the dative case (*я вам очень рад* 'I am very glad to see you').

ради.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic ради and Old Church Slavonic ради ('for the sake of, on account of'), from Proto-Slavic *radi, an old locative/instrumental case form connected with *radъ ('glad, willing, caring for', modern рад) and Old Persian rādiy ('on account of, for the sake of').

history.meaning: for the sake of, because of
for the sake of (governs the genitive case)

радиатор.etymology: Borrowed via German Radiator or English radiator from New Latin radiator ('that which radiates heat'), formed from Latin radiare ('to emit rays, radiate', from radius 'ray, spoke').

радовать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic радовати ('to gladden, make joyful'), derived from рад ('glad, joyful', from Old East Slavic радъ, from Proto-Slavic *radъ) + verbal suffix -овать.

радоваться.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic радоватися and Proto-Slavic *radovati sę ('to rejoice, be glad'), a denominal verb built on рад ('glad, joyful', Proto-Slavic *radъ) with the suffix -ова- and reflexive -ся.
радоваться.notes: Takes the dative case for the cause of joy: радоваться весне ('to rejoice at the spring'), радоваться успехам ('to be glad at successes').

радостно.etymology: Adverb formed from радостный ('joyful, glad'), derived from радость ('joy, gladness', Old East Slavic радость), which is built with the abstract suffix -ость on рад ('glad', Proto-Slavic *radъ).

радостный.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic and Old Church Slavonic радостьныи, formed with suffix -ный from радость ('joy, gladness'), derived from рад ('glad'), from Proto-Slavic *radostь.

радость.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic радость and Proto-Slavic *radostь ('joy, gladness'), formed from рад ('glad, joyful', Proto-Slavic *radъ) with the feminine abstract-noun suffix -ость.

радуга.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic радуга (Ukrainian райдуга). The second element is дуга ('arc, bow', Proto-Slavic *dǫga); Vasmer explains the first element as built on the root of рад ('glad, bright, merry'; compare dialectal Russian and Ukrainian весёлка 'rainbow', from весёлый 'merry'), later reshaped in some dialects by folk association with рай ('paradise').

раз.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic разъ ('stroke, blow; one time, occasion'), from Proto-Slavic *razъ, an o-grade noun derived from *rězati ('to cut, strike', modern Russian резать). Just as French coup and German Schlag shifted from 'a strike' to 'one time', a single stroke of counting became Russian раз ('time, occasion; one!').

раз-два-три.etymology: Compound rhythmic counting phrase uniting раз ('one, stroke', originally 'a cut/strike' from Proto-Slavic *razъ, related to резать 'to cut'), два ('two', from Proto-Slavic *dъva < PIE *dwóh₁), and три ('three', from Proto-Slavic *trьje < PIE *tréyes). Used both as a starting signal ('one, two, three!') and as the vocal cadence keeping 3/4 time in a waltz.

cognates.meaning: cognates of два and три from PIE *dwóh₁ and *tréyes

разбивать.etymology: Imperfective of разбить ('to smash, break to pieces'), formed with prefix раз- ('apart, into pieces') from бивать / бить ('to beat, strike', from Proto-Slavic *biti).

разбиваться.etymology: Imperfective reflexive of разбиться ('to break into pieces, shatter, crash'), formed from prefix раз- ('apart, into pieces') + биваться (iterative of бить 'to strike, beat', from Proto-Slavic *biti) + -ся.

разбирать.etymology: Imperfective of разобрать ('to take apart, sort out, take one by one'), formed with prefix раз- ('apart') and lengthened-grade iterative stem -бирать from брать ('to take', Proto-Slavic *bьrati).

history.meaning: to take apart; to take, grab (one each); to sort out

разбираться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of разбирать ('to take apart, sort out, examine'), formed from раз- ('apart') + -бирать (iterative of брать 'to take', Proto-Slavic *bьrati), developing the sense 'to understand thoroughly'.

history.meaning: to understand well, to know one's stuff; be sorted out

разбитый.etymology: Originally the past passive participle of разбить ('to smash, shatter, break into pieces', from раз- 'apart, in pieces' + бить 'to beat, strike', Proto-Slavic *biti), used as an adjective meaning 'broken, shattered, smashed'.
разбитый.notes: In Russian, разбить / разбитый is used for brittle things that shatter into pieces (a cup, plate, window, or mirror), whereas сломать / сломанный is used for mechanisms, furniture, or bones.

разбить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic разбитии, formed from the prefix раз- ('apart, into pieces') and бить ('to beat, strike', Old East Slavic бити, Proto-Slavic *biti). Literally, 'to strike into pieces, smash, shatter'.

history.meaning: to break, smash, shatter; to wreck (a car)

разбиться.etymology: Reflexive of разбить ('to smash, break into pieces', inherited from Old East Slavic розбити / разбити, from prefix раз- 'apart' + бить 'to beat, strike', from Proto-Slavic *biti) + -ся.

разбогатеть.etymology: Formed from prefix раз- (indicating full development or intensity of a state) + богатеть ('to grow rich', derived from богатый 'rich, wealthy', from Proto-Slavic *bogatъ, derived from *bogъ 'share, fortune, wealth').

разболеться.etymology: Formed from prefix раз- (indicating an action gaining intensity) + болеть ('to hurt, ache, be ill', from боль 'pain', from Proto-Slavic *bolěti) + reflexive suffix -ся ('to start hurting badly or fall seriously ill').

history.meaning: to start aching badly; to fall thoroughly ill

разбрасывать.etymology: Imperfective of разбросать ('to scatter, throw about'), formed from prefix раз- ('apart, in different directions') + брасывать (iterative of бросать 'to throw, cast', from Proto-Slavic *brъsati).

разбрасываться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective formed with prefix раз- ('in all directions, wastefully') and -ся from брасывать / бросать ('to throw, fling'), from Proto-Slavic *brosati.

разбудить.etymology: Formed from раз- ('out of a state, stirring up') + будить ('to wake someone up', Old East Slavic будити, Proto-Slavic *buditi, the ancient Indo-European o-grade causative of *bʰewdʰ- 'to be awake, aware', cognate with бодрый and Sanskrit bodhati).
разбудить.notes: Transitive ('to wake someone else up'); to wake up on one's own is проснуться.

разваливаться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective of развалиться ('to collapse, fall apart, sprawl'), formed with prefix раз- ('apart') and -ся from валить ('to topple, tumble'), from Proto-Slavic *valiti.

развалиться.etymology: Reflexive of развалить ('to pull down, demolish', formed from prefix раз- 'apart' + валить 'to topple, tumble, roll', from Proto-Slavic *valiti) + -ся ('to fall apart, collapse; to sprawl').

развалюха.etymology: Colloquial noun derived from развалиться / разваливаться ('to fall apart, crumble', from раз- + валить 'to topple', Proto-Slavic *valiti) + expressive colloquial noun suffix -юха.

разве.etymology: Adopted from Old Church Slavonic развѣ (and Old East Slavic розвѣ), originally a preposition meaning 'apart from, outside of, except, unless' (built on *orz- / *raz- 'apart'). From 'except if, unless perhaps' in conditional clauses it shifted into an interrogative particle expressing surprise or disbelief ('really? can it be that...?').
разве.notes: **Разве** asks a surprised or doubtful question when the speaker expected the opposite (*Разве магазин уже закрыт?* 'Is the shop really closed already?').

разведка.etymology: Noun in -ка formed from разведать ('to find out, explore, reconnoiter'), derived from раз- + ведать ('to know, inquire'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *vědati ('to know').

разведчик.etymology: Formed with the agent suffix -чик from разведать ('to reconnoiter, find out, explore'), derived from раз- + ведать ('to know, inquire', from Proto-Slavic *vědati).

разведённый.etymology: Past passive participle of развести ('to lead apart, separate, divorce; to dilute'), formed from раз- ('apart') + вести ('to lead', from Proto-Slavic *vesti).

развернуть.etymology: Formed with the prefix раз- ('apart, un-') + вернуть ('to turn, roll', from Proto-Slavic *vьrnǫti / *vьrtěti 'to turn'): 'to unroll, unfold, unwrap'.

развернуться.etymology: Formed from раз- ('apart, un-, all the way around') + вернуться ('to turn', from вертеть / вернуть) + -ся: both 'to unwrap/unfold' and 'to turn right around (180 degrees) to face or go the opposite way'.

развесить.etymology: Formed with the distributive prefix раз- ('around, in various places') + весить ('to hang', causative of висеть 'to be hanging', from Proto-Slavic *věsiti).

history.meaning: to hang up around, string out

развестись.etymology: Reflexive form of развести ('to lead apart, separate, dissolve a marriage'), formed from the prefix раз- ('apart') + вести ('to lead', from Proto-Slavic *vesti) + -сь.

развешивать.etymology: Imperfective of развешать ('to hang up in various places'), formed from prefix раз- ('around, in various places') + вешать ('to hang', iterative of весить, from Proto-Slavic *věšati).

развеяться.etymology: Reflexive of развеять ('to scatter in the wind, dispel', formed from prefix раз- 'apart, away' + веять 'to blow, winnow', from Proto-Slavic *vějati) + -ся ('to disperse; figuratively to clear one's head, unwind').

history.meaning: to dispel, scatter in the wind
to disperse; to clear one's head, unwind

развиваться.etymology: Imperfective reflexive of развиться ('to untwist, unroll; to develop, evolve', a semantic calque of French se développer / German sich entwickeln), formed from prefix раз- ('un-, out') + вивать (iterative of вить 'to twist, wind', from Proto-Slavic *viti) + -ся.

развитие.etymology: Verbal noun from развить / развиться ('to unroll, unwind; to develop', calquing French développement and German Entwicklung), formed from раз- ('un-, out') + вить ('to wind, twist', Proto-Slavic *viti) + -тие.

развитый.etymology: Past passive participle of развить ('to unwind; to develop', calquing French développé / German entwickelt), formed from prefix раз- + вить ('to twist, wind', from Proto-Slavic *viti).

развлекаться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of развлекать ('to divert, entertain', originally 'to draw/pull apart [one's thoughts from care]', calquing French distraire / divertir), built on Old Church Slavonic развлѣщи (from *velkti 'to draw, drag').

развод.etymology: Deverbal noun formed from разводить / развести ('to lead apart, separate; to dissolve a marriage; to breed; in slang, to string someone along / con'), built from раз- ('apart') + водить ('to lead', Proto-Slavic *voditi). Literally 'a leading apart', whence 'divorce' (and in modern colloquial slang, 'a scam, con, hustle').

history.meaning: leading apart, separation → divorce; (slang) scam, con

разводить.etymology: Imperfective of развести ('to lead apart, separate, divorce; to breed, raise; to dilute'), formed from prefix раз- ('apart, in various directions') + водить ('to lead, conduct', from Proto-Slavic *voditi).

history.meaning: to lead apart, divorce; to breed
to breed, raise; to divorce; (slang) to scam

разводиться.etymology: Imperfective reciprocal verb formed from разводить ('to lead apart, separate', from раз- 'apart' + водить 'to lead', Proto-Slavic *voditi) + -ся: literally 'to part ways, dissolve a marriage'.

разволноваться.etymology: Formed from prefix раз- (indicating rising intensity of a state) + волноваться ('to worry, be agitated', originally 'to surge in waves', derived from волна 'wave', from Proto-Slavic *vьlna).

history.meaning: to get worked up, become very nervous

разворовать.etymology: Formed from prefix раз- ('in all directions, completely') + воровать ('to steal, thieve', derived from вор 'thief; in 16th–17th c. Russian rebel, state criminal, impostor').

развязать.etymology: Perfective verb formed from the prefix раз- ('apart, un-') and вязать ('to tie, bind, knot', inherited from Old East Slavic вязати, Proto-Slavic *vęzati). Means literally 'to untie, unbind' and figuratively 'to unleash, start (a war or quarrel): развязать войну'.

history.meaning: to untie, unknot; to unleash (a conflict)

развязывать.etymology: Imperfective verb formed with the secondary imperfectivizing suffix -ывать from развязать ('to untie, unfasten'), built on prefix раз- ('apart, un-') + вязать ('to tie, bind', from Proto-Slavic *vęzati).

разгадать.etymology: Formed with the prefix раз- ('apart, unravelling') + гадать ('to guess, divine, ponder'), inherited from Old East Slavic гадати and Proto-Slavic *gadati ('to suppose, divine, speak').

history.meaning: to solve, figure out (a riddle, mystery, or code)

разгар.etymology: Deverbal noun from разгореться / разгораться ('to flare up, burn brightly'), formed from prefix раз- + гар- (ablaut grade of гореть 'to burn', from Proto-Slavic *gorěti / *garъ 'burning, heat').

разгибаться.etymology: Imperfective reflexive of разогнуться ('to unbend, straighten one's back'), formed from prefix раз- ('un-, apart') + гибать (iterative of гнуть 'to bend', from Proto-Slavic *gъbnǫti / *gybati) + -ся.

разгладиться.etymology: Reflexive/intransitive form in -ся of разгладить ('to smooth out, iron flat'), formed with prefix раз- ('out flat') + гладить ('to smooth, stroke, iron', from гладкий 'smooth', Proto-Slavic *gladъkъ).

history.meaning: to smooth out → to smooth out, unpucker (of a wrinkled brow or cloth)

разговаривать.etymology: Formed in Russian as the imperfective of an older perfective разговорить, from раз- ('back and forth, in various directions') + говаривать (iterative of говорить 'to speak, talk', from говор 'talk, speech', Proto-Slavic *govorъ): 'to converse, talk with someone'.

history.meaning: to speak -> to converse, talk back and forth

разговор.etymology: Formed as a prefixal-stem noun from разговаривать ('to talk, converse', from раз- 'back and forth' + говор 'speech, talk', Proto-Slavic *govorъ): 'an exchange of speech, conversation, talk'.

разговорить.etymology: Formed from prefix раз- (indicating getting an action going thoroughly) + говорить ('to speak, talk', from Proto-Slavic *govoriti).

history.meaning: to get someone talking, draw into conversation

разговорчик.etymology: Diminutive of разговор ('conversation, talk', deverbal from разговориться / разговаривать 'to converse', from раз- + говорить 'to speak', Proto-Slavic *govoriti) + suffix -чик.

history.meaning: little chat; (in plural разговорчики!) backtalk, chatter

разгребать.etymology: Imperfective of разгрести ('to rake apart, shovel away, clear up'), formed from prefix раз- ('apart, away') + гребать (iterative of грести 'to rake, row, scrape', from Proto-Slavic *grebti).

history.meaning: to rake aside; (figurative) to clear up a mess

разгром.etymology: Deverbal noun from разгромить ('to smash, rout, devastate'), formed from prefix раз- ('apart, completely') + громить ('to smash, destroy, thunder against', from гром 'thunder', Proto-Slavic *gromъ).

разгромный.etymology: Adjective formed with -ный from разгром ('utter rout, devastation'), deverbal noun from разгромить ('to smash, rout'), from раз- + громить ('to smash, thunder against'), derived from гром ('thunder', Proto-Slavic *gromъ).

разгружать.etymology: Formed as the imperfective counterpart of разгрузить ('to unload'), from раз- ('apart, off, un-') + грузить ('to load', from груз 'load, cargo, heavy weight', Proto-Slavic *grǫzъ 'sinking weight, ballast', with з -> ж in the imperfective).

history.meaning: to unload (a truck, ship, or boxes)

разгрузить.etymology: Formed from reversative prefix раз- ('un-') + грузить ('to load; originally to sink, submerge under weight', derived from груз 'load, cargo', from Proto-Slavic *grǫziti 'to sink, load').

разгрузка.etymology: Action noun derived from разгрузить / разгружать ('to unload', from prefix раз- 'un-' + грузить 'to load', from груз 'cargo, load', Proto-Slavic *grǫziti) + suffix -ка.

раздавать.etymology: Imperfective of раздать ('to distribute, hand out'), formed from the distributive prefix раз- ('out in various directions') + давать ('to give', iterative of дать, from Proto-Slavic *davati).

раздать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic роздати / раздати (Proto-Slavic *orzdati), formed from раз- ('out in different directions, to several recipients') + дать ('to give', Proto-Slavic *dati): 'to hand out, distribute'.
раздать.notes: Conjugates like дать: я раздам, ты раздашь, он раздаст, они раздадут.

раздевалка.etymology: Colloquial noun formed in Russian with the room/place suffix -лка from раздеваться ('to undress, take off one's coat or street clothes'), built from раз- ('un-, off') + девать / деть ('to put, place', Proto-Slavic *děti).

history.meaning: to undress / take off coats → locker room, changing room, cloakroom

rootFamily.gloss: to undress, take off one's coat

раздевать.etymology: Imperfective of раздеть ('to undress'), formed from reversative prefix раз- ('un-') + девать (iterative of деть 'to put, place; in clothing compounds to put on', from Proto-Slavic *děvati / *děti).

раздеваться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of раздевать ('to undress'), imperfective of раздеть, formed with prefix раз- ('un-, apart', by antonymic analogy with одеть 'to dress') from деть ('to put', Proto-Slavic *děti).

history.meaning: to take off one's coat; to undress

раздел.etymology: Deverbal noun from разделить ('to divide, partition, share'), inherited from Old East Slavic роздѣлъ / Old Church Slavonic раздѣлъ, from раз- ('apart') + делить ('to divide', from Proto-Slavic *děliti).

разделать.etymology: Formed from prefix раз- + делать ('to do, make, work, dress [skins, timber, meat]', from дело 'work, deed', from Proto-Slavic *dělati).

history.meaning: to dress, butcher, fillet (meat or fish)

разделение.etymology: Verbal noun from разделить ('to divide, separate'), inherited from Old Church Slavonic раздѣление, from раз- ('apart') + дѣлити ('to divide, share', Proto-Slavic *děliti).

разделить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic раздѣлити ('to divide, part, distribute'), formed with prefix раз- ('apart, into parts') + делить ('to divide, share', from Proto-Slavic *děliti, related to *dělъ 'part, share').

разделка.etymology: Action noun derived from разделать / разделывать ('to dress, butcher, fillet meat or fish', from prefix раз- + делать 'to work, dress', from Proto-Slavic *dělati) + suffix -ка.

разделывать.etymology: Imperfective of разделать ('to dress/butcher a carcass, finish off, prepare'), formed with prefix раз- ('apart') from делать ('to do, make, work on'), from Proto-Slavic *dělati.

раздельно.etymology: Adverb formed from раздельный ('separate, distinct'), derived from разделить ('to divide apart'), from раз- + делить ('to divide', Proto-Slavic *děliti).

разделять.etymology: Imperfective of разделить ('to divide, separate; to share'), borrowed from or influenced by Old Church Slavonic раздѣляти, from раз- ('apart') + делить ('to divide, share', from Proto-Slavic *děliti).

history.meaning: to divide; to share (views or feelings)

раздеть.etymology: Formed from reversative prefix раз- ('un-') + деть ('to put, place; in одеть/надеть to dress', inherited from Old East Slavic дѣти, from Proto-Slavic *děti 'to put, do').

раздеться.etymology: Reflexive of раздеть ('to undress', formed from reversative prefix раз- 'un-' + деть 'to put, dress', from Proto-Slavic *děti) + -ся ('to undress oneself').

раздражать.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic раздражати ('to provoke, incite, irritate'), imperfective of раздражити, formed from раз- + дражити ('to tease, provoke, irritate', cognate with Russian дразнить, from Proto-Slavic *dražiti).

раздражённый.etymology: Past passive participle of раздражить ('to irritate, provoke, anger', from Old Church Slavonic раздражити, from раз- + дражити 'to tease, provoke', Proto-Slavic *dražiti).

раздумывать.etymology: Imperfective of раздумать ('to ponder, deliberate; to change one's mind'), formed with prefix раз- from думать ('to think'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *dumati.

раздумье.etymology: Derived from раздумать / раздумывать ('to ponder, muse, deliberate', from prefix раз- + думать 'to think, meditate', from дума 'thought, council', Proto-Slavic *duma) + neuter abstract suffix -ье.

разливать.etymology: Imperfective verb formed from разлить ('to pour out into vessels; to spill'), built on prefix раз- ('out, into several containers') + ливать (iterative of лить 'to pour', from Proto-Slavic *liti).

history.meaning: to pour out (tea, soup into cups/bowls); to spill

разливаться.etymology: Imperfective reflexive of разлиться ('to overflow, spill out, spread'), formed from prefix раз- ('out, in all directions') + ливаться (iterative of лить 'to pour', from Proto-Slavic *liti) + -ся.

разлить.etymology: Formed with prefix раз- ('out, apart, into vessels') from лить ('to pour'), inherited from Old East Slavic лити (лию), from Proto-Slavic *liti ('to pour').

различать.etymology: Imperfective of различить ('to distinguish, tell apart'), borrowed from Old Church Slavonic различати / различити ('to differentiate, distinguish', derived from ликъ / лице 'face, form, appearance', Proto-Slavic *likъ, *lice).

разложить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic розложити / Old Church Slavonic разложити ('to lay out, spread out, distribute'), formed from prefix раз- ('apart, out') + ложить ('to lay, place', from Proto-Slavic *ložiti).

history.meaning: to lay out, spread out; to decompose

разлучить.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic разлучити ('to separate, part, sever', corresponding to Old East Slavic розлучити), formed from раз- ('apart') + лучити ('to join, destin, separate', from Proto-Slavic *lǫčiti).

размазать.etymology: Formed from prefix раз- ('out, over a surface') + мазать ('to smear, daub, anoint', inherited from Old East Slavic мазати, from Proto-Slavic *mazati).

размах.etymology: Deverbal noun from размахнуть / размахивать ('to swing wide, brandish'), formed from prefix раз- ('wide, apart') + мах ('swing, stroke', from махать 'to wave, swing', from Proto-Slavic *maxati).

разменять.etymology: Formed from prefix раз- ('into smaller parts, apart') + менять ('to change, exchange', from мена 'exchange', from Proto-Slavic *měniti / *měna).

history.meaning: to change (money), break a larger note

размер.etymology: Deverbal noun formed from размерить ('to measure out, proportion'), built from prefix раз- ('out, apart') + мерить / мера ('to measure / measure', from Proto-Slavic *měra, from PIE *meh₁- 'to measure').

history.meaning: to measure out → size, dimension, meter

разместить.etymology: Formed from prefix раз- ('around, in respective places') + местить ('to place, locate', derived from место 'place, space, site', from Proto-Slavic *město).

разминаться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective of размяться ('to stretch one's limbs, warm up'), formed with prefix раз- from мять (мну, iterative -минать, 'to knead, rub, limber up'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *męti ('to knead, press').

history.meaning: to knead, press, work until supple
to warm up, to limber up

разморозить.etymology: Formed from reversative prefix раз- ('un-, de-') + морозить ('to freeze', derived from мороз 'frost, freezing cold', East Slavic pleophonic form of Proto-Slavic *morzъ).

разморозиться.etymology: Reflexive/intransitive of разморозить ('to defrost, thaw', formed from reversative prefix раз- 'un-' + морозить 'to freeze', from мороз 'frost', Proto-Slavic *morzъ) + -ся.

размытый.etymology: Past passive participle of размыть ('to wash out, blur with water'), formed from prefix раз- + мыть ('to wash', from Proto-Slavic *myti).

history.meaning: to wash out → blurred, washed-out, smudged

размыть.etymology: Formed with the prefix раз- ('apart, dissolving') + мыть ('to wash', inherited from Old East Slavic мыти and Proto-Slavic *myti): 'to wash away, erode with water, blur ink or paint'.

history.meaning: to wash out, blur (with water or moisture)

размышлять.etymology: Imperfective of размыслить ('to ponder, reflect, deliberate'), borrowed from or influenced by Old Church Slavonic размышляти (with Church Slavonic -шл- from *slj), from раз- + мыслити ('to think', from мысль 'thought', Proto-Slavic *myslь).

разнервничаться.etymology: Inceptive/intensive reflexive formed with circumfix раз-...-ся from нервничать ('to be nervous, fret'), derived from нервный / нерв ('nerve', borrowed via German Nerv / French nerf from Latin nervus 'sinew, nerve').

history.meaning: to get worked up, to get all nervous

разнести.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic рознести / Old Church Slavonic разнести ('to carry in different directions, scatter'), formed from prefix раз- ('apart, around') + нести ('to carry', from Proto-Slavic *nesti).

history.meaning: to deliver around; to smash to pieces

разница.etymology: Derived with the feminine noun suffix -ица from разный ('different, various'), which goes back via Old Church Slavonic разьнъ ('apart, different') to Proto-Slavic *orzьnъ, built on the prefix/preposition *orz- (Russian раз- 'apart, asunder').
разница.notes: Used constantly in какая разница? ('what's the difference? / what does it matter?').

разногласие.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic разногласиѥ ('discord, dissonance, disagreement', calquing Ancient Greek διαφωνία), compound of разный ('different, diverse', from *orznъ) + -о- + гласъ ('voice, sound', Church Slavonic reflex of *golsъ) + -ие.

разнообразный.etymology: Compound adjective (modeled on Old Church Slavonic разнообразьнъ, calquing Ancient Greek ποικιλόμορφος / πολυειδής) formed from разный ('different, various', from *orznъ) + -о- + образ ('form, shape, image', from Proto-Slavic *oborzъ) + -ный.

разносить.etymology: Imperfective of разнести ('to carry around, deliver; to scatter, smash'), formed from prefix раз- ('around, apart') + носить ('to carry', iterative of нести, from Proto-Slavic *nositi).

history.meaning: to deliver around, hand round; to wear in (shoes)

разносторонний.etymology: Compound adjective formed from разный ('different, various', from Church Slavonic разнъ, Proto-Slavic *orznъ) + -о- + сторонний (from сторона 'side, direction', East Slavic pleophonic form of Proto-Slavic *storna).

разный.etymology: Adopted with the South Slavic prefix vocalism раз- (alongside older native розный) from Old Church Slavonic разьнъ ('divided, separate, different'), built on the prefix/preposition *orz- ('apart, asunder', related to резать 'to cut') + adjectival suffix -ный.

разобрать.etymology: Formed with prefix разо- ('apart') from брать ('to take'), inherited from Old East Slavic бърати, from Proto-Slavic *bьrati ('to take, gather').

history.meaning: to take apart, to dismantle; to sort out

разобраться.etymology: Perfective reflexive verb formed from разобрать ('to take apart, sort out, dismantle'), built from раз- / разо- ('apart') + брать ('to take', Proto-Slavic *bьrati). From the concrete sense of 'sorting items out one by one', it developed the figurative sense 'to figure out, understand thoroughly, settle a matter'.

history.meaning: to sort out → to figure out, get to the bottom of

разогревать.etymology: Imperfective of разогреть ('to warm up, reheat'), formed with prefix разо- ('thoroughly, up') from греть ('to warm, heat'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *grěti.

разогреть.etymology: Prefixed perfective verb formed from разо- (prevocalic variant of раз- 'thoroughly, up') + греть ('to warm, heat'), inherited from Old East Slavic грѣти, from Proto-Slavic *grěti ('to warm', related by ablaut to гореть 'to burn' and жар 'heat').

разозлить.etymology: Perfective formed with intensive prefix разо- from злить ('to anger, make mad'), derived from злой ('angry, wicked, evil'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *zъlъ.

разозлиться.etymology: Formed from the intensive prefix разо- + злиться ('to get angry', from злить 'to anger', derived from злой 'evil, angry', Proto-Slavic *zъlъ).

history.meaning: to get angry, lose one's temper

разойтись.etymology: Formed from prefix разо- ('apart, in different directions') + идти ('to go, walk', from Proto-Slavic *jьti) + reflexive suffix -сь ('to walk apart, disperse, part ways, divorce').

history.meaning: to disperse, part ways, break up

разок.etymology: Colloquial diminutive formed with the suffix -ок from раз ('time, occasion, once'), which is inherited from Old East Slavic разъ (originally 'a single stroke, cut, blow', related by ablaut to резать 'to cut', Proto-Slavic *razъ).

history.meaning: time, once → just once, one quick time

разок-другой.etymology: Colloquial compound adverbial phrase formed from разок (diminutive in -ок of раз 'time, occasion', from Proto-Slavic *razъ 'stroke, time') + другой ('another, a second', from Proto-Slavic *drugъ).

разорвать.etymology: Formed with the prefix разо- ('apart, in pieces') + рвать ('to tear, rip, rend'), inherited from Old East Slavic ръвати and Proto-Slavic *rъvati ('to tear, pluck').

history.meaning: to tear in two, tear up

разорить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic and Old Church Slavonic разорити ('to destroy, demolish, lay waste'), formed from раз- ('apart') + орити ('to tear down, overthrow, destroy', Proto-Slavic *oriti).

history.meaning: to ruin, to bankrupt, lay waste

разослать.etymology: Formed from prefix разо- ('out in various directions') + слать ('to send', inherited from Old East Slavic сълати, from Proto-Slavic *sъlati).

history.meaning: to send out in various directions

разочарование.etymology: Verbal noun from разочаровать ('to disenchant, disappoint'), formed as a calque on French désenchantement / German Enttäuschung from раз- ('un-') + очарование ('enchantment, charm', from чары 'magic, sorcery').

разочаровать.etymology: Formed with reversative prefix раз- ('un-, dis-') from очаровать ('to charm, enchant', derived from чары 'magic, spell', Proto-Slavic *čarъ), calquing French désenchanter ('to break a spell, disillusion').

разрешать.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic разрѣшати (imperfective of разрѣшити 'to untie, loosen, absolve, permit'), from раз- ('apart, un-') + рѣшити ('to untie, solve', Proto-Slavic *rěšiti).

history.meaning: to untie, release from a bond, permit

разрешение.etymology: Verbal noun from разрешить ('to untie, resolve, permit'), borrowed from Old Church Slavonic разрѣшение ('loosing, absolution, solution'), from раз- + рѣшити ('to untie, release', Proto-Slavic *rěšiti).

разрешить.etymology: Borrowed from Church Slavonic разрѣшити ('to untie, unbind, absolve, release from a prohibition'), formed from prefix раз- ('un-, apart') + рѣшити ('to untie a knot, loosen, solve', from Proto-Slavic *rěšiti): literally 'to untie a restriction', hence 'to allow, permit' and 'to resolve'.

разрешиться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of разрешить ('to untie, resolve, settle'), from Old Church Slavonic разрѣшити ('to untie, loosen', from Proto-Slavic *rěšiti).

history.meaning: to be resolved, to work itself out

разрешённый.etymology: Past passive participle of разрешить ('to permit, allow; to solve; originally to untie, release from a bond'), borrowed from Old Church Slavonic разрѣшити ('to untie, absolve, permit', from раз- + рѣшити 'to untie, loose', Proto-Slavic *rěšiti).

разрулить.etymology: Originally an aviation and driving verb meaning 'to taxi an aircraft or steer a vehicle out of a tight spot', formed from prefix раз- + рулить ('to steer', from руль 'rudder, steering wheel', borrowed from Dutch roer); in late 20th-century slang 'to sort out a tricky situation'.

history.meaning: to steer clear; (colloquial) to sort out, resolve

разрушать.etymology: Imperfective of разрушить ('to destroy, demolish'), borrowed from or influenced by Old Church Slavonic разрушати / разрушити, from раз- ('apart, down') + рушити ('to pull down, break, disturb', from Proto-Slavic *rušiti).

history.meaning: to tear down, break up, move

разрушение.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic разрушениѥ ('destruction, demolition'), verbal noun from разрушити ('to destroy', from раз- + Proto-Slavic *rušiti) + -ение.

разрушенный.etymology: Past passive participle of разрушить ('to destroy, ruin, demolish', from Old Church Slavonic разрушити, from раз- + Proto-Slavic *rušiti 'to break, pull down').

разрушить.etymology: Perfective verb formed from the prefix раз- ('apart, into pieces') and рушить ('to pull down, demolish, shatter'), inherited from Old East Slavic рушити and Proto-Slavic *rušiti ('to tear apart, break up, set in motion', cognate with Lithuanian raũšti 'to dig up, tear').

разрушиться.etymology: Reflexive/intransitive of разрушить ('to destroy, demolish', from раз- + рушить 'to pull down, crumble', from Proto-Slavic *rušiti) + -ся ('to collapse, fall into ruin').

разрыв.etymology: Deverbal noun from разорвать / разрывать ('to tear apart, sever, burst'), formed from prefix раз- ('apart') + рыв- (lengthened-grade stem of рвать 'to tear', from Proto-Slavic *rъvati).

разряд.etymology: Deverbal noun from разрядить ('to arrange in order, classify; later also to unload or discharge a gun or capacitor'), inherited from Early Modern Russian разрядъ ('order, distribution of service duties, rank'), from раз- + ряд ('row, order, rank', Proto-Slavic *rędъ).

history.meaning: to arrange by rank; to unload, discharge

разум.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic разумъ ('understanding, reason, mind', corresponding to Old East Slavic розумъ), formed from prefix раз- (*orz-) + умъ ('mind, intellect', from Proto-Slavic *umъ).

разумеется.etymology: Grammaticalized parenthetical particle from the third-person singular present reflexive of разуметь ('to understand, comprehend', from разум 'reason, mind', Proto-Slavic *orzuměti), literally 'it is understood (само собой разумеется)'.

history.meaning: it is understood -> of course, naturally

разумный.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic and Old Church Slavonic разумьныи ('endowed with reason, wise, sensible'), derived from разум ('reason, intellect'), from раз- + ум ('mind, intellect', Proto-Slavic *umъ).

разуть.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic розути / Old Church Slavonic разути ('to take off footwear'), formed from reversative prefix раз- (*orz- 'un-') + Proto-Slavic root *-uti ('to put on footwear', as in обуть 'to put on shoes', cognate with Lithuanian auti).

history.meaning: to take off shoes or boots

разъезжать.etymology: Formed from prefix разъ- ('around, in various directions') + езжать (iterative of ездить 'to ride, drive, travel', from Proto-Slavic *ězditi).

разъясниться.etymology: Reflexive of разъяснить ('to clarify, explain, make clear', formed from prefix разъ- + яснить, from ясный 'clear, bright', Proto-Slavic *jasnъ) + -ся ('to clear up [of weather or a situation], become clear').

разыграть.etymology: Formed with prefix раз- ('out, thoroughly') from играть ('to play, act'), inherited from Old East Slavic играти, from Proto-Slavic *jьgrati ('to play').

history.meaning: to play a prank on; to act out; to raffle

разыгрывать.etymology: Imperfective of разыграть ('to play out, stage, raffle; to play a prank on someone'), formed from prefix раз- + игрывать (iterative of играть 'to play', from игра 'game, play', Proto-Slavic *jьgra).

history.meaning: to play out, stage; to trick, prank
to stage; to pull someone's leg, prank

рай.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic and Old Church Slavonic раи ('paradise, Garden of Eden'), from Proto-Slavic *rajь; usually considered an early Iranian borrowing (cf. Avestan rāy- 'wealth, splendor, happiness', Old Persian rāy-) or cognate with Sanskrit rāy- ('treasure, felicity').

район.etymology: Borrowed in the 18th–19th centuries from French rayon ('spoke of a wheel, radius, ray; surrounding zone or district measured from a centre'), derived from Old French rai ('ray, spoke'), from Latin radius ('staff, wheel spoke, beam, radius').

рак.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic ракъ ('crayfish; cancer'), from Proto-Slavic *rakъ ('crayfish, crab'); the medical sense 'cancer' is an ancient calque on Latin cancer / Greek καρκίνος ('crab; malignant tumor', after the crab-like swollen veins around a tumor).

ракия.etymology: Borrowed via Bulgarian ракия and Serbian ракија from Ottoman Turkish rakı ('distilled fruit spirit, arrack'), itself from Arabic ʿaraq ('perspiration, sweat; condensation drops in distillation, distilled liquor').

раковина.etymology: Derived from рак ('crayfish, crab, crustacean', inherited from Old East Slavic ракъ, from Proto-Slavic *rakъ) + possessive/augmentative suffix -овина; originally 'shell of a crustacean or mollusk', and by shape comparison 'ear concha' and 'plumbing sink/basin'.

рама.etymology: Borrowed via Polish rama ('frame') from Middle High German rame (modern German Rahmen, 'frame, loom, support'). The Germanic word derives from Proto-Germanic *hramō ('frame, prop, rack'), from a Proto-Indo-European root *krem- ('to hang, build a wooden framework').

рамка.etymology: Diminutive in -ка of рама ('frame, window frame'), borrowed via Polish rama from Middle High German rame / German Rahmen ('frame, border, support').

ранить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic ранити and Proto-Slavic *raniti ('to wound, injure'), a denominal verb built on рана ('wound', Proto-Slavic *rana, cognate with Sanskrit vraṇá 'wound, sore').
ранить.notes: A biaspectual verb in Russian: ранить functions as both imperfective and perfective.

ранний.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic рании ('early'), adjective formed from рано ('early, in the morning'), from Proto-Slavic *ranъ ('early').

рано.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic рано and Proto-Slavic *rano ('early; in the early morning'), related to *ranъ ('early', Russian ранний) and *zarja ('dawn, morning glow', Russian заря).
рано.notes: Notice how in Polish (rano), Czech (ráno), and Ukrainian (ранок), this root became the standard noun for 'morning', whereas Russian preserved утро for 'morning' and kept рано as 'early'.

рановато.etymology: Attenuative adverb formed from рано ('early', from ранний / раний 'early', from Proto-Slavic *ranъ 'early, morning') + attenuative suffix -овато ('a bit too, rather').

history.meaning: a bit early, rather too early

раньше.etymology: Formed in Russian as the comparative of рано ('early') and ранний ('early'), from Proto-Slavic *rano ('early, in the morning'), related to *ranъ ('early'; compare утро раное). From 'earlier in the day' it generalized to 'earlier, ahead of time, formerly, used to'.

рапорт.etymology: Borrowed in the Petrine era via German Rapport from French rapport ('report, official account'), deverbal from rapporter ('to bring back, report', from re- + apporter, from Latin apportare 'to bring to').

history.meaning: official report, formal letter of resignation

раскатать.etymology: Formed with prefix рас- ('out, flat') from катать ('to roll'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *katati ('to roll').

history.meaning: to roll out flat; (colloq.) to crush, to steamroll

раскладной.etymology: Derived from раскладывать ('to unfold, spread out', from prefix рас- 'apart, out' + класть / кладывать 'to lay, put', from Proto-Slavic *klasti) + adjectival suffix -ной.

раскладывать.etymology: Formed as the imperfective counterpart of разложить ('to lay out, spread out, unfold'), built from рас- ('apart, out in order', voiceless variant of раз- before к) + кладывать (iterative of класть 'to lay, put', Proto-Slavic *klasti).

history.meaning: to lay out, spread out, unfold (imperfective)

раскручивать.etymology: Imperfective of раскрутить ('to untwist, unscrew, spin up; in slang, to promote'), formed with prefix рас- ('un-; into full motion') from крутить ('to twist, turn, spin', from Proto-Slavic *krǫtiti).

history.meaning: to unscrew, take apart; (colloq.) to promote

раскрывать.etymology: Formed with the prefix рас- ('apart, un-') and the imperfective stem -крывать, from крыть ('to cover'). The verb descends from Proto-Slavic *kryti ('to cover, hide'), from the Proto-Indo-European root *(s)krew- ('to cover, hide, pile'). Adding рас- reverses the action of covering ('to uncover, open wide, disclose').

раскрываться.etymology: Reflexive/intransitive form in -ся of раскрывать ('to open wide, uncover'), formed from prefix рас- ('apart, wide') + крывать (iterative of крыть 'to cover', from Proto-Slavic *kryti).

history.meaning: to uncover, open wide → to open up, fall open (of a book, flower, or door)

раскрыть.etymology: Formed from reversative/expansive prefix рас- ('un-, open') + крыть ('to cover', inherited from Old East Slavic крыти, from Proto-Slavic *kryti).

history.meaning: to uncover, open up, solve (a crime)

раскрыться.etymology: Formed from раскрыть ('to uncover, open wide', combining рас- 'apart, wide' + крыть 'to cover') + the reflexive/intransitive suffix -ся: 'to open wide, unfold, blossom, or come to light'.

раскупить.etymology: Formed from distributive/exhaustive prefix рас- ('all up, in various directions') + купить ('to buy', inherited from Old East Slavic купити, from Proto-Slavic *kupiti, an early borrowing from Gothic kaupon 'to trade').

раскусить.etymology: Formed from prefix рас- ('apart, open') + кусить ('to bite', from Proto-Slavic *kǫsiti 'to bite, taste'); figuratively 'to crack open like a nut, see through someone's intentions'.

history.meaning: to bite through; (figurative) to see through, figure out

распаковать.etymology: Formed from reversative prefix рас- ('un-') + паковать ('to pack', borrowed via German packen or Polish pakować, from Middle Low German / Middle Dutch pak 'bundle, pack').

распахнуть.etymology: Semelfactive perfective verb formed with prefix рас- ('wide apart') + пахнуть ('to sweep, wave, fling', from older Russian пахать 'to sweep, fan, wave', distinct from пахнуть 'to smell'). Literally 'to fling wide open with a sweeping motion'.

history.meaning: to throw open, fling wide (doors, windows, or coat lapels)

расписание.etymology: Formed as a verbal noun in -ние from расписать ('to write out in detail, enter in a schedule or table', from рас- 'out in order' + писать 'to write'): 'a written schedule or timetable'.

history.meaning: to write out in order, schedule

расписаться.etymology: Formed from рас- ('out') + писать ('to write') + -ся: 'to write one's signature in an official register, receipt book, or marriage registry'.

history.meaning: to sign one's name (on a receipt or register)

расписаться.notes: Usage contrast: подписать takes a direct object (подписать документ 'to sign a document'), whereas расписаться is intransitive and takes в + prepositional or за + accusative (расписаться за посылку 'to sign for a parcel').

расписка.etymology: Deverbal noun formed in Russian with the suffix -ка from расписаться / расписать ('to sign in acknowledgment, write out'), built from рас- + писать ('to write', inherited from Old East Slavic писати, Proto-Slavic *pьsati).

history.meaning: to sign for → written receipt, signed IOU or acknowledgment

rootFamily.gloss: to sign; to register a marriage

расписной.etymology: Adjective formed with the suffix -ной from расписать ('to paint with decorative patterns'), built on prefix рас- ('all over, out') + писать ('to paint, write', from Proto-Slavic *pьsati, originally 'to adorn with colour or incisions').

history.meaning: to decorate with paint → painted, hand-decorated

расписываться.etymology: Imperfective reflexive of расписаться ('to sign one's name; to register a marriage officially'), formed from prefix рас- + писывать (iterative of писать 'to write', from Proto-Slavic *pisati) + -ся.

history.meaning: to sign; to register one's marriage
to sign; to get married at a registry office

расплакаться.etymology: Inceptive/intensive reflexive formed with circumfix рас-...-ся from плакать ('to weep, cry'), inherited from Proto-Slavic *plakati ('to weep').

history.meaning: to burst into tears, start crying

расплатиться.etymology: Formed from prefix рас- + платить ('to pay', from Old East Slavic платити, from Proto-Slavic *platiti, derived from *platъ 'piece of cloth used as currency') + reflexive suffix -ся ('to pay off completely, settle accounts').

расплачиваться.etymology: Imperfective reflexive of расплатиться ('to pay off, settle accounts; to pay the price for one's actions'), formed from prefix рас- + плачивать (iterative of платить 'to pay', from Proto-Slavic *platiti) + -ся.

history.meaning: to pay, settle up; to pay for one's mistakes

расплываться.etymology: Reflexive imperfective formed from рас- ('outward in all directions'), плыть ('to float, swim, flow'), and -ся. The root descends from Proto-Slavic *plyti / *pluti ('to float, flow'), from the Proto-Indo-European root *plew- ('to flow, float, swim'). It is cognate with English flow, fleet, and flood, as well as Ancient Greek πλέω (pléō, 'to sail').

history.meaning: to blur, run (of ink), break into a smile

cognates.meaning: to move as a liquid (from PIE *plew-)

располагаться.etymology: Imperfective reflexive of расположиться ('to arrange oneself, settle down, camp; to be situated'), formed from prefix рас- + полагать ('to lay, place, suppose', from Proto-Slavic *polagati, iterative of *položiti) + -ся.

history.meaning: to settle in, make oneself comfortable
to settle down; to be located

распорка.etymology: Derived with the instrumental noun suffix -ка from распор ('outward bracing pressure'), from распереть / распирать ('to push apart, brace from within'). Combine рас- ('apart') with the Proto-Slavic root *perti / *pьrǫ ('to press, push, prop'), from Proto-Indo-European *per- ('to press, strike, push through'). A распорка is thus a bar that holds two sides taut by pressing them apart.

распоряжение.etymology: Formed as a verbal noun in -ние from распорядиться ('to arrange, issue orders, manage'), built from рас- + по- + ряд ('row, order', Proto-Slavic *rędъ, as in порядок 'order'): 'an official instruction, order, or disposal'.

history.meaning: to give orders -> instruction, order, disposal

распоряжение.notes: Used in в вашем распоряжении ('at your disposal').

расправить.etymology: Formed from рас- ('out, apart, un-') + править ('to make straight', from правый 'straight, right', Proto-Slavic *pravъ): 'to straighten out, smooth out creases or folds, or spread (wings or shoulders)'.

расправляться.etymology: Imperfective reflexive of расправиться ('to straighten out; to deal harshly with, settle scores with'), formed from prefix рас- + править ('to direct, set right, govern', from правый 'straight, right', Proto-Slavic *praviti) + -ся.

history.meaning: to deal with, make short work of

распределять.etymology: Imperfective of распределить ('to distribute, allocate, apportion'), formed in bookish Russian from рас- ('apart') + предел ('boundary, limit, allotted share', borrowed from Old Church Slavonic прѣдѣлъ, from *děliti 'to divide').

распробовать.etymology: Formed with prefix рас- ('thoroughly, fully') from пробовать ('to try, taste, test'), borrowed via Polish próbować and Middle High German prōben from Latin probāre ('to test, approve').

распространять.etymology: Imperfective of распространить ('to spread, extend, disseminate'), borrowed from or formed on Old Church Slavonic распространяти / распространити ('to widen, spread out', from рас- + пространьнъ 'wide, spacious', from про- + страна 'side, expanse').

распространённый.etymology: Past passive participle of распространить ('to spread, disseminate', from Old Church Slavonic распространити 'to widen, extend', derived from пространьнъ 'spacious, wide').

распугать.etymology: Formed with prefix рас- ('in all directions, away') from пугать ('to frighten, scare'), of expressive East Slavic origin (related to пужать).

распустить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic роспустити / Old Church Slavonic распустити ('to let go, dismiss, dissolve'), formed from prefix рас- ('apart, in all directions') + пустить ('to let go, release', from Proto-Slavic *pustiti).

history.meaning: to dismiss, disband; to spread (a rumor); to spoil (lack discipline)

распуститься.etymology: Reflexive of распустить ('to let go, loosen, unfurl', from рас- + пустить 'to release', Proto-Slavic *pustiti) + -ся ('to open up, blossom; to lose self-restraint, get out of hand').

history.meaning: to bloom, open; to get out of hand

рассада.etymology: Deverbal collective noun from рассадить ('to plant out, transplant seedlings into separate spots'), formed from prefix рас- ('apart') + садить ('to plant, seat', from Proto-Slavic *saditi).

рассадка.etymology: Action and result noun formed with -ка from рассадить ('to seat people in their respective places; to transplant seedlings'), composed of рас- ('around, into separate places') and садить ('to seat, plant'). The root descends from Proto-Slavic *saditi (causative of *sěděti, 'to sit'), from the Proto-Indo-European root *sed- ('to sit'). It is directly cognate with English set (the Germanic causative of sit).

history.meaning: to sit / to cause to sit, set

cognates.meaning: to cause to sit, place (from PGmc *satjaną < PIE *sodéyeti)

рассердиться.etymology: Formed from perfective prefix рас- + сердиться ('to be angry', derived from сердце 'heart; in older usage also anger, wrath', from Proto-Slavic *sьrdьce).

history.meaning: to get angry, lose one's temper

рассеянный.etymology: Past passive participle of рассеять ('to scatter, disperse', from prefix рас- 'apart' + сеять 'to sow, winnow', from Proto-Slavic *sějati); in the sense 'absent-minded, distracted', a 18th-century semantic calque of French distrait / German zerstreut.

рассказать.etymology: Formed from the prefix рас- ('out in detail, thoroughly', Proto-Slavic *orz-) + сказать ('to say, tell', from *sъkazati, built on *kazati 'to show, point out, speak'): literally 'to lay out a story in full detail, recount'.

history.meaning: to tell in full, recount, narrate

рассказывать.etymology: Imperfective counterpart of рассказать ('to tell, narrate, recount'), formed from the prefix раз- / рас- ('out, in detail') + сказывать / сказать ('to say, tell', from Proto-Slavic *kazati 'to show, point out, speak').

расслабить.etymology: Inherited from Old Church Slavonic / Old East Slavic раслабити ('to loosen, weaken, relax'), formed with prefix рас- from слабить ('to make weak/loose'), derived from слабый ('weak, slack', Proto-Slavic *slabъ).

расслабиться.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed from рас- ('un-, loose') + слабить ('to slacken, weaken', from слабый 'weak, slack, loose', inherited from Old East Slavic слабыи, Proto-Slavic *slabъ, cognate with German schlaff 'limp' and English sleep) + -ся.

расслаблять.etymology: Imperfective of расслабить ('to relax, loosen'), formed from рас- + слабый ('slack, loose, weak', inherited from Proto-Slavic *slabъ).

расслабляться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of расслаблять ('to relax, loosen up'), derived from рас- + слабый ('slack, loose, weak', from Proto-Slavic *slabъ).

расследование.etymology: Verbal noun from расследовать ('to investigate, inquire into'), formed with prefix рас- ('thoroughly') from следовать ('to follow a track, examine'), derived from след ('footprint, track, trace', Proto-Slavic *slědъ).

расслышать.etymology: Formed from prefix рас- (indicating discerning or making out clearly, as in рассмотреть) + слышать ('to hear', inherited from Old East Slavic слышати, from Proto-Slavic *slyšati).

history.meaning: to catch, make out by hearing

рассматривать.etymology: Imperfective of рассмотреть ('to examine closely, scrutinize, consider'), formed from prefix рас- + сматривать (iterative of смотреть 'to look, observe', from Proto-Slavic *sъmotriti).

рассмотреть.etymology: Formed from prefix рас- (indicating thorough, detailed inspection) + смотреть ('to look, watch', inherited from Old East Slavic съмотрити, from Proto-Slavic *sъmotriti).

history.meaning: to discern, examine closely; to consider

рассол.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic рассолъ, formed from рас- (from Proto-Slavic *orz- 'apart, dissolved through') + соль ('salt', Proto-Slavic *solь, PIE *séh₂ls): literally 'water in which salt has been dissolved, pickle brine'.

расспросить.etymology: Formed from prefix рас- (indicating thorough, detailed action) + спросить ('to ask', from с- + просить 'to ask, request', from Proto-Slavic *prositi).

history.meaning: to question thoroughly, ask in detail

расставание.etymology: Verbal noun from расставаться ('to part, separate, break up', formed from prefix рас- 'apart' + ставать, iterative of стать 'to stand', from Proto-Slavic *stavati) + suffix -ние.

расставаться.etymology: Imperfective reflexive of расстаться ('to part ways, separate, break up'), formed from prefix рас- ('apart') + ставать (iterative of стать 'to stand', from Proto-Slavic *stati) + -ся.

расставить.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic росставити / Old Church Slavonic расставити ('to set out, place apart, arrange'), formed from prefix рас- ('apart, in various places') + ставить ('to place, set upright', from Proto-Slavic *staviti).

history.meaning: to arrange, set out, place at intervals

расстаться.etymology: Formed from the prefix рас- / раз- ('apart') + стать ('to stand, step', from Proto-Slavic *stati) + the reciprocal/reflexive enclitic -ся ('to step apart from one another, part ways').

расстояние.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic разстояниѥ ('distance, interval', calquing Ancient Greek διάστημα and Latin distantia), verbal noun from разстояти ('to stand apart', from раз- 'apart' + стояти 'to stand', Proto-Slavic *stojati).

расстраивать.etymology: Imperfective of расстроить ('to throw into disorder, put out of tune, frustrate, upset'), formed from reversative/disruptive prefix рас- + страивать (from строить 'to arrange, tune, build', from строй 'order, harmony', Proto-Slavic *strojiti).

history.meaning: to put out of order/tune; to upset

расстраиваться.etymology: Imperfective reflexive verb (paired with расстроиться) formed from расстраивать / расстроить ('to throw out of order; to detune a musical instrument; to upset'), built from раз- / рас- ('apart, out of order') + строить ('to arrange, tune, build', Proto-Slavic *strojiti). Just as настроение ('mood') comes from tuning an instrument, расстраиваться means 'to become out of tune emotionally, get upset or distressed'.

history.meaning: to come out of tune → to get upset, feel distressed

расстроенный.etymology: Past passive participle of расстроить ('to put out of tune, disorder, upset', from prefix рас- 'un-, out of' + строить 'to order, tune, arrange', from Proto-Slavic *strojiti).

history.meaning: to put out of tune, upset

расстроить.etymology: Formed with reversative prefix рас- ('out of order, apart') from строить ('to tune an instrument, arrange in order, build'), derived from строй ('order, harmony, tuning', Proto-Slavic *strojь), shifting from 'to put out of tune/order' to 'to upset emotionally'.

history.meaning: to put in order, tune, arrange
to put out of tune, disrupt; to upset, distress

расстроиться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of расстроить ('to put out of tune/order, upset'), formed from рас- ('out of order') + строить ('to arrange, tune', Proto-Slavic *strojiti).

history.meaning: to fall through, be disrupted; to get upset

расстройство.etymology: Derived from расстроить ('to throw out of order, disrupt, upset', from prefix рас- + строить 'to order, arrange', from Proto-Slavic *strojiti) + abstract suffix -ство.

расступиться.etymology: Formed from prefix рас- ('apart, to both sides') + ступить ('to step, tread', from Proto-Slavic *stǫpiti) + reflexive suffix -ся ('to step aside in different directions, make way').

рассчитать.etymology: Formed with prefix рас- ('out, completely') from считать ('to count, reckon'), from Old East Slavic съчитати ('to count up', from Proto-Slavic *sъ-čitati).

history.meaning: to calculate, to judge; to pay off and dismiss

рассчитаться.etymology: Reflexive of рассчитать ('to calculate, count out, pay off'), formed from prefix рас- + считать ('to count, reckon', from Old East Slavic съчитати, from съ- + читати, Proto-Slavic *čьtati) + -ся ('to settle accounts, get even').

history.meaning: to settle up, pay off; to get even

рассчитывать.etymology: Imperfective of рассчитать ('to calculate, reckon, pay off'), formed from the prefix рас- / раз- + считать ('to count, reckon', from Proto-Slavic *sъčitati).

рассыпать.etymology: Formed with prefix рас- ('apart, in all directions') from сыпать ('to pour/scatter dry material'), inherited from Old East Slavic сыпати, from Proto-Slavic *sypati.

растаять.etymology: Formed from perfective prefix рас- ('away, completely') + таять ('to melt, thaw', inherited from Old East Slavic таяти, from Proto-Slavic *tajati 'to melt, thaw', from PIE *teh₂- 'to melt, dissolve').

раствор.etymology: Deverbal noun from растворить ('to dissolve, mix; to open wide'), built on раз- / рас- ('apart, throughout') + творить ('to make, knead, slake lime, shape', from Proto-Slavic *tvoriti). Used both for builder's mortar and for a chemical/culinary solution.

history.meaning: to mix, dissolve → mixture, mortar, solution

растение.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic растениѥ ('growth, plant', with Church Slavonic initial ра- from Proto-Slavic *orst-), verbal noun from расти ('to grow', from Proto-Slavic *orsti).

растереть.etymology: Prefixed perfective verb formed from рас- ('all over, into fine particles') + тереть ('to rub, grate, grind'), inherited from Old East Slavic терти (1sg. търу), from Proto-Slavic *terti, from Proto-Indo-European *terh₁- ('to rub, turn'; cognate with Latin terere 'to rub').

history.meaning: to rub apart, grind fine, rub over
to rub down, massage; to grind, mash

растерзать.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic растьрзати ('to tear to pieces, lacerate'), formed from prefix рас- ('apart') + терзать ('to tear, rend, torment', from Proto-Slavic *tьrzati, iterative of *tьrgati 'to pull, tear').

растерянность.etymology: Abstract noun derived from растерянный ('confused, bewildered, at a loss', originally past passive participle of растерять / растеряться 'to lose everything; to lose one's composure', from рас- + терять 'to lose') + suffix -ость.

history.meaning: to lose one's head, be at a loss

растеряться.etymology: Reflexive perfective verb formed from рас- ('in all directions, completely') + терять ('to lose') + -ся: literally 'to lose one's wits or bearings in every direction, be at a loss'.

history.meaning: to lose one's composure, become flustered or confused

расти.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic расти / рости (present расту), from Proto-Slavic *orsti (1st sg. *orstǫ, 'to grow'), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂erdʰ- / *h₁er-d- ('to grow high, upright'; compare Latin arduus 'steep, high' and Sanskrit ṛdhnóti 'thrives, prospers'). Initial Proto-Slavic *orC- gave ра- in South Slavic / Church Slavonic (which influenced the Russian infinitive spelling расти) and ро- in East Slavic (preserved in the past tense рос, росла and noun рост 'growth, height').

растить.etymology: Borrowed from or influenced by Old Church Slavonic растити ('to make grow, cultivate, rear', corresponding to Old East Slavic ростити), causative of расти ('to grow', from Proto-Slavic *orstiti / *orsti).

history.meaning: to raise, bring up; to grow (plants)

растолстеть.etymology: Formed from prefix рас- (indicating expansion outward or thorough change of state) + толстеть ('to grow fat, put on weight', derived from толстый 'thick, fat, stout', from Proto-Slavic *tъlstъ).

history.meaning: to get fat, put on weight

расторгнуть.etymology: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic расторгнути ('to tear apart, break, sever [bonds]'), formed from prefix рас- ('apart') + торгнути ('to pull, tear, wrench', from Proto-Slavic *tъrgnǫti).

history.meaning: to dissolve, annul, terminate (a contract or marriage)

растрогать.etymology: Formed with prefix рас- ('thoroughly') from трогать ('to touch'), inherited from East Slavic трогать (compare торгать 'to pull, jerk'), acquiring the emotional sense 'to touch/move deeply' as a calque on French toucher / attendrir.

растрогаться.etymology: Reflexive form (-ся) of растрогать ('to touch deeply, move emotionally'), formed from рас- ('thoroughly') and трогать ('to touch'). The verb comes from Proto-Slavic *torgati ('to pull, tug, stir'), which softened semantically in Russian to 'to touch physically or emotionally'. In the eighteenth century, under the influence of French toucher ('to touch, move the heart'), растрогаться acquired its warm emotional sense.

растяжение.etymology: Verbal noun from растянуть ('to stretch out, distend, sprain', formed from prefix рас- + тянуть 'to pull, stretch', from Proto-Slavic *tęgnǫti, with stem consonant alternation г/ж before -ение).

растянуть.etymology: Formed from prefix рас- ('out, apart') + тянуть ('to pull, draw, stretch', inherited from Old East Slavic тягнути, from Proto-Slavic *tęgnǫti).

history.meaning: to stretch out, prolong; to sprain

расхваливать.etymology: Imperfective of расхвалить ('to praise to the skies, extol'), formed from intensive prefix рас- + хваливать (iterative of хвалить 'to praise', from хвала 'praise', from Proto-Slavic *xvaliti).

расхлёбывать.etymology: Imperfective of расхлебать ('to sup up all the broth together; idiomatically расхлёбывать кашу to eat up the porridge one has brewed, i.e., clean up a mess'), from prefix рас- + хлебать ('to sup, slurp', from Proto-Slavic *xlebati).

history.meaning: to slurp, eat with a spoon
to sup up; (idiomatic) to clean up a mess, face the music

расход.etymology: Deverbal noun from расходиться ('to go out, be spent, be consumed'), inherited from Old East Slavic росходъ / расходъ, formed from prefix рас- ('apart, out') + ход ('going, motion', from Proto-Slavic *xodъ).

расходиться.etymology: Imperfective reflexive of разойтись ('to walk apart, disperse, separate'), formed from prefix рас- ('apart, in different directions') + ходить ('to walk, go', from Proto-Slavic *xoditi) + -ся.

расцвести.etymology: Formed with prefix рас- ('opening out') from цвести (цвету, 'to bloom, blossom'), inherited from Old East Slavic цвѣсти, from Proto-Slavic *kvisti (*kvьtǫ, 'to bloom, shine').

расцеловать.etymology: Formed from intensive/distributive prefix рас- ('warmly, repeatedly, on both cheeks') + целовать ('to kiss; originally in Old East Slavic цѣловати to greet, wish health/wholeness to', from целый 'whole, hale', Proto-Slavic *cělovati).

расчёска.etymology: Derived from расчесать / расчёсывать ('to comb out', formed from prefix рас- + чесать 'to comb, card', from Proto-Slavic *česati) + instrument/action suffix -ка.

расчёт.etymology: Deverbal noun from рассчитать / расчесть ('to count out, calculate, settle accounts'), formed from рас- + чёт ('count, even number', from Proto-Slavic *čьtъ, from *čьsti 'to count, read').

расшатываться.etymology: Imperfective formed with -ывать and reflexive -ся from расшатать ('to shake loose'), combining рас- ('apart, loose') + шатать ('to rock, sway, shake to and fro', an expressive East Slavic verb; compare шаткий 'rickety, unsteady').

history.meaning: to shake loose → to work loose, become wobbly

расширяться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of расширять ('to widen, expand, broaden'), imperfective of расширить, formed with prefix рас- from ширить ('to widen'), derived from ширь / широкий ('wide, broad', Proto-Slavic *širokъ).

расщедриться.etymology: Formed from intensive/inchoative prefix рас- + щедриться ('to be generous', derived from щедрый 'generous, bountiful', from Old East Slavic and Old Church Slavonic щедръ 'merciful, generous', from Proto-Slavic *ščedrъ).

рать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic and Old Church Slavonic рать ('war, battle, host, army'), from Proto-Slavic *ortь ('strife, war, troop'), cognate with Old High German ernust ('seriousness, struggle, combat') from PIE *h₃er- ('to stir, rise, fight').

раунд.etymology: Borrowed in the late 19th or early 20th century from English round ('a single stage or bout in boxing or a competition'), from Old French roont ('round'), from Latin rotundus ('wheel-shaped, round').

history.meaning: bout or stage in a match

рвать.etymology: Inherited from Old East Slavic ръвати ('to tear, pluck, pull out'), from Proto-Slavic *rъvati ('to tear, pluck'), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃rew- ('to tear up, dig out, rend', cognate with Latin ruere and Sanskrit rávati).

history.meaning: to tear, rip, pick; (impersonal) to vomit

рваться.etymology: Reflexive form in -ся of рвать ('to tear, rend, pull'), inherited from Old East Slavic ръвати, from Proto-Slavic *rъvati ('to tear, pluck'), meaning both 'to tear/break' and 'to strain eagerly forward'.

history.meaning: to strive for, rush toward; to tear

рвота.etymology: Derived from рвать (in its impersonal sense меня рвёт 'I am vomiting', literally 'it tears/wrenches me', from Proto-Slavic *rъvati 'to tear, wrench') + noun suffix -ота (on the pattern of икота, зевота, тошнота).

ре.etymology: Borrowed from Italian re, the second syllable of the medieval solfège scale introduced by Guido of Arezzo in the eleventh century. Like the other solfège names, it was extracted from the initial syllable of the second half-line of the Latin hymn to Saint John the Baptist: 'Resonare fibris' ('to resound with full strings/voice'). Latin resonāre derives from re- ('back, again') and sonāre ('to sound', from PIE *swenh₂-).

history.meaning: to resound (second phrase of Guido's hymn)
second note of the scale, D

cognates.meaning: second note of the solfège scale

реагировать.etymology: Borrowed via German reagieren from Medieval and New Latin reagere ('to act back, react'), compounded from Latin re- ('back, in response') + agere ('to act, drive, do').

реакция.etymology: Borrowed via German Reaktion and French réaction from New Latin reactiō ('counter-action, response'), built from Latin re- ('back, in response') + āctiō ('action', from agere 'to act').

реалист.etymology: Borrowed in the 19th century via French réaliste and German Realist, derived from Late Latin realis ('real, actual', from Latin res 'thing, fact') + agent suffix -ist.

реально.etymology: Adverb and predicative short neuter of реальный ('real, realistic'), borrowed via German real / Polish realny from Late Latin realis ('actual, relating to things themselves', from Latin res 'thing, matter').

реальность.etymology: Derived from реальный ('real, actual', borrowed via German real / French réel from Late Latin realis 'actual, relating to things themselves', from Latin res 'thing') + abstract noun suffix -ость (calquing French réalité / German Realität).

реальный.etymology: Borrowed via German real or Polish realny from Late Latin reālis ('relating to things themselves, real, actual'), derived from Latin rēs ('thing, matter').

реанимация.etymology: Twentieth-century medical borrowing from French réanimation / New Latin reanimatio ('resuscitation, restoring to life'), formed from Latin re- ('again') + animare ('to give breath or life to', from anima 'breath, soul, life').

history.meaning: to restore breath or life to
